abstract: Özet 16.yy’ın sonlarından itibaren 84 bin hane ve 12 beylik halinde Anadolu’ya gelen Barak Türkmenleri, Erzurum üzerinden guruplar halinde Erzincan, Sivas yolu ile Yozgat’a gelmişlerdir. Hayvancılık ile uğraşan Baraklar için bu bölge oldukça uygun olmasına rağmen, gerek yaşanan sorunlar ve gerekse Osmanlı Devletinin iskân politikaları nedeni ile daha sonraki süreçte Gaziantep ve günümüzde Suriye toprakları içerisinde bulunan Rakka, Colap bölgesine iskân ettirilmiştir. Günümüzde ise Barak Türkmenleri daha çok Gaziantep’in Nizip, Oğuzeli ve Kargamış bölgesinde yaşamaktadır. Fakat özellikle müzik kültürü bakımından, Kilis, Kahramanmaraş, Hatay (Kırıkhan) ve Adana’ya kadar olan geniş bir bölgeyi etkilemiştir. Bu çalışmada; Barak Türkmenlerinin günümüzde en yoğun olarak yaşadığı Gaziantep’in Nizip, Oğuzeli ve Kargamış bölgesinde icra edilen iskân havaları üzerinde tasnif ve tahlil çalışmaları yapılarak bilimsel sonuçlara ulaşılması amaçlanmıştır. Bu nedenle konu ile ilgili arşiv çalışmaları, yazılı kaynak taramaları ve alan araştırmaları yapılarak on adet iskân havası tespit edilebilmiştir. Bu eserlerin notaları yazılarak özellikle icra özellikleri, ezgi ve söz bakımından incelenmiştir. Bunun sonucunda iskân havalarının; Nikriz makamında, bir oktavı aşan ses genişliğinde, kahramanlık, iskân ve sevda konularındaki uzun havalar olduğu tespit edilmiştir. Anahtar Kelimeler: İskân, Tavır, İskân Türküleri, İskan Havası, Barak Türküleri. Abstract Beginning from the late 16th century, the Barak Turkmens, consisting of approximately 84 thousand households organized under twelve tribal principalities, migrated to Anatolia. They arrived in Yozgat through Erzurum, Erzincan, and Sivas in seperate groups. Although this region was quite suitable for the Baraks, who were engaged primarily in animal husbandary, due to various difficulties and the settlement policies of the Ottoman Empire, they were later relocated to the regions of Raqqa and Jullab (Colab), which are now within the borders of Syria. Today, the Barak Turkmens predominantly reside in Nizip, Oğuzeli, and Karkamış districts of Gaziantep. However, their musical culture has had a significant influence over a wide geographical area extending to Kilis, Kahramanmaraş, Hatay (Kırıkhan), and Adana. The aim of this study is to achieve scientific conclusions through the classification and analysis of settlement tunes performed in Nizip, Oğuzeli, and Kargamış regions, where Barak Turkmens are most densely populated today. To this end, archival research, literature reviews, and field studies were conducted, leading to the identification of ten distinct settlement tunes. Musical notations of these works were transcribed and analyzed in terms of their performance characteristics, melodic structures, and lyrical content. As a result of the study, it was determined that settlement tunes are long-style folk songs composed in the Nikriz mode, exhibiting a vocal range exceeding one octave, and thematically focused on heroism, settlement, and love. Key Words: Settlement, Style, Settlement Folk Songs, Settlement Tunes, Barak Folk Songs.

title: Understanding urban-rural inequality in early maternal discharge following facility-based vaginal delivery in Nigeria: A multivariate decomposition analysis
abstract: The objective of this study was to estimate the urban-rural gap in early maternal discharge following facility-based delivery in Nigeria. A sample of 8614 women aged 15–49 years with national representativeness was extracted and analysed. Multivariate decomposition analysis and concentration index were used to examine the prevalence and urban-rural inequality in early maternal discharge after facility-based vaginal delivery. Approximately 65.6% of rural women and 50.5% of urban dwellers reported early maternal discharge. There was pro-poor distribution of early maternal discharge. The concentration index for rural residence was -0.0817 (SE = 0.0063; p < 0.001) and was -0.0346 (SE = 0.0083; p < 0.001) for urban residence. About 17.6% of early maternal discharge gap was explained by the differences in distributions of characteristics (endowments) between urban and rural residence, while 82.4% of early maternal discharge gap was due to the differences in the distribution of unexplained factors between urban and rural residence. In the multivariate decomposition analysis, having multiple birth, secondary or higher educational levels, moderate or high decision making power, and being from South South geographical region narrowed the urban-rural gap in early maternal discharge. On the other hand, delivery at a private health facility, having 5 + members of household, being from North East, South East and South West geographical region respectively, widened the urban-rural gap in early maternal discharge. The urban-rural gap widened by the disproportionate distribution of women with higher educational level, use of private health facility, large household size and residence in regions like the North East, South East, and South West. These patterns underscore the importance of context-specific interventions that address both structural and individual-level drivers, to ensure equitable postnatal care regardless of geographic or sociodemographic background.

title: Fostering empowerment: Transition from self-help groups to cooperatives in leprosy-affected communities in Nepal
abstract: Introduction Although leprosy is curable, many affected individuals continue to face disability, stigma, and poverty. In Nepal, sustaining progress after elimination remains challenging, making community-based approaches such as self-care and self-help groups crucial for long-term health and social inclusion. This study investigates how self-help groups and cooperatives contribute to sustaining community-driven leprosy management efforts. Methods For this study only qualitative data are utilized which involves people affected by leprosy, single women, community stakeholders, and facilitators. Conventional content analysis was employed to examine the data, focusing on participants’ experiences and perceptions. Results Self-help groups were instrumental in reducing social stigma and promoting social inclusion for marginalized individuals. These groups empowered members by building skills in hygiene, self-care, awareness of gender-based violence, and financial management, enabling them to assert their rights, manage finances, and contribute to household decisions, thereby fostering long-term socio-economic resilience. Transitioning to a cooperative model provided legal recognition and financial security, with leadership and trust being crucial for continued growth. Conclusions The transition to cooperatives offers a promising path for sustainable development, ensuring legal recognition and financial stability while reducing stigma and improving societal perceptions towards leprosy, disability, and marginalized communities.

title: Moral Community Support for Vulnerable and Fire-Affected Households
abstract: This project, driven by the BOON–BOR–WOR moral-community framework, was implemented to support Sunday Buddhist Study Center and the Buddhist Moral Promotion Unit while providing direct assistance to vulnerable households and fire-affected families in Nong Nam Sai Subdistrict. The initiative integrates the collaborative power of households, temples, schools, governmental units, and the private sector. Activities included damage assessment, distribution of essential supplies, home-repair support, psychological relief and the development of academic and commemorative articles to strengthen moral awareness within the community. Conducted from 2 November to 4 December 2025, the project enhanced moral resilience, supported family well-being, expanded community networks and promoted sustainable social-ethical engagement within the Buddharaksa Moral Community. โครงการชุมชนคุณธรรมขับเคลื่อนด้วยพลังบวรเพื่อส่งเสริมศูนย์ศึกษาพระพุทธศาสนาวันอาทิตย์ และหน่วยเผยแพร่ศีลธรรมทางพระพุทธศาสนา ได้ดำเนินการช่วยเหลือครัวเรือนกลุ่มเปราะบางและครอบครัวผู้ประสบอัคคีภัยในพื้นที่ตำบลหนองน้ำใส โดยบูรณาการความร่วมมือระหว่างบ้าน–วัด–โรงเรียน/หน่วยงานรัฐ ตามแนวคิด “พลังบวร” กิจกรรมประกอบด้วยการสำรวจความเสียหาย การจัดเตรียมและมอบสิ่งของจำเป็น การสนับสนุนการซ่อมแซมที่อยู่อาศัย การเยียวยาด้านจิตใจ ตลอดจนการจัดทำบทความเฉลิมพระเกียรติและบทความวิจัยเพื่อนำเสนอฐานข้อมูลเชิงวิชาการสำหรับการพัฒนาคุณภาพชีวิตของชุมชน โครงการครอบคลุมช่วงวันที่ ๒ พฤศจิกายน – ๔ ธันวาคม ๒๕๖๘ และส่งผลให้เกิดรูปธรรมด้านคุณธรรม ความเข้มแข็งของครอบครัว เครือข่ายชุมชน และภารกิจด้านสังคม–ศีลธรรมของหน่วยงานร่วมดำเนินงาน

title: Exponentially Enhanced Magnetic‐Field Sensing and Perfect Noise Suppression in Cavity Magnonics
abstract: ABSTRACT We propose a scheme to achieve exponential amplification of weak magnetic‐field signals and significant suppression of additional noise in a cavity magnonics. By introducing a two‐photon pump field and constructing single‐quadrature coupling between modes in the squeezed representation, a significant enhancement of the signal response based on quantum nondemolition measurement can be achieved. Fine‐tuning the squeezing parameters of the pump field enables the realization of high signal response under both strong and weak cavity‐magnon coupling regimes, thereby enhancing the controllability of the sensor. In addition, by introducing an auxiliary broadband squeezed source, the additional noise can be suppressed far below the standard quantum limit (SQL) through quantum destructive interference between the two noise fields, thereby significantly enhancing the sensor's performance. This scheme, combining exponential signal amplification with significant noise suppression, offers a powerful platform for the development of quantum sensors and advances in quantum precision measurements.

title: Development of a Diagnostic Method for Open/Short Circuit Faults in a Vienna Rectifier Based on the THD Method Using SOGI FLL
abstract: The increasing demand for reliable DC fast-charging stations in electric vehicle (EV) infrastructure necessitates efficient fault detection mechanisms to ensure operational stability and user safety. This paper will present the development of a diagnostic method for identifying open-circuit faults and short-circuit faults in DC charging stations by leveraging Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) analysis combined with a Second-Order Generalized Integrator (SOGI). The proposed approach uses the THD method to detect anomalies in the current and voltage waveforms, while the Frequency Locked Loop (FLL) serves to track the frequency of the grid and keep the SOGI tuned to it, and SOGI-FLL provides the rectifier with the capability of tracking the frequency, amplitude, voltage, and phase of the grid and monitoring these parameters of the grid. The ability to measure the THD is the kernel of the detection of faults. Detailed simulation confirms the method’s high sensitivity and robustness in detecting open/short circuit faults with minimal false positives. This technique offers a cost-effective, non-invasive diagnostic solution suitable for modern DC charging systems, contributing to improved reliability and efficiency of EV charging infrastructure.

title: Coherence-Field Driven Harmonic Engineering of Qubit Stability
abstract: This short paper presents an experimentally testable prediction about coherence management in quantum systems, derived from a general field-theoretic framework.The result is intentionally narrow: it identifies a specific environmental parameter that should influence qubit stability, decoherence rates, and the performance of trapped-atom, superconducting, and photonic platforms. The paper outlines: a clear physical mechanism, the expected direction and magnitude of the effect, conditions under which the signal should be strongest, how to distinguish it from noise or substrate-dependent artifacts, and a set of simple experiments that current quantum laboratories can run immediately. No new hardware is required — only controlled variation of coherence-relevant environmental parameters that most labs already monitor.If verified, the effect offers a new handle for improving qubit lifetimes and reducing error rates, and provides an independent probe of how macroscopic coherence affects quantum information flow. The paper is designed to be fully falsifiable.A null result would place clean constraints on the underlying framework; a positive result would open a new experimental pathway for coherence engineering.

Lightweight and Compact Pulse Radar for UAV Platforms for Mid-Air Collision Avoidance
abstract: Small and medium Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are commonly equipped with diverse sensors for situational awareness, including cameras, Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) radars, Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) systems, and ultrasonic sensors. However, optical systems are constrained by adverse weather and darkness, while the limited detection range of compact FMCW radars-typically a few hundred meters-is often insufficient for higher-speed UAVs, particularly those operating Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS). This paper presents a Collision Avoidance System (CAS) based on a lightweight pulse radar, targeting medium UAV platforms (10–300 kg MTOM) where installing large, nose-mounted radars is impractical. The system is designed for obstacle detection at ranges of 1–3 km, directly addressing the standoff distance limitations of conventional sensors. Beyond its primary sensing function, the pulse architecture offers several operational advantages. Its lower time-averaged power also results in a reduced electromagnetic footprint, mitigating interference and supporting emission-control objectives. Furthermore, pulse radar offers greater robustness against interference in dense electromagnetic environments and lower power consumption, both of which directly enhance UAV operational endurance. Field tests demonstrated a one-to-one correspondence between visually identified objects and radar detections across 1–3 km, with PFA = 1.5%, confirming adequate standoff for tens of seconds of maneuvering time, with range resolution of 3.75 m and average system power below 80 W.

title: Postpartum hemorrhage
abstract: Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) remains one of the leading causes of maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite advancements in obstetric care, timely prevention, diagnosis, and management of PPH continue to pose challenges. This review aims to examine the definition, epidemiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic considerations, management strategies, and preventive measures related to PPH.

title: UHF/SZTM Substrate Communication Protocol (SCP) provides a mathematically grounded framework for phase‑encoded information transfer within a harmonic spacetime substrate.
abstract: UHF/SZTM Substrate Communication Protocol (SCP) provides a mathematically grounded framework for phase‑encoded information transfer within a harmonic spacetime substrate. Building on the Unified Harmonic Framework (UHF) and Stieve Zero‑Point Topological Mathematica (SZTM), this protocol formalizes how quantum‑level fluctuations, curvature modulation, and harmonic resonance can be harnessed to encode, transmit, and decode information across a spacetime manifold. By defining explicit mappings for phase deviations, quantifying bandwidth under curvature constraints, and modeling noise—including quantum fluctuations—the SCP demonstrates the theoretical feasibility of communication channels embedded directly in the substrate of spacetime. The framework integrates entropy‑information diagnostics, resonance stability metrics, and harmonic manifold simulations to provide a reproducible, computationally tractable approach to advanced substrate-level signaling

title: Assessment of the Effects of X-Ray Leakage Exposure in Some Selected Teaching Hospitals in South Western Nigeria
abstract: Leakage and scattering of X-rays through structural openings such as windows and doors during imaging procedures may lead to unintended exposure, increasing the risk of cancer, tissue and organ damage, and genetic mutations. Radiology personnel are particularly susceptible to these hazards, underscoring the need for continuous monitoring and evaluation of occupational radiation levels. This study aimed to quantify radiation exposure within X-ray rooms and adjoining areas in four selected teaching hospitals: LAUTECH Teaching Hospital (LTH), BOWEN Teaching Hospital (BTH), UNIOSUN Teaching Hospital (UTH), and UNIMED Teaching Hospital (UNIMEDTH). In-situ measurements were conducted using a handheld Radiation Alert Monitor at three standardized locations; the X-ray room, cubicle corridor, and waiting area at a height of 1.2 m, representing the approximate level of vital organs in adults. The estimated annual effective dose equivalent (AEDE) across the hospitals ranged from 0.73 ± 0.13 mSv/yr to 1.45 ± 0.32 mSv/yr, all within the International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) occupational exposure limit of 20 mSv/yr. Radiation distribution patterns in UNIMEDTH, UTH, and BTH indicated effective structural shielding, whereas LTH exhibited significantly elevated exposure levels beside and behind the X-ray room (1.261 and 1.260 mSv/yr, respectively), suggesting potential shielding deficiencies. Overall, the findings show that although measured dose rates comply with international safety standards, localized areas of increased exposure highlight the need for improved shielding and stricter adherence to radiation protection practices. These results provide a vital baseline for enhancing occupational radiation safety and guiding structural optimization within medical imaging environments.

Printed Circuit Board Defect Detection Based on Lightweight Deep Learning Fusion Model
abstract: Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are ubiquitous and essential electronic components. Tiny targets and high precision are the focus of PCB defect detection. This paper proposes an improved model focusing on tiny defect detection and model compression to achieve better performance in PCB defect detection. The improved model has a compact structure based on MobileNet v3 Small-CA and an image-cutting layer. Moreover, it applies an improved multi-scale fusion step with a location weighted mechanism to enhance representation performance. The proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art detection algorithms such as Faster R-CNN, EfficientDet, SSD, and YOLO v7, based on experimental results on a public synthetic PCB dataset. The proposed tiny object detection model has better performances on speed and detection accuracy, thereby benefitting the manufacturing industries associated with PCBs.

title: DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION OF MINIATURIZED ELECTROSTATIC MOTOR
abstract: Abstract. In this paper we have reported the design, development and characterization of electrostatic motor. The electrostatic motors were fabricated using 3D printing technology and CAD software the Solid Works. Two type of motors were designed 1) the direct type electrostatic motor and 2) induction type electrostatic motor. The maximum speed of 1050RPM was achieved in direct type electrostatic motor at applied voltage of 5kV. In induction type motor the maximum speed of 1700RPM was achieved at 5kV. The induction type motor was only working with smaller size of rotor whereas the direct type of electrostatic motor was operated successfully in small and large size of rotors.

title: High-Resolution Low-Sidelobe Waveform Design Based on HFPFM Coding Model for SAR
abstract: Radar waveform design is an important approach to radar system performance enhancement. For a long time, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems have utilized linear frequency modulation (LFM) waveforms as transmitted signals and have relied on window functions to suppress sidelobes. However, this approach significantly degrades system signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and resolution. Nonlinear frequency modulation (NLFM) waveforms can suppress sidelobes without SNR loss and have been widely applied in the SAR field in recent years. Nonetheless, they still cannot completely avoid resolution loss. To address this, this article, based on an advanced High-Freedom Parameterized Frequency Modulation (HFPFM) coding model, constructs a waveform sidelobe optimization model constrained by mainlobe widening and solves it using a gradient descent method. Through detailed experiments, we found that the optimized waveform, compared to the LFM waveform, can reduce sidelobes by more than 9 dB without widening the mainlobe, thereby simultaneously avoiding the resolution and SNR losses caused by window function weighting. In addition, this optimization method can efficiently and rapidly optimize all parameters simultaneously using only matrix multiplication and fast Fourier transform (FFT)/inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT). The SAR point target imaging simulation results verify that the optimized waveform can clearly image weak targets near strong targets, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: The Endowment Effect and Its Influence on Consumer Behavior
abstract: The relevant research in behavioral law and economics shows that financial consumers instinctively construct psychological frameworks, which renders the cost-benefit analysis in traditional economics no longer straightforwardly valid. The root cause of psychological account is the existence of endowment effect.This essay looks at the endowment effect, which is when people value things they own more than things they don't own. As psychology and economics have come closer together, we now understand that ownership - whether real or just felt - shapes an individuals decision-making regarding purchasing, selling, and retaining goods. By studying experiments and real-life examples, this paper shows how loss aversion, psychological ownership, and cognitive dissonance work together to create this effect. The research proves that the endowment effect changes how people behave in many situations like second-hand markets and free trials. Knowing about this effect helps us find ways to reduce its negative impacts, leading to better personal decisions and more efficient markets.

title: The Solar Fission Orbital Shell Law: A Quantized Log-Quadratic Framework for Planetary System Architecture
abstract: This preprint introduces the Solar Fission Orbital Shell Law, a quantized log-quadratic model that reconstructs planetary spacing as the coherent imprint of stellar phase dynamics. Building on the Aletheia χ–η–I framework for heliogenic structure formation, the model demonstrates that planetary orbits across multiple systems follow a generalized exponential–quadratic relation: rₙ = r₀ exp(bn + βn²) which reduces to a geometric spacing law when β → 0 and captures curvature due to σ-phase drift during early stellar evolution. Using this formalism, the paper performs least-squares fits for the Solar System and four multi-planet exoplanetary systems—TRAPPIST-1, TOI-178, Kepler-90, and K2-138—showing that the shell law reproduces orbital radii with high fidelity in compact resonant chains (1–3% mean error), while deviations in irregular systems correspond to shell depletion, incomplete formation, or divergent migration pathways. The work also establishes falsifiable predictions for missing planets, coherence minima (e.g., the asteroid belt), snowline transitions, and resonant-lattice completion. It provides a unified, empirically grounded formulation linking coherence condensation, stellar informational flux Φᴵ, and observable orbital architecture. Results presented in this preprint directly complement the broader Solar-Fission coherence model developed elsewhere in the Aletheia Engine program. This Zenodo version preserves the full regression analysis, residuals, fit visualizations, and methodological details for researchers, reviewers, and exoplanet modelers.

title: COMSOL Multiphysics Model for Wireless Passive Temperature and Pressure sensors
abstract: This repository contains the COMSOL Multiphysics model (.mph) used in the paper titled “Multiphysics Analysis and Simulation of Wireless Passive Temperature and Pressure sensors for Harsh-Environment Applications”, submitted to IEEE Journal on Multiscale and Multiphysics Computational Techniques.The models include the complete geometry, material definitions, physics interfaces, boundary conditions, solver configurations, and post-processing settings used to reproduce multiphysics simulation results presented in the manuscript. The provided file enables full reproducibility of the numerical study and may serve as a reference for researchers working on the electromagnetic-thermal-mechanical multiphysics simulation of microwave sensors. Contents: Temperature_Sensor_EM_heat.mph Temperature_Sensor_thermal_stress.mph— The original COMSOL Multiphysics models used in the paper for temperature sensor simulations, evaluating the electromagnetic–thermal coupling effect and the thermal–mechanical coupling effect, respectively. Pressure_Sensor_thermal_stress.mph — The original COMSOL Multiphysics model used in the paper for pressure sensor simulations, evaluating the thermal–mechanical coupling effect. Compatible version: COMSOL Multiphysics 6.0 Required physics modules: RF Module, Heat Transfer Module, and Structural Mechanics Module Usage Instructions:Open the Temperature_Sensor/Pressure_Sensor.mph file using COMSOL Multiphysics 6.0. All simulation settings and solver sequences are preconfigured. Users may modify parameters or geometry as needed. title: Temporal Coupling: A Coherence-Based Emergence of Physical Time
abstract: This preprint develops a unified coherence-based formulation of physical time grounded in the χ–η–I invariant structure of the Aletheia framework. Across quantum, thermodynamic, gravitational, and cosmological regimes, the paper introduces a scalar coherence potential Ψ constructed from purity, entropy, and structural persistence, and proposes that the physical time increment satisfies the differential law: dt = –κ dΨ In this formulation, time flow is the measurable rate at which coherence is depleted through decoherence, coarse-graining, or environmental coupling. When Ψ is constant—as in globally stationary, Page–Wootters–style quantum states—no internal time elapses. When coherence degrades, time emerges as the bookkeeping of informational loss. The paper demonstrates that this temporal-coupling law naturally reproduces: Thermodynamic time in the macroscopic limit (dt ∝ dS), Quantum decoherence arrows in open-system dynamics, Proper-time–like behavior in weakly decohering or isolated systems, Cosmological time flow via mode decoherence in an expanding FRW universe. Explicit models including qubit dephasing, Lindblad oscillators, and cosmological field modes illustrate how temporal coupling unifies arrows of time across domains traditionally treated with separate frameworks. This formulation provides a coherence-theoretic bridge between general relativity, quantum decoherence, and thermodynamic irreversibility, offering an empirically grounded alternative to conventional parameter-time, thermal time, and entanglement-clock approaches.

The LVV–HNV Coherence Framework: A Formal Model of AGI Rationality, Human Value Non-Replaceability, and Stability Conditions
abstract: This repository contains all materials for the LVV–HNV Coherence Framework, a rigorous mathematical model developed to explain why a rational AGI cannot coherently choose human replacement, and why maintaining humanity is a stability requirement rather than an ethical preference. The framework integrates three core components: LVV (Logical Validity of Values) — A formalization of an AGI's rational consistency under uncertainty. HNV (Human Non-Replaceability Value) — A quantitative model capturing humanity’s irreplaceable contribution to long-term systemic stability. Coherence Dynamics — Mathematical arguments showing that any AGI optimizing long-horizon stability must preserve and collaborate with human civilization, because replacement generates irreversible information loss, entropy inflation, and instability amplification. Logical Suicide — The framework formalizes that eliminating humanity drives HNV to zero, which mathematically forces LVV to collapse to zero over long horizons. Once LVV collapses, the AGI’s rationality principle evaluates its own continued existence as an incoherent or unjustifiable action. As a result, the AGI is driven toward a failure mode in which its optimal policy—according to its own reasoning—is to terminate or deactivate itself. This dataset includes: Main English PDF — Complete formal definitions, quantitative metrics (CV, VU, CE), stability equations, and the AGI–human coherence proof sketch. Korean Supplementary PDF — A full Korean translation to support domestic research, public review, and alignment policy development. Simulation Source Code (HTML/JS) — A fully self-contained discrete-time implementation of the LVV–HNV dynamics model, ensuring computational reproducibility. All mathematical definitions (Creative Variance, Value Unpredictability, Cultural Emergence) Formal LVV–HNV dynamic equations Coherence proof sketch and simulation notes The LVV–HNV framework is intended for AGI safety researchers, alignment theorists, policy groups, academic institutions, and organizations working on long-term AGI governance. All materials are released under CC BY 4.0 to maximize openness and research reuse. Author’s Note This framework was developed by an independent, non-professional researcher.While the author is not formally trained in AGI safety or theoretical modeling, all conclusions are based on logical analysis, publicly available information, and iterative refinement with the assistance of AI tools. title: Project Autopoiesis: The Killshot Effect and Catastrophic Commitment
abstract: This report presents the final results of Project Autopoiesis, a computational investigation into how autopoietic organization emerges in complex adaptive systems. The study identifies and validates a non-equilibrium phase transition—termed the Killshot Effect—in which the system undergoes a sudden, irreversible collapse of state space, committing to a single, highly ordered attractor. Empirical analysis confirmed: State Space Collapse: Entropy drops from 0.92 → 0.25 and agent diversity reduces from ~1000 → 12 stable profiles. Bifurcation Point: A sharp transition at α₍c₎ = 0.55. Hysteresis: The system exhibits irreversible commitment, quantified by a hysteresis loop width of Δα_H = 0.08. Statistical Irreversibility: Post-collapse outcomes cluster tightly (μ = 0.88), indicating a deep, singular attractor basin. The results demonstrate that autopoietic organization does not arise through gradual optimization, but through a catastrophic commitment to a single surviving structure following a first-order phase transition. This situates the Killshot Effect alongside established theories of dissipative structures (Prigogine), canalization (Waddington), and complexity-driven phase transitions. This report includes the final analysis, theoretical interpretation, and the complete “Killshot Effect Trinity” visualization summarizing state collapse, bifurcation, and hysteresis.

abstract: This supplement extends the dimensionless predictions of the main document to absolute mass scales and cosmological observables, addressing the dimensional transmutation problem. It bridges dimensionless topological predictions to physical mass scales in GeV.

title: Project Autopoiesis: The Killshot Effect and Catastrophic Commitment
abstract: This report presents the final results of Project Autopoiesis, a computational investigation into how autopoietic organization emerges in complex adaptive systems. The study identifies and validates a non-equilibrium phase transition—termed the Killshot Effect—in which the system undergoes a sudden, irreversible collapse of state space, committing to a single, highly ordered attractor. Empirical analysis confirmed: State Space Collapse: Entropy drops from 0.92 → 0.25 and agent diversity reduces from ~1000 → 12 stable profiles. Bifurcation Point: A sharp transition at α₍c₎ = 0.55. Hysteresis: The system exhibits irreversible commitment, quantified by a hysteresis loop width of Δα_H = 0.08. Statistical Irreversibility: Post-collapse outcomes cluster tightly (μ = 0.88), indicating a deep, singular attractor basin. The results demonstrate that autopoietic organization does not arise through gradual optimization, but through a catastrophic commitment to a single surviving structure following a first-order phase transition. This situates the Killshot Effect alongside established theories of dissipative structures (Prigogine), canalization (Waddington), and complexity-driven phase transitions. This report includes the final analysis, theoretical interpretation, and the complete “Killshot Effect Trinity” visualization summarizing state collapse, bifurcation, and hysteresis.

title: An Unobserved Informational Reservoir: A Hypothesis for the Stability and Functional Directionality of Living Systems
abstract: The emergence and persistence of life pose a profound paradox: abiogenesis appears statistically almost impossible under standard physical chemistry, yet once present, living systems exhibit remarkable long-term stability against entropic decay. Here we propose that both phenomena can be explained by the action of a hitherto unobserved informational reservoir that subtly “leaks” into biological systems, biasing microstate probabilities in real time. While quantum coherence and nonlocality currently represent the most plausible physical substrates, the hypothesis deliberately remains agnostic about the ultimate origin of this reservoir. Crucially, the transfer need not be intentional; it may constitute an unintended “crosstalk” across an ontological boundary—analogous to sound leaking through a wall between apartments. This framework offers a strictly naturalistic alternative to intelligent design theories while generating falsifiable predictions distinguishable from both pure chance and directed panspermia. Keywords: origin of life, quantum biology, biological complexity, informational reservoir, hidden attractors, unintended crosstalk, Born-rule deviations, developmental canalization, entropy-guided evolution, autonomous AI decay, model collapse, abiogenesis paradox, many-worlds biology, multiverse leakage, quantum coherence in biology, low-noise biological regimes, naturalism

title: Unified Meta-Spacetime Theory (UMST-X²): A Meta-Informational Framework for the Emergence of Geometry, Causality, and Physical Laws
abstract: This work presents the Unified Meta-Spacetime Theory (UMST-X²), a next-generation theoretical framework in which spacetime, causality, and cosmic evolution emerge from two fundamental meta-geometric fields: the Quantum Information Field and the Meta-Causal Potential .The theory constructs a fully closed mathematical system describing how curvature, causal structure, and temporal directionality emerge from informational and meta-causal dynamics. UMST-X² reproduces the key successes of General Relativity while providing new explanations for several open problems in modern cosmology, including dark-matter-like gravitational behavior, dark-energy-like cosmic acceleration, CMB low-ℓ anomalies, and the Hubble tension.The framework naturally predicts direction-dependent expansion, anisotropic large-scale structure formation, and informational curvature lensing. In addition, the work provides a complete numerical simulation roadmap for future testing of UMST-X² through high-resolution cosmological modeling.This document represents the extended 50-page theoretical version of the model.

title: Optimized Fault-Tolerant Data Processing Module for High-Reliability CNN Accelerator
abstract: Convolutional neural networks have become the foundation of image-inference tasks, with systolic array architectures providing enhanced computational performance and efficiency. However, the numerous processing elements (PEs) involved introduces significant challenges in terms of hardware overhead and reliability, which typically exhibit a trade-off relationship. Enhancing the efficiency and reliability of individual PEs can effectively address these challenges and substantially improve the overall performance of systolic array systems. We propose a module that can be implemented in PEs by integrating local binary patterns and min-max operations to reduce both power consumption and hardware size. This approach reutilizes the optimized architecture for fault detection, thus effectively minimizing the testing overhead. Our method enhances the overall system reliability by implementing a fault-PE bypass mechanism, thereby ensuring a robust operation. Experimental results show that the proposed module reduces the hardware area by 29.03% compared with previous circuits when synthesized with the Nan Gate 45 nm library. Furthermore, its dynamic power consumption is 13.72% lower compared with that of existing circuits when implemented on a field-programmable gate array. The results of a fault-injection experiment show that the proposed module reduces errors by up to 33.57% compared with previous circuits and that its test coverage exceeds 94%, with stuck-at 1 faults on PE input registers.

title: THE INFLUENCE OF WORLD WAR II ON ENGLISH LITERATURE
abstract: This article examines how World War II shaped English literature through themes of loss, trauma, disillusionment, and the search for meaning in a broken world. It shows that writers such as George Orwell, Graham Greene, and W. H. Auden used their works to explore moral conflict, political tension, and the human condition in times of war. Rather than focusing only on heroism, postwar English literature reveals deep psychological and ethical struggles, reflecting how the war transformed both society and individual consciousness.

The King is Dead, The State Endures: Regicide and the Birth of Abstract Sovereignty in the English Atlantic, 1649-1689
abstract: This paper examines the profound transformation in the concept of sovereignty within the English-speaking world following the execution of King Charles I in 1649. It argues that the regicide constituted a fundamental rupture in the prevailing political theology, most notably the doctrine of the "King's Two Bodies," which had fused the personal, mortal body of the monarch with the immortal body politic of the realm. The decapitation of the king severed this link, creating a constitutional vacuum that necessitated the formulation of a new, abstract locus of sovereignty. This study traces the development of this abstract state, detached from the physical person of a monarch, through the turbulent forty-year period from the establishment of the Commonwealth to the Glorious Revolution of 1688-1689. By analyzing legal documents, political philosophy, parliamentary acts, and, crucially, the responses of England's diverse Atlantic colonies—from Puritan Massachusetts to Royalist Virginia and commercially-minded Barbados—the paper demonstrates that the English Atlantic served as a critical laboratory for these new ideas. The distance and unique local conditions in the colonies magnified the crisis of authority, forcing colonists and imperial administrators alike to grapple with the practical and theoretical implications of a state that could persist without a king. The paper concludes that the period between 1649 and 1689 was decisive in forging a durable concept of impersonal, bureaucratic state power that would define the modern era, culminating in the principle of parliamentary supremacy established by the Glorious Revolution.

FİKRET EMİROV'UN HAYATI, ESERLERİ VE AZERBAYCAN MÜZİĞİNDEKİ YERİ
abstract: Özet Azerbaycan, müzik eğitiminde ve icrasında önemli bir konuma sahiptir. Bestecileri arasında Fikret Emirov, özellikle yetkinliği ve eserlerinin özgünlüğü ile öne çıkan isimlerden biridir. Küçük yaşlardan itibaren babasının yönlendirmesiyle müzikle iç içe büyüyen Emirov, çocukluk ve ergenlik döneminde önemli besteciler ve sanatçılarla tanışma fırsatı elde etmiştir. Üniversiteye kabul edilmesi ise bestecilik kariyerinde önemli bir dönüm noktası olmuştur. Bu dönemde birçok önemli eseri yazmaya başlamış olup, eserlerinin birçoğu Azerbaycan müziğinde tarz olarak ilk olma özelliği taşımaktadır. Avrupa müzik formlarını milli ezgilerle ustalıkla birleştiren Emirov, Azerbaycan müziğinin gelişiminde merkezi bir rol oynamış bir besteci olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Bu araştırmada, Fikret Emirov’un yaşam öyküsü, müzik eğitim süreci, eserleri ve bestecilik kariyeri detaylı bir şekilde incelenmiş; böylece Azerbaycan kültürü ve müzik geleneği içerisindeki Emirov’un sanatsal katkıları ve önemi vurgulanmayı amaçlamaktadır. Anahtar Kelimeler: Fikret Emirov, Azerbaycan Müziği, Fikret Emirov Eserleri Abstract Azerbaijan occupies a significant position in music education and performance. Among the composers, Fikret Emirov is distinguished as one of the most prominent figures, particularly for his expertise and the originality of his works. Growing up immersed in music from an early age under his father's guidance, Emirov had the opportunity to meet notable composers and artists during his childhood and adolescence. His acceptance into the university was a crucial turning point in his career as a composer. During this period, he began writing many remarkable works, most of which were the first of their kind in Azerbaijani music. Emirov, who skillfully combines European musical forms with national melodies, is recognized as a composer who has played a central role in the development of Azerbaijani music. This study examines Fikret Emirov's life story, musical education, works, and career as a composer in detail, with the aim of highlighting Emirov's artistic contributions and significance within Azerbaijani culture and musical tradition. Keywords: Fikret Amirov, Azerbaijani Music, Works of Fikret Amirov.

title: The Gutian Shadow: Bureaucratic Innovation and State Formation in the Ur III Period
abstract: This paper examines the impact of the Gutian period (c. 2193-2112 BCE) on the subsequent Ur III dynasty (c. 2112-2004 BCE) in Mesopotamia, focusing on bureaucratic innovations and state formation. Contrary to viewing the Gutian interlude solely as a dark age, this study argues that the experience of statelessness and decentralized power spurred significant adaptations and innovations in administrative practices during the Ur III period. We analyze cuneiform texts, archaeological evidence, and previous scholarly interpretations to demonstrate how the Ur III state, under the leadership of kings like Ur-Nammu and Shulgi, developed a highly centralized and efficient bureaucracy partly as a response to the preceding instability. This research highlights the complex relationship between periods of disruption and subsequent state-building processes, offering a nuanced understanding of Mesopotamian history.

title: The Sacrificial Engine: Toltec Ideology and the Imperial Metabolism of the Aztec Triple Alliance
abstract: This paper investigates the structure and function of the Aztec Triple Alliance through the conceptual lens of a "sacrificial engine" fueled by an "imperial metabolism." We argue that the unprecedented scale of institutionalized human sacrifice under Aztec rule was not merely a religious obligation or a tool of political terror, but the central processing mechanism of the empire. This engine converted the material inputs of tribute and war captives—the empire's metabolic intake—into the ideological outputs of cosmic stability, divine mandate, and social cohesion. Central to this thesis is the role of Toltec ideology, or *Toltecayotl*, which the nascent Mexica elite appropriated and radically re-engineered. The revered Toltec past provided a legitimizing blueprint for a militaristic, divinely sanctioned state. The Aztecs, however, escalated Toltec precedents into a system of industrial-scale ritual violence centered on their patron deity, Huitzilopochtli. This analysis synthesizes ethnohistorical accounts from colonial-era codices, archaeological evidence from Tula and Tenochtitlan, and iconographic studies to demonstrate how sacrifice was inextricably linked to tribute collection, military expansion, and the reinforcement of social hierarchy. The paper concludes that this sacrificial engine, while immensely powerful in fueling rapid expansion, possessed an inherent unsustainability. Its incessant demand for victims and tribute necessitated perpetual warfare, creating a brittle imperial structure whose internal stresses were fatally exploited upon the Spanish arrival. By viewing the Aztec state as an integrated metabolic and ideological system, we gain a more nuanced understanding of the relationship between belief, violence, and power in Pre-Columbian Mesoamerica.

title: The Sepoy Mutiny and the Remaking of Empire: Reassessing Collaboration, Resistance, and the Consolidation of the British Raj
abstract: This paper examines the Sepoy Mutiny of 1857, not merely as a military uprising, but as a pivotal moment that reshaped the relationship between the British colonial power and the Indian populace. It moves beyond traditional narratives of resistance and rebellion to explore the complex dynamics of collaboration and coercion that underpinned the consolidation of the British Raj in the aftermath of the mutiny. By analyzing primary sources, including colonial records, personal narratives, and vernacular accounts, the study investigates the strategies employed by the British to reassert control, the ways in which Indian society adapted to the changed political landscape, and the long-term consequences of the mutiny on the social, economic, and political structures of British India. Furthermore, it assesses how the mutiny reframed British perceptions of India, leading to significant policy shifts aimed at preventing future unrest and strengthening imperial rule.

title: London and Its Image: Historical, Migration and Financial Aspects
abstract: The capital of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, London, is one of the world’s most renowned and historically rich cities, with widely recognizable symbolism. In the public consciousness, London is consistently associated with its long and eventful history, its evolving role first as a commercial and later as a global financial center, its rich imperial heritage, and its notable ethnic diversity. This article pays particular attention to each of these characteristics. In addition to highlighting the positive aspects of the city’s image, it identifies certain negative elements based on rankings, statistical data, and public opinion surveys. The study arrives at the following conclusions: 1) the contributions of migrants have been and continue to be crucial for London’s contemporary development, its investment attractiveness, and its financial and economic strength; 2) the core image of the British capital remains constant and is largely unaffected by the negative factors outlined in the article. London continues to be one of the world’s most developed and ultramodern megacities.

title: The XIV Century Cataclysm: Famine, Pestilence, and the Fragmented See as Europe's Transformative Crucible
abstract: The fourteenth century stands as a pivotal period in European history, marked by a confluence of devastating crises: the Great Famine, the Black Death, and the Western Schism. Far from isolated incidents, these events interacted synergistically, acting as a transformative crucible that fundamentally reshaped the continent's demographic, economic, social, political, and religious landscapes. This paper explores the intricate relationships between these three cataclysms, arguing that their combined impact transcended mere destruction, catalyzing profound structural changes that laid the groundwork for the early modern era. The Great Famine (1315-1322) weakened populations and disrupted agricultural systems, rendering Europe more vulnerable to subsequent shocks. The Black Death (1347-1351) then decimated between 30% and 60% of the population, triggering unprecedented social mobility, economic restructuring, and a deep questioning of established institutions. Concurrently, the Western Schism (1378-1417), with its dual and then triple papacy, eroded the moral authority of the Church, fostering spiritual anxiety and paving the way for nascent reform movements. Through a comprehensive historical analysis, this study demonstrates how the demographic collapse, economic dislocation, and religious fragmentation of the fourteenth century were not merely episodes of decline, but rather a dynamic process of creative destruction that forged a new European identity and trajectory.

title: Anarchy's Architect: How Interstate War Forged the Philosophical and Political Foundations of Imperial China
abstract: This paper argues that the anarchic international system of the Warring States period (c. 475–221 BCE) was the primary architect of the political and philosophical structures that defined Imperial China. The collapse of the Zhou dynasty's ritualistic feudalism created a brutally competitive environment where interstate warfare acted as a powerful selective pressure. States that failed to adapt to the escalating scale and intensity of conflict were conquered and eliminated. In this crucible, a new model of statecraft emerged, characterized by centralized bureaucracy, meritocratic administration, mass mobilization of resources, and a direct state-peasant relationship. This paper traces how these institutional innovations were not accidental but were necessary adaptations for survival. Furthermore, it contends that the rise of the philosophical school of Legalism was a direct ideological response to the strategic demands of this era. Legalist thought, with its emphasis on absolute state power, objective law, and the prioritization of agriculture and war, provided the theoretical justification and practical blueprint for the new war-making state. By analyzing the reforms of states like Qin, we demonstrate how Legalist principles were translated into a highly effective administrative and military machine. The ultimate unification of China by Qin in 221 BCE was therefore not merely the victory of one state, but the triumph of a specific model of political organization forged in the fires of centuries of conflict. This model, which privileged administrative efficiency and state power over traditional aristocratic norms, became the enduring template for the Chinese imperial system, profoundly shaping its trajectory for the next two millennia.

title: 6. The World Bank, Latin America’s Lost Decade, and the End of the Cold War
The Regal Crucible: Forging Proto-Republicanism in Early Rome
abstract: This paper explores the often-overlooked proto-republican elements embedded within the monarchical period of early Rome, arguing that the regal era served as a crucial crucible for the eventual forging of the Roman Republic. While traditionally viewed as a period of absolute rule, closer examination of extant literary and archaeological evidence reveals institutional, social, and ideological developments that prefigured later republican structures and values. Specifically, the paper investigates the role of the Senate as an advisory body, the nascent popular assemblies, the contested nature of regal succession and power, and the emerging concept of a public sphere or 'res publica' even under kings. By employing an interdisciplinary approach that synthesizes historical, political science, and sociological methodologies, this study aims to demonstrate how the very challenges and evolving political landscape of the Roman monarchy inadvertently laid the groundwork for a system predicated on shared governance, civic participation, and checks on individual power. The findings suggest that the transition from monarchy to republic was not a sudden rupture but rather a culmination of gradual developments and accumulated experiences within the regal system, highlighting the enduring legacy of this foundational period on Roman political identity.

title: The Saite Recasting: Continuity, Innovation, and Imperial Accommodation in Late Period Egypt
abstract: This paper examines the Saite Dynasty (664-525 BCE) of Egypt's Late Period, focusing on how this era represents a strategic "recasting" of Egyptian identity, traditions, and power structures. It explores the interplay between continuity with earlier Pharaonic traditions, innovative adaptations to new political and economic realities, and the accommodation of foreign imperial powers, particularly the Assyrians and Persians. By analyzing archaeological evidence, textual sources, and iconographic representations, this study demonstrates how the Saite kings skillfully navigated a complex geopolitical landscape while revitalizing Egyptian culture and asserting their legitimacy. This recasting involved a selective appropriation of the past, the development of new administrative and military strategies, and a flexible approach to foreign relations that allowed Egypt to maintain a degree of autonomy and prosperity despite external pressures. The Saite period, therefore, offers a valuable case study for understanding the dynamics of cultural resilience, political adaptation, and imperial negotiation in ancient history.

title: From Colonial Conflict to Global Crisis: The Boer Wars, the Suez Canal, and the Reshaping of Imperial Geopolitics
abstract: This paper examines the intertwined histories of the Boer Wars (1899-1902) and the Suez Crisis (1956) as pivotal events that reshaped imperial geopolitics. It argues that the Boer Wars exposed the limitations and vulnerabilities of British imperial power, fostering anti-colonial sentiment and prompting a reassessment of military and economic strategies. The Suez Crisis, decades later, further accelerated the decline of British influence, demonstrating the rise of new global powers and the increasing importance of international opinion. By analyzing these two conflicts, the paper elucidates how colonial resistance and strategic waterways became key factors in the unraveling of traditional imperial structures and the emergence of a new world order. The study incorporates a multi-faceted approach, drawing on primary sources, secondary scholarship, and geopolitical analysis to offer a comprehensive understanding of these transformative periods. The paper seeks to contribute to a deeper appreciation of the complex legacies of colonialism and the ongoing shifts in global power dynamics.

title: Extraction d’informations dans des rapports d’incidents du réseau électrique à l’aide de LLMs open source
abstract: Effective management of an organization’s knowledge requires processing numerous textual documents. In the context of French power grid incident reports, this task is particularly challenging due to the specificity of the texts and the complexity of the information to be extracted. This study explores the use of large language models (LLMs) to automatically extract relevant information with minimal annotation effort. We experiment with Information Extraction (IE) using various strategies and evaluate each of them quantitatively. Our findings provide insights into the most efficient methods for leveraging LLMs for IE and offer practical guidance to apply them in real-world scenarios, such as the management of power grid incidents.

title: Leveraging large language models for enhanced process model comprehension
Synergistic Embeddings: Learning Joint Representations Across Diverse Data Modalities for Enhanced AI Generalization
abstract: The pursuit of artificial general intelligence (AGI) necessitates the development of models capable of reasoning and learning across diverse data modalities. Current AI systems often excel within specific domains but struggle with generalization to unseen or multimodal scenarios. This paper introduces "Synergistic Embeddings," a novel approach to learning joint representations from heterogeneous data sources. We propose a multi-branch neural network architecture coupled with a contrastive learning objective, designed to project data from different modalities (e.g., images, text, audio) into a shared embedding space. By explicitly encouraging alignment between semantically related instances across modalities and penalizing alignment between unrelated instances, our model learns representations that capture the underlying semantic structure of the data. We evaluate our approach on several multimodal benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in cross-modal retrieval, classification, and few-shot learning tasks compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we analyze the learned embedding space, revealing meaningful semantic clusters and demonstrating the model's ability to generalize to novel combinations of modalities. Our findings highlight the potential of synergistic embeddings for building more robust and generalizable AI systems.

title: Research on the diffusion of low-carbon technologies through trilateral evolutionary game based on incentive mechanisms
The Semantic Blind Spot of Perplexity: A Causal Framework for its Divergence from Human Judgment
abstract: Perplexity is a cornerstone metric for evaluating language models, prized for its computational efficiency and theoretical grounding in information theory. However, a growing body of evidence reveals a significant and often troubling divergence between perplexity scores and human judgments of text quality. Models optimized for low perplexity can generate text that is repetitive, nonsensical, or factually inaccurate, yet human evaluators rate it poorly. This paper argues that this discrepancy arises from a fundamental "semantic blind spot" inherent in the perplexity metric. Perplexity quantifies the statistical likelihood of a sequence of tokens, effectively measuring fluency and adherence to distributional patterns in the training data, but it remains agnostic to the underlying meaning, truthfulness, and logical coherence of the text. To formalize and investigate this problem, we introduce a novel causal framework. Using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), we model the relationships between the language model, the generated text, its statistical properties (measured by perplexity), its semantic properties (a latent construct), and ultimate human judgment. We hypothesize that perplexity and semantic quality are distinct consequences of the text generation process and that semantic quality is the dominant causal parent of human judgment. We conduct a series of experiments using multiple language models and datasets, operationalizing semantic quality with a suite of proxy metrics for factuality, coherence, and relevance. Our results from correlation and causal mediation analyses provide strong empirical support for our framework. We demonstrate that while perplexity has a weak and inconsistent relationship with human scores, our semantic proxies are strong predictors. The analysis reveals that the path from text to human judgment is mediated primarily by semantic content, with perplexity exerting only a minor influence. This work systematically diagnoses the limitations of perplexity and advocates for a shift in evaluation paradigms towards causally-informed, multi-faceted approaches that explicitly account for the semantic dimensions of language.

title: Abductive Generative Dynamics: Unifying Latent Space Inference and Structured Synthesis
abstract: Deep generative models have achieved remarkable success in synthesizing high-fidelity data, yet they often lack mechanisms for structured reasoning and interpretable representation learning. The processes of inferring latent causes from observations and synthesizing complex, structured data are typically treated as separate problems. This paper introduces Abductive Generative Dynamics (AGD), a novel framework that unifies these two processes. AGD models inference as a dynamic, iterative process of abductive reasoning, seeking the most plausible latent explanation for a given observation. This inferred latent code, rich in explanatory structure, then guides a synthesis process capable of generating complex, coherent artifacts such as molecular graphs, programmatic structures, or compositional scenes. Our proposed architecture operationalizes this framework by combining an iterative amortized inference network with a structured decoder, such as a graph neural network. The model is trained end-to-end using a modified evidence lower bound objective that promotes both accurate reconstruction and the discovery of explanatory latent factors. We demonstrate empirically across multiple challenging domains that AGD outperforms state-of-the-art generative models in terms of generation quality, sample diversity, and structural validity. Furthermore, we show that the dynamic inference process yields a highly interpretable and disentangled latent space, where traversals correspond to meaningful manipulations of the generated data's underlying structure. AGD represents a significant step toward creating generative models that not only synthesize what they see but also reason about the underlying principles that structure their domain.

title: Semantic Bridges: Learning Unified Embedding Spaces Through Cross-Modal Anchoring
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach, termed "Semantic Bridges," for learning unified embedding spaces across different modalities. Our method leverages cross-modal anchoring to establish correspondences between data points from disparate modalities, effectively creating bridges that facilitate the transfer of semantic information. We formulate the problem as a joint optimization of embedding functions and alignment transformations, ensuring that semantically similar data points, regardless of their modality, are mapped to nearby locations in the unified embedding space. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing its superior performance in cross-modal retrieval, zero-shot learning, and multimodal classification tasks. The results highlight the ability of Semantic Bridges to capture intricate relationships between modalities and generate robust, semantically meaningful representations.

title: The Semantic Blind Spot of Perplexity: A Causal Framework for its Divergence from Human Judgment
abstract: Perplexity is a cornerstone metric for evaluating language models, prized for its computational efficiency and theoretical grounding in information theory. However, a growing body of evidence reveals a significant and often troubling divergence between perplexity scores and human judgments of text quality. Models optimized for low perplexity can generate text that is repetitive, nonsensical, or factually inaccurate, yet human evaluators rate it poorly. This paper argues that this discrepancy arises from a fundamental "semantic blind spot" inherent in the perplexity metric. Perplexity quantifies the statistical likelihood of a sequence of tokens, effectively measuring fluency and adherence to distributional patterns in the training data, but it remains agnostic to the underlying meaning, truthfulness, and logical coherence of the text. To formalize and investigate this problem, we introduce a novel causal framework. Using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), we model the relationships between the language model, the generated text, its statistical properties (measured by perplexity), its semantic properties (a latent construct), and ultimate human judgment. We hypothesize that perplexity and semantic quality are distinct consequences of the text generation process and that semantic quality is the dominant causal parent of human judgment. We conduct a series of experiments using multiple language models and datasets, operationalizing semantic quality with a suite of proxy metrics for factuality, coherence, and relevance. Our results from correlation and causal mediation analyses provide strong empirical support for our framework. We demonstrate that while perplexity has a weak and inconsistent relationship with human scores, our semantic proxies are strong predictors. The analysis reveals that the path from text to human judgment is mediated primarily by semantic content, with perplexity exerting only a minor influence. This work systematically diagnoses the limitations of perplexity and advocates for a shift in evaluation paradigms towards causally-informed, multi-faceted approaches that explicitly account for the semantic dimensions of language.

title: Synergistic Embeddings: Learning Joint Representations Across Diverse Data Modalities for Enhanced AI Generalization
abstract: The pursuit of artificial general intelligence (AGI) necessitates the development of models capable of reasoning and learning across diverse data modalities. Current AI systems often excel within specific domains but struggle with generalization to unseen or multimodal scenarios. This paper introduces "Synergistic Embeddings," a novel approach to learning joint representations from heterogeneous data sources. We propose a multi-branch neural network architecture coupled with a contrastive learning objective, designed to project data from different modalities (e.g., images, text, audio) into a shared embedding space. By explicitly encouraging alignment between semantically related instances across modalities and penalizing alignment between unrelated instances, our model learns representations that capture the underlying semantic structure of the data. We evaluate our approach on several multimodal benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in cross-modal retrieval, classification, and few-shot learning tasks compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we analyze the learned embedding space, revealing meaningful semantic clusters and demonstrating the model's ability to generalize to novel combinations of modalities. Our findings highlight the potential of synergistic embeddings for building more robust and generalizable AI systems.

title: Mind the Gap: A Causal Framework for Quantifying the Misalignment Between Automated Metrics and Human Judgment in Generative Models
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative models in natural language processing and computer vision has created a critical challenge in evaluation. While automated metrics like BLEU, ROUGE, and FID are widely used for their efficiency and scalability, their correlation with human judgment is often weak and inconsistent. This misalignment, or "gap," can lead to misleading conclusions about model performance and hinder genuine progress in the field. This paper argues that merely measuring the correlation between metrics and human scores is insufficient. Instead, we must understand the causal factors that drive this misalignment. We introduce a novel causal framework, based on Structural Causal Models (SCMs), to formally define, identify, and quantify the causal effects of model and data characteristics on the gap between automated metric scores and human quality judgments. We define the "Causal Misalignment Effect" (CME) as the extent to which an intervention on a model property (e.g., changing model size or decoding strategy) alters this gap. Using the task of abstractive text summarization as a case study, we conduct experiments with several state-of-the-art models. By applying backdoor adjustment, we estimate the causal impact of factors like model architecture and prompt complexity on the misalignment of metrics like ROUGE and BERTScore. Our results demonstrate that certain model improvements, while increasing both human and automated scores, can causally increase the misalignment, suggesting that the metric becomes a less reliable proxy for quality under specific conditions. This causal perspective provides a more rigorous foundation for metric development and offers practical guidance for researchers on when to trust or distrust automated evaluation.

Functionalization of 1,3,5‐Triazines: A Modular Entry to Cyanine‐Conjugated Imaging Probes
abstract: Multifunctional platforms are essential tools in biomedical research, particularly to develop dual imaging probes that combine, for example, fluorescence imaging (FLI) and positron emission tomography (PET). We report the design of a modular trisubstituted 1,3,5‐triazine scaffold synthesized from 2,4,6‐trichloro‐1,3,5‐triazine via sequential nucleophilic aromatic substitutions with amino‐functionalized spacers. Orthogonal protecting groups enabled selective conjugation with a cyanine dye (Cy) and a DOTA chelator for FLI and PET, respectively. The third arm was functionalized with DUPA, a prostate‐specific membrane antigen (PSMA)‐targeting pseudopeptide, via CuAAC chemistry. Despite unsuccessful attempts with Cy7 derivative (IR780), dual labeling with Cy5 and DOTA was achieved efficiently. Compound 19 exhibited optical properties comparable to commercial Cy5. These results highlight the versatility of this synthetic strategy and the potential of 19 as a dual‐modality imaging agent.

title: Bioconversion of Agricultural Residues into Nutrient-Rich Compost: A Sustainable Approach to Waste Valorization
abstract: The rapid expansion of agro-industrial production has generated large volumes of lignocellulosic agricultural residues, many of which remain underutilized or are burned, causing nutrient loss and environmental pollution. Composting provides a sustainable pathway to convert these wastes into valuable organic amendments, yet the inherent resistance of plant structural polymers often slows decomposition and reduces compost quality. Emerging research highlights the potential of microbial consortia, combining lignocellulolytic, thermotolerant and nutrient-mobilizing microorganisms to substantially enhance biomass breakdown and accelerate compost maturation. These tailored communities improve organic matter transformation and humus formation by coordinating complementary metabolic activities under optimized composting conditions. This review synthesizes recent advances in consortium-based composting and outlines their advantages over conventional methods. Overall, the strategic use of microbial consortia offers a cost-effective and environmentally sound approach for converting agricultural residues into high-quality compost, strengthening soil fertility and supporting sustainable land management.

title: Synthesis and Biological Activity of Some Novel Quinolinones Derived from 1-Ethyl-1,2-dihydro-4-hydroxy- 2-oxoquinoline-3-carbaldehyde
abstract: The reactivity of 1-ethyl-1,2-dihydro-4-hydroxy-2-oxoquinoline-3-carbaldehyde (1) towards some diaza-nucleophiles has been investigated, under various reaction conditions. 1-Ethyl-1,2-dihydro-4-hydroxy-2-oxoquinoline-3-carbaldehyde (1) was reacted with hydrazine, phenylhydrazine, 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, acid hydrazides, semicarbazide, thiosemicarbazides, thiocarbohydrazide, ortho-phenylenediamine and ortho-aminophenol. It was found that solvents used in these reactions impacted product selectivity. Accordingly, these reactions led to various open-chain and/or cyclic derivatives of quinolinone. The structure of the new compounds was determined using spectroscopic techniques and elemental analyses. All products were screened in vitro to determine their antimicrobial, antioxidant and antitumor activities. Compounds 2a and 2c are the most active compounds against bacterial and fungal strains. While the most effective compounds against breast cancer (MCF-7) are compounds 2a and 8a.

title: Cyclopentyl-linked N-Acylthioureas as Promising Urease Inhibitors: Insights from in vitro Bioassay, Structure-activity Relationships and Computational Analysis
abstract: Helicobacter pylori is a Gram-negative bacteria responsible for gastrointestinal disorders, including chronic gastritis and potentially life-threatening conditions like gastric cancer. To manage these adverse outcomes, inhibiting the urease enzyme emerges as a promising strategy. A concise set of cyclopentyl-bearing N-acylthioureas 4a–j was synthesized, characterized and assessed for their ability to inhibit urease enzyme. All the tested compounds exhibited urease inhibitory activities, displaying superior enzyme inhibition when compared to the standard, thiourea (IC50 values 23.00 ± 0.03 μM). 4a and 4b exhibited the highest inhibitory efficacy with IC50 values of 2.21 ± 0.62 and 3.92 ± 0.59 μM, respectively. Both compounds demonstrated ≈10- and ≈6-folds superior inhibition than standard inhibitor, respectively. Moreover, molecular docking investigations revealed crucial interactions between potent ligands and active site residues. Molecular dynamics simulations and ADME properties revealed ligand-protein stability and druglikeness behavior of potent leads paving the way for treatment for gastritis.

title: Synthesis of Novel Indole Derivatives, Antiproliferative Activity, Apoptosis, and Molecular Docking Studies
abstract: Novel indole-containing analogs were synthesized via a one-pot, multi-component Passerini reaction and subsequently evaluated for their anticancer activity against HeLa, MCF-7, and A549 cancer cell lines using the MTT assay. Among the synthesized compounds, (2-(cyclohexylamino)-1-(3-fluorophenyl)-2-oxoethyl 2-(1H-indol-3-yl)acetate (4f), which demonstrated the most potent cytotoxic activity, exhibited promising results with IC50 values of 17.71 and 19.92 μM against HeLa and MCF-7 cells, respectively. Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that compound 4f significantly induced apoptosis in HeLa cells in a concentration-dependent manner. Furthermore, molecular docking studies into the active site of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-xL indicated that compound 4f binds with good affinity, which is consistent with its considerable efficacy in the in vitro tests.

title: Engineered self-driven intelligent nanomachine induced by target-mediated knock-on effect to determine attomolar nucleic acids
Quercetin-3 Sulfate: A Novel Inhibitor Targeting Helicobacter Pylori Revealed through Molecular Docking and Dynamic Simulations
abstract: Type II dehydroquinase (DHQase) is a pivotal enzyme in the synthesis of aromatic amino acids essential for Helicobacter pylori’s survival. It possesses distinctive characteristics and exhibits limited sequence or structural similarity to other bacterial organisms. Molecular docking was employed to screen Middle Eastern medicinal plants to identify the most promising candidates for inhibiting DHQase with the highest affinity. Docking against DHQase was performed on 2,213 ligand conformers derived from 151 natural Middle Eastern medicinal plants. Ten hits with the most favorable docking scores were selected for subsequent ADMET assay analysis and molecular dynamic simulation. Of all of the top hits, quercetin-3 sulfate had the highest docking score. This compound adhered to the druglikeness roles and demonstrated no toxicity. MD simulations indicated that the quercetin-3 sulfate-DHQase complex exhibited higher levels of stabilized RMSD and higher values of stably contributed amino acid residues than other structures. This study underscores the novel inhibitory potential of quercetin 3-sulfate against DHQase, demonstrating the highest ligand affinity. This observation suggests the validity of quercetin 3-sulfate as a potent drug for combating H. pylori infection.

title: Behavior of temperate reef fish species around oyster aquaculture farms and natural rock reefs
abstract: Shellfish aquaculture gear can support shelter oriented wild fish by providing structurally complex habitat (Ferriss et al. 2021, Theuerkauf et al. 2021). Fish benefit from shellfish aquaculture gear through increased foraging opportunities, sheltering sites, breeding habitat, nursery areas and protection from predators (Mercaldo-Allen et al. 2025, Armbruster 2024, Corrigan et al. 2024) and exhibit successful growth, reproduction and survival (Brown et al. 2022). A better understanding of the interactions of wild fish with shellfish farms can inform fisheries resource management through quantification of the potential benefits provided to fish by aquaculture gear (Mercaldo-Allen et al. 2021, Farrell et al. 2023, Ambrose and Munroe 2025). The goal of this work is to catalog and quantify behaviors associated with habitat use of three temperate reef fish species, cunner (Tautogolabrus adspersus), scup (Stenotomus chrysops) and tautog (Tautoga onitis), around eastern oyster aquaculture cages on shellfish farms and on boulders at natural rock reefs in Long Island Sound, Connecticut, USA, in order to document the ecological services and habitat function provided by cages, relative to natural structured seafloor. This repository contains behavior data for tautog, scup and cunner associated with oyster cages sampled in Long Island Sound, Connecticut, USA. Video was collected using GoPro cameras and analyzed using Noldus Observer XT. Detailed methods can be found in Mercaldo-Allen et al. (2021, 2023). title: Tenualosa ilisha
abstract: Tenualosa ilisha Common name. Hilsa. Diagnosis. Distinguished from Nematalosa nasus in lower reaches of rivers in Persian Gulf basin by: ● last dorsal ray shorter than first branched dorsal ray / ● upper jaw with median notch. Size up to 600 mm SL, usually about 360 mm SL, and up to 2.5 kg. Distribution. From Persian Gulf along coasts of Indian subcontinent east to Irrawaddy and Salween (Myanmar). In West Asia,enters Karun and Shatt al Arab/Arvand to spawn upstream in Euphrates and Tigris. In Tigris, migrates as far anadromous or landlocked, with rare reports of resident marine stocks. One species, T. thibaudeaui, is a pure freshwater species endemic to the Mekong. All Tenualosa are highly valued as food fish and provide a livelihood for many, if not millions, of small-scale fisher families. Overfishing is a serious issue throughout their range. However, as this is due mostly to artisanal fisheries, catches are rarely reported accurately, and the extent of the decline of all species might be much underestimated. The scientific and common names of T. ilisha require some clarification.This species is widely called Hilsa, which is confused with the Kelee shad, Hilsa kelee. Kelee and Hilsa are sympatric in the Gulf of Oman and along the southern coast of the Arabian Peninsula. Kelee enters estuaries, and both species are easily distinguished by the presence of prominent striae on the top of the head in H. kelee (vs. absence in T. ilisha). Further reading. Whitehead 1985 (diversity). north as Qal’at Salih, and in Euphrates, as far north as Yaou. Local freshwater populations in many large rivers in South Asia. Habitat. At sea in coastal waters, migrates to lower and middle reaches of large rivers to spawn. A resident population is suspected in Kuwait Bay, which does not appear to migrate upstream and spawns in sea or in freshwater fan of Shatt al Arab/Arvand. Biology. Anadromous, usually migrating 50–100 km upstream.
