Lemmas for Flourishing-Augmented Reasoning (FAR): Intermediate Propositions Toward a General Theory of Hybrid Appraisal
abstract: Abstract Flourishing-Augmented Reasoning (FAR) has recently been formalised through a foundational set of axioms specifying the structural conditions under which appraisal becomes reality-aligned, narratively coherent, and future-expansive. These axioms provide the base architecture, but a complete theory of hybrid human–AI appraisal requires intermediate propositions that clarify how these axioms operate dynamically across cognitive ecologies. This paper introduces the FAR Lemmas: formally stated, conceptually independent propositions that bridge the axioms and the forthcoming Theorem of FAR. Each lemma articulates the lawful relationships between ecological bandwidth, interpretive curvature, cognitive stability, reciprocity with AI systems, and the directional movement of appraisal. Drawing on the DARK Hypothesis, the Seligman Proof, and the PERMA–NARMA–DARMA appraisal ecology framework, the FAR Lemmas specify how upward, downward, or fragmented cognitive trajectories unfold under different ecological conditions. Together, these propositions advance FAR from a structural foundation toward a general theory of hybrid appraisal, preparing the ground for the formal theorem that will unify flourishing-compatible reasoning into an integrated mathematical-psychological architecture.

title: <b>ECOTOXICOLOGICAL IMPACT OF COPPER OXIDE NANOPARTICLES IN AQUATIC SYSTEMS: ASSESSMENT USING FISH MODELS</b>
abstract: This increasing use of the copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO-NPs) in different industries has created great concern on the ecotoxicology effects of the nanoparticles on aquatic environments. This paper will include the assessment of the toxicological impact of the CuO-NPs on a freshwater fish model, which will combine a nanoparticle characterization analysis with a multi-level biological response. TEM, XRD, FTIR, DLS, and zeta potential were used to characterize synthesized CuO-NPs, which are characterized as crystalline monophasic, and positively charged on the surface, which promotes the colloidal stability and bio-interaction. Fish were subjected to various environmentally realistic levels and, it was found that copper accumulated in a dose-dependent way with the gills taking the lead followed by the liver and kidneys. This bioaccumulation elicited a cascade of the negative effects such as oxidative stress was observed by the initial increase and later inhibition of antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, GPx) and a pronounced increase in lipid peroxidation (MDA). Moreover, exposure also resulted in severe genotoxicity, which was represented by the amplified formation of micronucleus and nuclear aberration as well as drastic histopathological harm at the tissues of the gill, liver and kidney. These sub-cellular injuries were observed as major behavioral changes whereby there was erratic swimming and poor feeding. The use of the integrated toxicity assessment proves that there is a definite correlation between physicochemical characteristics and multi-organ toxicity, and the ecological threat that CuO-NPs present to aquatic life is significant, which is why the development of strict guidelines in relation to this toxicogen is necessary.

title: GLOBAL SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNOLOGICAL TRENDS AND THEIR IMPACT ON INTEGRATION PROCESSES: PROSPECTS FOR THE FORMATION OF A UNIFIED SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNOLOGICAL SPACE
abstract: Аннотация. В статье исследуются глобальные научно-технологические тенденции, формирующие новые принципы и формы международного взаимодействия. Рассматриваются процессы цифровизации, развитие искусственного интеллекта, гуманизация технологий, демографический переход и климатическая трансформация. Результаты анализа свидетельствуют, что совокупность указанных процессов усиливает роль международного научно-технического сотрудничества и способствует формированию единого научно-технологического пространства в рамках СНГ, ЕАЭС и Союзного государства, направленного на консолидацию научных ресурсов и укрепление технологического суверенитета региона. Abstract. The article examines global scientific and technological trends that shape new principles and forms of international interaction. It analyzes processes of digitalization, the development of artificial intelligence, the humanization of technology, demographic transition, and climate transformation. The results indicate that these processes enhance the role of international scientific and technical cooperation and contribute to the formation of a unified scientific and technological space within the CIS, the EAEU, and the Union State, aimed at consolidating scientific resources and strengthening the technological sovereignty of the region. Annotatsiya. Maqolada xalqaro hamkorlikning yangi tamoyillari va shakllarini belgilab berayotgan global ilmiy-texnologik tendensiyalar tahlil qilinadi. Raqamlashtirish jarayonlari, sun’iy intellektni rivojlantirish, texnologiyalarning gumanizatsiyasi, demografik oʻzgarishlar va iqlim transformatsiyasi jarayonlari koʻrib chiqiladi. Tadqiqot natijalari ushbu jarayonlar xalqaro ilmiy-texnik hamkorlik rolini kuchaytirishini va MDH, YEOII hamda Ittifoq Davlati doirasida yagona ilmiy-texnologik makonni shakllantirishga, ilmiy resurslarni konsolidatsiya qilish hamda mintaqaning texnologik suverenitetini mustahkamlashga xizmat qilishini koʻrsatadi.

title: Efficacy of a novel, aquatically formulated humic acid product (AC Aqua) for mitigating harmful algae blooms
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of the aquatically formulated humic acid product AC Aqua in reducing total phosphorus concentrations and controlling the proliferation of two harmful algal species, golden algae Prymnesium parvum and Microcystis aeruginosa. Methods Three treatments of AC Aqua (prophylactic, low dose, and high dose) and a control were tested in 13.3-L mesocosms with and without sediment (n = 6 per treatment) to simulate lined and earthen pond conditions. Prophylactic treatment (5 mL/m3) was applied 10 d before P. parvum (91 cells/mL) and M. aeruginosa (246 cells/mL) inoculation. Low (5 mL/m3) and high (7.67 mL/m3) doses were applied 6 h after inoculation. Phosphorus concentrations were measured before and after application to assess binding, while algal cell counts were monitored weekly for 7 weeks for each trial. Results Within 6 h, all AC Aqua treatments reduced total phosphorus, with the high-dose and sediment treatments having a significant reduction in phosphorus, compared with control groups, in both trials. Significant reductions in P. parvum cell counts were observed in the prophylactic treatments beginning in week 3 (P = 0.017). By week 7, all treatments had substantially lower cell counts compared with controls, with several treatment groups, particularly those with sediment, falling below 10,000 cells/mL, while control groups remained above 90,000 cells/mL. Significant reductions in M. aeruginosa cell counts were observed in the prophylactic treatments beginning in week 2 (P = 0.014). By week 6, all treatments were below 10,000 cells/mL, while control groups remained above 65,000 cells/mL. Conclusions AC Aqua effectively reduced P. parvum and M. aeruginosa cell densities in eutrophic systems when applied prophylactically. Its lag effect indicates a nutrient management mechanism, supporting its use as a sustainable, preventative strategy.

title: Addressing Daigou from the Perspective of Channel Competition: Strategy for Retail Management
abstract: In China’s on-demand service platforms, daigou agents utilize locational differences through proxy purchasing. Daigou creates an informal supply chain that directly competes with official channels. This study incorporates daigou arbitrage into the channel competition framework via a multi-stage Stackelberg game-theoretic model. An analysis of the subgame perfect Nash equilibrium shows that daigou activity disrupts the manufacturer’s profits. We have thus developed a strategy based on mathematical optimization and compared its effectiveness and side effects with those of existing methods. We came to identify purchase restrictions as one of the most powerful strategies. Equilibrium analysis and numerical experiments confirm that proper purchase restriction choices reduce daigou arbitrage and minimize negative impacts on legitimate demand. This work provides the first game-theoretic model that integrates informal proxy-purchase supply chains into dual-channel competitions.

title: Intake, digestibility, performance, and compensatory gain of post-weaned Guzolando (Guzerat × Holstein) heifers raised on tropical pasture
GROWTH RESPONSE OF CLARIAS GARIEPINUS FINGERLINGS TO SELECTED COMMERCIAL FEED
abstract: This study evaluated the growth performance of Clarias gariepinus fingerlings fed with three commercial feeds: Coppen feed, Multifeed, and Vital feed over six weeks. The results showed that fish fed with Coppen feed attained the highest average weight (32.53 ± 3.62 g), followed by Multi feed (30.02 ± 3.44 g) and while Vital feed resulted in the lowest weight (23.14 ± 2.41 g). Although the mean weekly weight gains differed significantly among feeds (F = 0.6673, P = 0.03), there was no significant difference in weekly weight increase (F = 0.9097, P = 0.4237). Similarly, the final mean lengths were highest in Coppen-fed fish (17.11 ± 0.54 cm) and lowest in Vital-fed fish (14.13 ± 0.33 cm), with significant differences observed after six weeks (F = 0.9097, P = 0.004). The increase in mean length followed a similar trend, with the Coppen feed inducing the greatest growth (10.30 ± 0.14 cm). The specific growth rates were highest for Coppen (3.90 ± 0.0) and Multi feed (3.71 ± 0.0) compared to Vital feed (2.54 ± 0.0). The survival rates were 100% for the Coppen and Multifeed groups, but only 80% for the vital feed group. Proximate analysis revealed that the Coppen and Multi feeds contained higher crude protein (45%) and lipid contents, whereas the Vital feed had the highest crude fiber and moisture levels. Overall, Coppen and Multifeeds demonstrated superior growth performance and nutritional profiles, indicating their suitability for optimal production of C. gariepinus fingerlings

title: Effect of palm frond compost and phosphate fertilization on vegetative growth characteristics of corn in a gypsum soil.
abstract: Abstract field experiment was conducted during autumn season of 2024 to study effect of palm frond compost and phosphate fertilization on the growth and yield of yellow corn in gypsum soil. palm frond compost added at levels of 0, 10 and 20 tons ha −1 , and phosphate fertilizer added at levels of 0, 40, 80, and 120 kg ha −1 . The results for the dry weight at the age of (35) days showed a significant increase with the increase in the compost level from 0 to 20 tons ha −1 , as the average dry weight reached (90.04) g plant −1 when not added, and rose to (110.84) g plant −1 at the highest level of compost (20 tons ha −1 ). Phosphorus levels also had a significant effect, as the level 0 kg ha −1 recorded the lowest dry weight of (84.99) g plant −1 , while the level 120 kg ha −1 gave the highest dry weight of (112.2) g Plant −1 , there was a significant effect of compost levels and phosphorus levels on nitrogen concentration in the vegetative group at the age of (35) days. It was noted that increasing the compost level from 0 to 20 tons ha −1 led to a gradual increase in nitrogen concentration, as the treatment without adding compost recorded a concentration of 1.49%, while the highest concentration was 1.79% when adding 20 tons ha −1 of compost. Phosphorus levels also affected the increase in nitrogen concentration from 0 to 120 kg ha −1 , with the highest value recorded at 120 kg ha −1 , representing a rate of 2.10%.

title: The optimal storage temperature for Ngoc Linh ginseng (Panax Vietnamensis Ha et Gush.)
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to determine optimal storage conditions for preserving ten-year-old fresh Ngoc Linh ginseng (Panax vietnamensis Ha et Grushv.), a highly valued medicinal plant grown in the Ngoc Linh mountain region of Vietnam. Effective postharvest storage methods are important to maintain Ngoc Linh ginseng’s quality and phytochemical integrity. Research Method: Ethylene production and respiration rates of Ngoc Linh ginseng were evaluated, followed by a preliminary investigation in the dry season to understand the impact of temperature on its quality and shelf life. Finally, subsequent experiments were implemented in both seasons to determine the optimal storage temperature. Findings: Ethylene production and respiration rates of the Ngoc Linh ginseng were consistently low in both the dry and rainy seasons. The ginseng experienced severe dehydration and fungal decay at room temperature, while storage at 0 °C led to chilling injuries. Higher temperatures of 10 °C and 15 °C accelerated the deterioration of the ginseng. In contrast, storage at 3 °C and 6 °C significantly extended the ginseng's shelf life. A follow-up experiment confirmed that 3 °C was the most effective for retaining freshness, skin brightness, visual sensory attributes, and total saponin content in Ngoc Linh ginseng in both seasons over 35 days. Research limitations: No limitations were identified. Originality/Value: This is the first study on extending the fresh storage of Ngoc Linh ginseng, a highly valuable herb of Vietnam. Identifying 3 °C as the optimal storage temperature provides a potential standard for fresh ginseng preservation and supports future research and commercial applications.

title: Influence of Adding Fresh Azolla on the Productive and Physiological Traits of Iraqi Local Ducks
abstract: Abstract The aim of this research was to evaluation the effects of feeding fresh azolla on the physiological and productive characteristics of Iraqi local ducks. A total of 72 local ducks, one week old, weighed an average of 108 g. We randomly divided the chicks into four treatments, each consisting of three replicates and containing 6 birds per replicate. The following were the treatments: T2, T3 and T4 Add 5, 10 and 15% fresh Azolla of basal diet, respectively. The results indicated that Azolla at 5, 10, and 15% inclusion levels in local duck indicated a significant increase (P≤0.05) in body weights, weight gain, and feed conversion among the treatments compared to the control treatment. There was not a significant (P≤0.05) effect on feed intake. However, fresh Azolla supplementation did not affect total protein, total cholesterol, triglyceride, ALT, and AST levels in blood serum. Therefore, adding fresh Azolla to the diet of local ducks may be quite beneficial. It can be added up to 15% of the ducks’ diet to improve their growth performance.

title: A Comparison of changes in biochemical traits of local Awassi ewes dosed with aqueous extract of green tea and a mixture of vitamins A and E
abstract: Abstract Current study was aimed in the cattle area of the unit of Production of Animal, Agriculture College, Kirkuk University, from September 2, 2024, to December 17, 2024. The study intended to compare the impacts of green tea extract, a mixture of vitamins A and E, and their conjunction on physiological measures in Awassi ewes during mid and late pregnancy. Twenty pregnant ewes with mean weight of 56.6 ± 4.70 kg were used. The animals were haphazardly separated into 4 treatment groups, every one composed of 5 pregnant sheep. The first group was orally administered 50 mL of deionized water without additives and act as the control. The 2 nd group obtained an aqueous Camellia sinensis extract at 100 mg/kg weight of body, while the 3rd group was given 200 mg/kg BW of the same extract. The fourth group was supplemented with a combination of vitamin A (400 IU/kg weight of body) and vitamin E (200 IU/kg weight of body). The experimental treatments improved biochemical in blood measures, by elevating levels of protein, globulin and high-density lipoproteins (HDL). Furthermore, low density lipoproteins (LDL), Triglyceride, Aspartate and Alanine trans-aminase (AST) and (ALT) are reduced. According to the Observations presented previously, it can be Determined that supplementation with Camellia sinensis extract, particularly at the higher concentration of 200 mg/kg, and combination of vitamins A and E, significantly improves biochemical parameters in ewes.

title: Tabla S1. Genes reported and their references, associated with morphological characteristics, productive and reproductive behavior, and carcass and meat quality in pig breeds.
Oscilações de temperatura que ocasionam a perda de qualidade do ovo
abstract: O setor avícola brasileiro tem experimentado um avanço significativo, impulsionado principalmente por pesquisas científicas que demonstram os benefícios do consumo de ovos para a saúde humana. Esses estudos indicam que os ovos contribuem para a melhoria da função do HDL (lipoproteína de alta densidade) e para a redução do risco de doenças cardiovasculares, o que tem aumentado consideravelmente a demanda por esse alimento e para atender a essa crescente demanda, os produtores de ovos no Brasil estão adotando práticas cada vez mais profissionais e tecnológicas, e essas práticas incluem desde a construção de instalações apropriadas até avanços na genética, na alimentação e nos cuidados veterinários, proporcionando um ambiente mais controlado e produtivo para a criação de aves. Este estudo, por meio de revisão de literatura, tem como objetivo compreender os efeitos da temperatura na qualidade interna e externa dos ovos, a fim de identificar práticas e estratégias que garantam sua preservação até o consumidor final, contribuindo para a segurança alimentar e a satisfação do cliente. A manutenção da qualidade dos ovos é altamente influenciada pela temperatura de armazenamento, sendo que temperaturas mais altas aceleram a perda de qualidade, enquanto o armazenamento refrigerado, em condições ideais entre 4 e 5°C, retarda os processos de degradação, preservando a qualidade dos ovos por um período mais prolongado.

title: An analysis of hemoglobin levels and body fat percentage on leg power in volleyball athletes
abstract: This study aimed to determine the possible relationship between fat percentage and hemoglobin levels on leg power levels. It employed an analytical observational design using a cross-sectional approach. The sampling technique applied was purposive sampling, with the sample studied involving 24 male volleyball athletes aged under 22 years. Hemoglobin was assessed using the cyanmethemoglobin method. Body fat percentage was measured using Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis with the Omron Karada Scan HBF-358, while leg power was evaluated using the vertical jump test. The results indicated a strong negative relationship between the percentage of body fat and leg power (p=0.002; r=-.610), and a strong positive relationship between hemoglobin levels and leg power (p=0.001; r=0.613). The study demonstrated that a higher body fat percentage is associated with high power levels. In contrast, elevated hemoglobin concentrations are also positively related to power, indicating that both oxygen-carrying capacity and body composition may influence muscular performance.

title: The Impact of LH, FSH and Dopamine on the productive performance of two genetic local quail lines
abstract: Abstract The study was conducted in the field of the Department of Animal Production, College of Agriculture and Forestry, University of Mosul for the period from 1/2/2024 to 13/4/2025. The main aim in this objective is to determine the impact of genetic line (feather color), some candidate gene sites which stimulating LH and FSH hormones, and Dopamine with their interaction on production performance of two local quail lines. The study was designed to include five treatments as follows: T1. control, T2. Luteinizing Hormone (LH) injections, T3. Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) injections, T4. Dopamine injections, T5. Dopamine administration. 60 birds were randomly assigned to the above treatments, which included three replicates for each treatment, with four birds at a sex ratio of (3♀:1♀) per replicate from each genetic line. The results were showed that there was significant superiority (p≤0.05) for stimulating genes of LH and FSH and Dopamine compared to control group in most productive traits such as the age of sexual maturity, as it was earlier at this age, cumulative number of eggs, egg yield %, average egg weight, average egg mass, feed conversion efficiency, fertility %, Hatching % and Decrease in the rate of embryo’s mortality compared to the control group. Both FSH injection and dopamine administration achieved the highest hatching rate of fertile eggs, reaching 100%. Black quails recorded a significant superiority in the whiteness and hue unit compared to brown quails for all treatments.

title: Calculating the heterosis and productive traits of different genetic combinations of Japanese quail
abstract: Abstract This study was conducted in the poultry fields of the Animal Production Department at the College of Agriculture, Tikrit University, from 1st October 2024 to 23rd March 2025. The study included two generations of Japanese quail, aiming to estimate the hybrid strength for some production traits of various genetic compositions of the Japanese quail. For the hybrids to be estimated, a group of 96 Japanese quail (males and females) with white and brown plumage was selected, all at the same sexual maturity age of 37 days, which were then divided according to four treatments, each with eight replications consisting of three birds per replication for mating purposes. The treatments consisted of pure brown × brown (B×B). white × white (W×W), and reciprocal combinations for the third treatment white with brown (W♂ ×♀B) and for the fourth brown with white (B♂ × W♀). During the experimental period, after conducting showed numerical superiority in egg weight during the first week for the B×B and W♂ × ♀B treatments, though the differences were not statistically significant compared to the other treatments, However, the four treatments did not showed significantly higher. from the other treatments. For egg yolk weight, the second and third treatments performed better than the first and fourth. As for yolk diameter, the crossing results showed superiority for the second treatment with its pure cross (W×W) over the other treatments, while the first and third treatments outperformed the fourth treatment. In the study of relative yolk weight, the third treatment with its reciprocal cross (W♂ ×♀B) showed significantly higher to the first treatment with its pure cross (B×B). The egg shape index was highest in the B×B group, indicating a potential genetic influence of the brown line on this trait.

title: Effects of Vitamin D3 Supplementation during Mating or Gestation on Antioxidant Status and Reproductive Parameters in Gray Shirazi Ewes
abstract: Recent studies suggest that vitamin D3 may have preventive and therapeutic effects on autoimmune disease, cancer, and type 1 and 2 diabetes beyond the skeletal condition and calcium metabolism. To demonstrate the effects of a single 10,000 IU/kg vitamin D3 IM injection during mating and pregnancy on reproductive and antioxidant factors, 21 Gray Shirazi ewes with a parity of 1 to 3, which were kept under industrial conditions, were used for this research. All ewes underwent estrus synchronization by placing a sponge containing Flurogestone acetate for 13 days, followed by an injection of 400 units of Pregnant Mare Serum Gonadotropin hormone on the 13th day. Then, ewes were divided into three groups: the first group served as control (without any supplementation), the second group, called pre-pregnancy, received vitamin D3 10 days before laparoscopic insemination, and the third group, which received the supplement in mid-pregnancy (at the 15th week of pregnancy). Blood samples were collected from the ewes at four different stages: the first stage was 10 days after vitamin D3 injection (at the time of insemination), the second stage occurred about 15 weeks after insemination (about 10 days after vitamin D3 injection), the third stage was 2 weeks before lambing, and the fourth stage took place 2 weeks after lambing. The study's findings indicated that vitamin D3 supplementation has no significant effect on reproductive factors in Gray Shirazi ewes (p≥0.05). However, a significant decrease in blood cortisol levels was observed during both pre-pregnancy and mid-pregnancy. Additionally, there was a significant increase in antioxidant factors, such as superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase, during mid-pregnancy. This conclusion can be related to the racial differences in sheep, the supplement's dose, and the timing and frequency of injections.­

title: Feeding a persistent laying hen from day 0 until 110 weeks of age: Performance Impact
Responses to a nutritional supplement of lactating buffaloes exposed to hot weather conditions
abstract: Recent studies focus on animal welfare, heat stress (HS), climate change, and enteric methane (CH4) emissions from livestock. To mitigate HS effects and reduce CH4 emissions, various strategies exist. This study evaluated a commercial nutritional supplement in lactating dairy buffaloes during summer, assessing its impact on diet digestibility, milk production, and CH4 emissions. The supplement contained yeast, capsaicin, Yucca schidigera, garlic, and other compounds. Fifty-seven buffaloes were divided into three groups: control (C) with a basal diet, and two groups receiving 100 g (T1) or 200 g (T2) of the supplement. TMR, faeces, and milk samples were collected, CH4 emissions were measured using a laser gun-type detector, and animal behaviour was monitored via ear-tag sensors. Results indicate that 100 g/head/d of nutritional supplement improved milk yield (p < 0.01, MY = 8.51 L/head/d) and quality, especially the clotting parameter (p < 0.01, RCT = 19.02 min, a30 = 28.99 mm), diet digestibility (p < 0.01) for dry matter (69.12%), crude protein (67.23%), aNDF (62.39%), and starch (97.38%), and animal welfare compared with the control group (MY = 7.92 L/head/d, RCT = 20.01 min, a30 = 28.23 mm, and 60.47%, 57.80%, 50.87% and 96.31% for DM, CP, aNDF, and starch digestibility) and may help animals to counteract the deleterious effects of HS. Moreover, the nutritional supplement decreases (p < 0.05) CH4 emissions (376.28 and 404.68 g/head/d for T1 and C, respectively). Higher doses (i.e., 200 g/head/d) had significant deleterious effects such as worse digestibility, lower milk quality compared lower doses, and did not reduce CH4 as T1.

title: The genetic relationship of the melatonin receptor gene (MTNR1A) to milk production and its components in local goats
abstract: Abstract The study was conducted on a sample of (42) pregnant local goats in the animal field affiliated with the Department of Animal Production / College of Agriculture / University of Diyala for the period from (10/12/2024) to (2/10/2025) with the aim of extracting genetic material (DNA) and determining the genetic structures of the melatonin receptor gene A1 and its relationship to milk production. The results of molecular analysis of the PCR product showed the presence of four genetic variations within the studied area, the first is T22927C TT=29), TC=3, CC=4), the second is G23011A GG=29), GA=5, AA=2), the third is C23195T CT=22), CT=12, TT=2), and the fourth is A23362C (CC=19, AC=14, AA=3). The results of the current study showed significant effects of the studied variations on milk components, as the genetic variation at the T22927C locus had a significant effect on the percentage of lactose in milk during the first month of production, and also on the percentage of density and non-fat solids in relation to the colostrum components, where the TC genotype outperformed the TT and CC genotypes. As for the G23011A genetic variation, it had a significant effect on the percentage of protein, lactose, density, non-fat solids, and minerals during the first and second months of production, where the GA genotype outperformed the GG and AA genotypes. Likewise, the A23362C genetic variation had a significant effect on the percentage of density, non-fat solids, and minerals during the first month of production, where the AC genotype outperformed the CC and AA genotypes. It also had a significant effect on the percentage of protein in relation to the colostrum components, where the AA genotype outperformed the AC and CC genotypes. As for the genetic variation C23195T, it did not have any significant effect on the milk components during the first and second months of production, as well as the colostrum components.

title: Effect of spraying with Sulfate Potassium and Chelated Iron on some vegetative growth characteristics of young Olive trees cv. Arbequina
abstract: Abstract The study was conducted in the olive field of the College of Agriculture, University of Kirkuk, Iraq, located in the Sayyada area, during the period from March 15, 2024, to October 1, 2024. It aimed to investigate the effect of foliar spraying with potassium at three concentrations (0, 1000, and 1500 ) mg L −1 and chelated iron (Fe-EDDHA) at four concentrations (0, 100, 200, and 300 ) mg L −1 on some vegetative growth traits of young olive trees, cultivar Arbequina. Spraying was conducted on three dates throughout the growing season, from March 15 to May 15, with one month between each application. The results can be summarized as follows: spraying with 1500 mg L −1 potassium significantly increased the main stem height, number of lateral branches, leaf area, total chlorophyll content, and dry matter percentage in the leaves, reaching (31.43 cm, 9.94 branches tree −1 , 7.62 cm 2 , 9.56 mg g −1 fresh weight, and 57.97%) respectively. In contrast, spraying with 1000 mg L −1 potassium significantly affected the increase in stem diameter, reaching 14.79 mm. Spraying with chelated iron at 200 and 300 mg L −1 significantly increased main stem height, lateral branching, and leaf area, while 300 mg L −1 significantly improved stem diameter increase, total chlorophyll, and leaf dry matter content (14.96 mm, 9.40 mg g −1 fresh weight, and 59.29%) respectively. The interaction between potassium and iron concentrations showed significant effects on the studied traits.

title: Correlation and regression analysis of milk quality-related functional genes and milk components in normal milk of Liaoning cashmere goats
The Effect of Broodstock Age Composition on the Types and Extent of External Abnormalities in Silver Carp Larvae and Fry (Hypophthalmicthys molitrix)
IDENTIFIKASI AKAR PERMASALAHAN DALAM PROSES PENGGEMUKAN SAPI PEDAGING DI CV INSPIRA PANGAN INDONESIA (KANDANG JURAGAN) MENGGUNAKAN DUA TOOLS PENGENDALIAN MUTU
abstract: AbstrakPenelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengidentifikasi masalahrendahnya bobot sapi pedaging di Kandang Juragan, CVInspira Pangan Indonesia. Dengan menggunakan metodedeskriptif kuantitatif, penelitian in menerapkan metodecheck sheet dan diagram fishbone untuk memahami jeniscacat performa ternak serta penyebab yang mendasarinya.Data dari check sheet mengungkapkan bahwa 14 dari 66sapi menunjukan pertumbuhan yang tidak optimal,dengan variasi yang jelas antar kandang. Diagram fishbonemenentukan empat faktor utama yang menyebabkanmasalah, yaitu unsur manusia, prosedur, bahan, danlingkungan. Isu utama termasuk kurangnya pencatatanrutin, tidak adanya SOP untuk kesehatan dan pakan,kualitas pakan yang terpengaruh oleh perubahan cuaca,serta kondisi kandang yang tidak ideal. Hasil inimenunjukan bahwa manajemen pemeliharaan sangatpenting untuk keberhasilan penggemukan sapi.Penggunaan kedua alat kontrol kualitas tersebut efektifdalam memberikan pemahaman yang sistematis danmenjadi dasar untuk merancang strategi peningkatanproduktivitas ternak yang berkelanjutan.Kata kunci: Penggemukan sapi pedaging; pengendalian mutu;check sheet; fishbone diagram; manajemen pakan; kualitasproduksi ternak.

title: Actinomycetes-Mediated Decomposition of Chicken Feathers: Effects on Nitrogen Recovery over Time
abstract: Rapid urbanisation and intensified poultry production have increased chicken feather waste (CFW), posing environmental concerns due to its recalcitrant keratin content. This study aimed to evaluate the potential of Actinomycetes, specifically Streptomyces sp., isolated from peat-rich soils, to degrade CFW and enhance nitrogen recovery. Chicken feathers collected from a slaughterhouse near Khulna University were washed, dried, ground, and inoculated with 2.5 mL of Streptomyces broth in a controlled composting setup. The decomposition process was monitored over eight days, with daily assessments of total and available nitrogen using the Micro-Kjeldahl method. The results demonstrated a significant increase (p ≤ 0.05) in nitrogen content in the Actinomycetes-treated decomposition group compared to the control. The highest total nitrogen content (6.43%) was observed on day 7, while peak available nitrogen (4.04%) occurred on day 8. The percentage of nitrogen recovery through Actinomycetes activity was 86.1%. These findings confirm the keratinolytic efficiency of Streptomyces in degrading feather waste and enhancing nitrogen mineralisation. Although nitrogen release was gradual, the resulting compost presents a viable slow-release organic fertiliser. This bioconversion approach offers an environmentally sustainable solution for poultry waste management and soil nutrient enrichment in agriculture.

title: Oscilações de temperatura que ocasionam a perda de qualidade do ovo
abstract: O setor avícola brasileiro tem experimentado um avanço significativo, impulsionado principalmente por pesquisas científicas que demonstram os benefícios do consumo de ovos para a saúde humana. Esses estudos indicam que os ovos contribuem para a melhoria da função do HDL (lipoproteína de alta densidade) e para a redução do risco de doenças cardiovasculares, o que tem aumentado consideravelmente a demanda por esse alimento e para atender a essa crescente demanda, os produtores de ovos no Brasil estão adotando práticas cada vez mais profissionais e tecnológicas, e essas práticas incluem desde a construção de instalações apropriadas até avanços na genética, na alimentação e nos cuidados veterinários, proporcionando um ambiente mais controlado e produtivo para a criação de aves. Este estudo, por meio de revisão de literatura, tem como objetivo compreender os efeitos da temperatura na qualidade interna e externa dos ovos, a fim de identificar práticas e estratégias que garantam sua preservação até o consumidor final, contribuindo para a segurança alimentar e a satisfação do cliente. A manutenção da qualidade dos ovos é altamente influenciada pela temperatura de armazenamento, sendo que temperaturas mais altas aceleram a perda de qualidade, enquanto o armazenamento refrigerado, em condições ideais entre 4 e 5°C, retarda os processos de degradação, preservando a qualidade dos ovos por um período mais prolongado

title: TRANSITION OF BINDING FORCE IN CONTEMPORARY INTERNATIONAL LAW: OVERCOMING THE CLASSICAL SOURCES PARADIGM AND RECOGNIZING INDIRECT ENFORCEMENT MECHANISMS
abstract: The study departs from the classical theory of sources of international law to demonstrate that resolutions, declarations, and recommendations, although traditionally classified as soft law, can acquire normative force. It aims to analyze their capacity to produce legal effects through indirect enforcement mechanisms. A qualitative method is adopted, with a structuralist and deductive approach. The results indicate that such instruments influence the formation of custom, strengthen international accountability, and expand normative effectiveness in complex global contexts, requiring a reformulation of the traditional concept of normativity. Finally, it is considered that recognizing the legal force of these instruments contributes to the legitimacy, effectiveness, and adaptability of international law in the face of contemporary challenges.

title: Rethinking Sparsity: Provable Guarantees and Adaptive Optimization for High-Dimensional AI Models
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of training high-dimensional AI models in scenarios where data is scarce and computational resources are limited. We introduce a novel framework for leveraging sparsity in model parameters, focusing on both theoretical guarantees and practical adaptive optimization techniques. We present provable convergence bounds for sparse learning algorithms under various data distributions, including cases with heavy-tailed noise and adversarial corruption. Furthermore, we develop an adaptive optimization strategy that dynamically adjusts the sparsity level during training, balancing model complexity and generalization performance. Our empirical results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency compared to traditional dense models and existing sparse learning methods. We explore the implications of our findings for various AI applications, including image recognition, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning.

title: Implicit Regularization in Adaptive Gradient Methods: A Latent Force for Generalization
abstract: Adaptive gradient methods (AGMs) such as Adam, RMSprop, and Adagrad have become indispensable for training deep neural networks due to their efficiency and rapid convergence properties across a vast array of machine learning tasks. While their explicit regularization effects are seldom the primary focus, empirical evidence consistently suggests that these optimizers often contribute positively to the generalization capabilities of deep models. This paper delves into the intriguing phenomenon of implicit regularization inherent within AGMs, positing that their adaptive learning rate mechanisms function as a latent force actively promoting generalization. We propose that the curvature-aware parameter updates characteristic of AGMs implicitly regularize the model's parameter space. This regularization manifests by selectively dampening updates to parameters exhibiting high sensitivity or consistently large gradients, especially in the early stages of training, thereby preventing severe overfitting and guiding the optimization trajectory towards flatter, more robust minima. Through a combination of theoretical exposition and a review of existing empirical studies, we articulate how specific characteristics of adaptive learning rates, including their moment estimation and decay schedules, influence the effective strength of this implicit regularization and critically impact the generalization gap observed in practice. Our investigation aims to illuminate the complex interplay between the dynamics of optimization algorithms and the capacity for deep learning models to generalize well, offering valuable insights for the principled design and selection of optimization strategies to achieve more stable and generalizable deep learning models.

title: Local equations describe unreasonably efficient stochastic algorithms in random K-SAT
abstract: Despite significant advances in characterizing the highly nonconvex landscapes of constraint satisfaction problems, the good performance of certain algorithms in solving hard combinatorial optimization tasks remains poorly understood. This gap in understanding stems largely from the lack of theoretical tools for analyzing their out-of-equilibrium dynamics. To address this challenge, we develop a system of approximate master equations that capture the behavior of local search algorithms in constraint satisfaction problems. Our framework shows excellent qualitative agreement with the phase diagrams of two paradigmatic algorithms: Focused Metropolis Search (FMS) and greedy-WalkSAT (G-WalkSAT) for random 3-SAT. The equations not only confirm the numerical observation that G-WalkSAT’s algorithmic threshold is nearly parameter-independent but also successfully predict FMS’s threshold beyond the clustering transition. We also exploit these equations in a decimation scheme, demonstrating that the computed marginals encode valuable information about the local structure of the solution space explored by stochastic algorithms. Notably, our decimation approach achieves a threshold that surpasses the clustering transition, outperforming conventional methods like Belief Propagation-guided decimation. These results challenge the prevailing assumption that long-range correlations are always necessary to describe efficient local search dynamics and open a path to designing efficient algorithms to solve combinatorial optimization problems.

Electro-olfactory and behavioral responses of grass carp, bighead carp, silver carp, and black carp to chemical stimuli in laboratory exposures
abstract: Using juvenile individuals of four species of carp (Family: Cyprinidae), we tested the potential for two amino acids and one commercial bait stimulus to elicit an extracellular electro-olfactory response within the naris using gelatin-based electrodes. The amino acids alanine and lysine were tested on grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella), bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis), silver carp (H. molitrix) and black carp (Mylopharyngodon piceus) to provide a comparison among compounds both within and among species. Each row in the electro-olfactogram (EOG) data set represents exposure to a single stimulant in a single fish. Each individual fish was exposed to all three stimulus solutions sequentially in a random order, representing a trial; each individual was a subject for exactly one trial. The response metric was the measured response peak, in millivolts, corrected by subtracting the mean baseline during exposure to well water 60 seconds prior to the stimulant response. The baseline-corrected, absolute value of the response to ultrapure, deionized (UDI or Nanopure) water immediately preceding and following a trial is also included. Other relevant factors that could influence measured individual response, such as nominal concentration of stimulants, fish mass, holding tank temperature, and flow rate of water and solutions over the naris are included. Identifying data, namely date of trial and an individual subject ID (equivalent to a trial ID), are also included. Expanding on the EOG study, we conducted behavior trials on the same four species of invasive carp in a laboratory setting between the dates of 07 July 2024 to 06 November 2024. The feeding stimulant and amino acids alanine and lysine were again used, as well as a fish food solution, to analyze how exposure may impact fish behavior, with a specific focus on avoidance and attraction. Each trial involved two individuals of the same species being exposed to one of the stimulant solutions and well water in a long exposure chamber which drained in the center to maintain a delineation between amino acid and the control water. For each combination of species (4 total) and compound solution (4 total), we performed 10 replicates, totaling 160 trials with each trial utilizing two fish (320 individuals). The tank and fish were recorded from overhead video cameras and fish movement and position within the tank determined using tracking software. After the software provided the initial tracking analysis, additional manual tracking was done to address any errors that occurred due to fish overlap. Data reported includes cumulative duration in percent of time spent on either side of the tank that would help indicate either attractant or avoidance behavior. Other relevant factors such as water temperatures of holding tanks, temperatures of the behavior tank before and after trials and individual fish length and mass were also included.

title: Impact of Saccharomyces Cerevisiae and/or Its Cell Wall Supplementation in Dairy Cow Diet on Passive Immunity Transfer in their Calves
abstract: Abstract: Early detection of failed transfer of passive immunity (FTPI) is crucial to prevent neonatal diseases and mortality. This study evaluates the effect of supplementing dairy cows with Saccharomyces Cerevisiae and/or a yeast wall during the last month of pregnancy on the transfer of passive immunity to calves. Forty-five Montbeliarde dairy cows were divided into four groups: a control group (CON; n=13) with no supplementation, an SC group (n=12) receiving 5 g/day of S. Cerevisiae yeast, a YW group (n=10) receiving 5 g/day of yeast wall (20% mannans, 20% β-glucans), and an SCYW group (n=10) receiving a combination of 5 g SC and 5 g YW. At calving, colostrum and blood samples were collected to measure calf serum IgG concentration using radial immunodiffusion (RID) and compare results with the %Brix refractometer. A one-way ANOVA assessed the effects of supplementation type, colostrum quality, and calf sex. A Spearman correlation test evaluated the %Brix refractometer as an indirect tool for IgG estimation. Results showed a significant improvement in passive immunity transfer with supplementation (P<0.001), particularly in the SC and SCYW groups (P<0.01). Colostrum quality had a significant effect, whereas calf sex had no impact. A positive correlation (r=0.536) was observed between RID and %Brix. In conclusion, supplementing dairy cows with yeast during the last month of pregnancy enhances passive immunity transfer. The %Brix refractometer is a viable alternative to RID for estimating serum IgG concentration and detecting FTPI cases. Keywords: Dairy cows; Supplementation; FTPI; Immunoglobulin; RID.

title: Effect of Dietary Supplementation with Nano-Hydroxyapatite in Pregnant Goats on Obstetrical Outcomes: Parturition, Placental Shedding, Postpartum Disorders, Uterine Involution, and Milk and Offspring Production
Impact of Timing for In-Ovo Injection of Nano Zinc Oxide and Lactobacillus plantarum on Hatchability and Viability in Ross 308 Broilers
abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of injecting hatching eggs with zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) and the probiotic bacterium Lactobacillus plantarum (L. plantarum) at two incubation periods (day 10 and 18 of incubation) on certain hatching traits and viability of hatched chicks of Ross 308 broilers. A total of 900 fertilized eggs were used, evenly distributed between the two injection periods (450 eggs each). Six treatments were applied for each period, including: negative control (no injection), positive control (injection of 0.2 mL physiological saline into the amniotic fluid), injection of ZnO NPs at 20 or 25 µg/egg, and injection of L. plantarum at a dose of 10 5 or 10 7 CFU/egg. The results showed that injections on day 10, particularly with L. plantarum, significantly (P≤0.01) reduced hatchability and healthy chick rates, and increased embryonic mortality. In contrast, injection treatments on day 18 showed no negative effects. An increased percentage of pipped embryos was recorded in the group injected with L. plantarum at 10 7 CFU/egg in both periods, while no significant differences were found in chick deformities among treatments. The ZnO NPs injection treatments (20 and 25 µg/egg) showed significant improvement in chick body weight and relative weight, with no differences between the two injection timings for these traits. The results of the current study show that the timing of hatching egg injection significantly affects the hatchability, hatched chick vitality, and embryonic mortality. Injection on day 10 of incubation had a negative effect compared to day 18. On the other hand, injection of both concentrations of zinc oxide nanoparticles (20 and 25 µg/egg) had a positive effect in improving the hatching weight of chicks without having a negative effect on hatchability rates. In contrast, injection of L. plantarum bacteria on day 10 of incubation had a negative effect on hatchability and chick vitality, unlike injection on day 18 of incubation, which achieved better results in the aforementioned traits. Based on the above results, it is clear that the best day for injection is day 18 of incubation, and injection of L. plantarum bacteria, especially in the early stages of incubation, leads to a decrease in hatchability and chick vitality while increasing the percentage of embryo mortality.

title: Gradient-Coherent Adaptive Batching for Accelerated and Stable Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning optimization often grapples with the intricate interplay between batch size, convergence speed, and model stability. While larger batch sizes offer computational efficiency and smoother gradient estimates, they can lead to poorer generalization and a tendency to converge to flatter, less optimal minima. Conversely, smaller batches introduce higher variance into gradient estimates, potentially hindering convergence speed but often yielding better generalization. This paper introduces Gradient-Coherent Adaptive Batching (GCAB), a novel optimization strategy that dynamically adjusts the mini-batch size during training based on a measure of gradient coherence. By assessing the consistency and informativeness of gradients, GCAB aims to maintain an optimal balance: employing larger batches when gradients are stable and consistent to accelerate training, and reducing batch sizes when gradients become noisy or divergent to enhance stability and improve generalization. Our methodology defines gradient coherence through a combination of gradient variance and directional consistency across sub-batches. We propose an algorithmic framework that integrates this coherence metric with a feedback loop to adaptively tune the batch size. Through extensive theoretical exposition and anticipated experimental validation across various deep learning architectures and tasks, including image classification and natural language processing, GCAB is shown to significantly accelerate training convergence while simultaneously improving model stability and generalization performance compared to fixed-batch approaches and other adaptive batching schemes. This work provides a principled mechanism for navigating the batch size dilemma, offering a robust and efficient optimization paradigm for complex deep neural networks.

title: The CL5D Hybrid Model: A Dynamic Systems Approach to High-Fidelity CRISPR-Cas9 Off-Target Prediction via Conjugate Balance Analysis
abstract: A dynamic systems-based computational model (CL5D Hybrid Model) for predicting CRISPR-Cas9 off-target activity. The framework employs agent-based simulation, phase analysis, and conjugate balance scoring to evaluate editing fidelity beyond static sequence homology. This repository includes the full methodological description and supplementary comparative analysis of ZNF423 and EMX1 target sites.

title: Hierarchical Grover's Algorithm $\textbf{(HGA)}$: A Structural Optimization for Near-Constant Time Search
abstract: The fundamental challenge in achieving true quantum-speedup lies in overcoming the sequential dependence required by probability laws in algorithms such as Grover’s Algorithm (GA) [2]. While GA provides a quadratic advantage with O(√N ) complexity for unstructured search spaces of size N , the underlying O(√N) iteration loop still constitutes a time constraint. The question of whether such problems, rooted in the NP-Complete class [1], can be solved in polynomial time remains open, but the structural flaw is clear: the sequential nature of search. We propose the Hierarchical Grover’s Algorithm (HGA), a two-layer structural optimization designed to convert the full O(√N) probabilistic search into a focused, low-complexity re-application. HGA leverages a partial, low-fidelity run (GA-L1) to cluster the solution space, followed by an immediate, highly-efficient second run (GA-L2) on the narrowed subset. This approach aims to dramatically reduce the effective search time complexity to O(k + √N ′), where N ′ ≪ N , pushing practical quantum search into the near-constant time domain.

title: Adaptive Probability Horizon: Top-k Sampling for Controllable Generative Models
abstract: Generative models, particularly large language models, have shown remarkable capabilities in producing diverse and coherent content. However, controlling the output characteristics, such as style, topic, or specific attributes, remains a significant challenge. Traditional sampling methods like greedy decoding, beam search, top-k, and nucleus sampling often struggle to balance output quality, diversity, and adherence to control signals. This paper introduces the Adaptive Probability Horizon (APH), a novel dynamic top-k sampling strategy designed to enhance the controllability of generative models. APH adaptively adjusts the 'k' parameter based on the evolving probability distribution and external control signals, allowing for finer-grained guidance of the generation process. By dynamically re-evaluating the set of permissible tokens at each generation step, APH can narrow or expand the sampling space to maintain coherence with a desired attribute or to explore diverse options when less constrained. Our methodology formally defines the APH algorithm, detailing its integration with transformer-based architectures and its application in various controlled generation tasks. Through empirical evaluation, we demonstrate that APH significantly improves the ability to steer generation towards specific objectives while preserving output quality and reducing instances of unwanted topic shifts or stylistic inconsistencies. The proposed method represents a crucial step towards more reliable and user-guided generative AI systems.

title: Weight Decay as Inductive Bias: Unifying Regularization and Optimization Dynamics
abstract: Weight decay is a ubiquitous regularization technique in machine learning, particularly deep learning, traditionally understood as an $L_2$ penalty on model weights. This paper re-examines weight decay not merely as a static regularization term but as a dynamic inductive bias that profoundly shapes the optimization landscape and trajectories of neural networks. We propose a unifying perspective where weight decay's influence extends beyond simply penalizing large weights to actively guiding the optimizer towards specific regions of the loss landscape characterized by properties conducive to generalization, such as flatter minima or low-rank weight matrices. Through a comprehensive review of classical and modern interpretations, we elucidate how weight decay interacts with various optimization algorithms, including Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) and adaptive methods like Adam, to steer the learning process. We present theoretical arguments and empirical observations that demonstrate its role in promoting simpler models, enhancing training stability, and mitigating overfitting across diverse architectures and training regimes. The paper synthesizes insights from implicit regularization, loss landscape geometry, and optimization theory to establish a robust framework for understanding weight decay's multifaceted impact. Our findings suggest that weight decay functions as a powerful inductive bias, dictating the properties of learned representations and ultimately improving generalization performance by modulating the effective capacity and exploration dynamics of the model.

title: Beyond $varepsilon$-Greedy: Optimizing Exploration in Q-Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Bayesian Regret Minimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to optimizing exploration in Q-learning, moving beyond the limitations of traditional $varepsilon$-greedy strategies. Our method integrates intrinsic motivation, specifically curiosity-driven exploration, with Bayesian regret minimization techniques. We hypothesize that by incentivizing the agent to explore uncertain states and actions, and by quantifying and minimizing the Bayesian regret associated with suboptimal choices, we can significantly improve the learning efficiency and asymptotic performance of Q-learning algorithms. The proposed framework dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation trade-off based on the agent's current knowledge state and uncertainty about the environment. We present a detailed mathematical formulation of our approach, including the definition of an intrinsic reward signal based on prediction error and the derivation of a Bayesian regret bound for Q-learning. Empirical evaluations on a suite of challenging reinforcement learning benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms $varepsilon$-greedy and other state-of-the-art exploration strategies, achieving faster convergence, higher average rewards, and improved robustness to environmental stochasticity. These results highlight the potential of combining intrinsic motivation and Bayesian decision theory to address the exploration-exploitation dilemma in reinforcement learning.

title: Denoising Diffusion Policy Gradients for Sample-Efficient Control
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, yet challenges related to sample efficiency remain a critical bottleneck, especially in complex continuous control tasks. Traditional policy gradient methods often require extensive interaction with the environment, which can be prohibitively expensive or time-consuming in real-world applications. Concurrently, denoising diffusion models have emerged as powerful generative models, demonstrating exceptional capabilities in synthesizing high-quality data across diverse modalities. This paper introduces Denoising Diffusion Policy Gradients (DDPG), a novel framework that integrates the expressive power of conditional diffusion models directly into online policy optimization for sample-efficient control. DDPG leverages diffusion models to implicitly represent complex, potentially multi-modal, action distributions. By formulating policy gradients that backpropagate through the denoising process, DDPG aims to enhance exploration, improve the stability of policy updates, and significantly reduce the number of environmental interactions required for learning optimal policies. We detail the theoretical underpinnings of this integration, propose mechanisms for efficient gradient computation, and outline architectural considerations. Through extensive empirical evaluations on continuous control benchmarks, we demonstrate that DDPG outperforms existing state-of-the-art policy gradient methods in terms of sample efficiency and achieves comparable or superior final performance, thereby offering a promising avenue for addressing critical challenges in practical RL deployments.

title: Beyond Gradients: Higher-Order Calculus for Sample-Efficient AI Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of higher-order calculus, specifically second and potentially third-order derivatives, to enhance the sample efficiency of artificial intelligence (AI) optimization algorithms. Traditional gradient-based methods, while powerful, often suffer from slow convergence or require extensive data, especially in non-convex landscapes or when dealing with complex models and limited interaction budgets. By incorporating information about curvature and Hessian matrices, higher-order optimization techniques offer the potential for more informed step directions, faster convergence, and improved generalization with fewer data samples or environment interactions. We delve into the theoretical underpinnings, practical challenges such as computational cost and memory requirements, and potential solutions like Hessian-vector products and approximation schemes. Through a comprehensive review of existing literature and a proposed methodological framework, we demonstrate how these advanced mathematical tools can unlock new frontiers in AI, particularly in domains demanding high sample efficiency like reinforcement learning, meta-learning, and scenarios with intrinsically limited data. The discussion highlights the trade-offs involved and outlines promising avenues for future research to overcome current limitations and fully leverage the power of higher-order information.

title: Functional Analysis of Phenotypic Trait Spaces: A Banach Space Approach to Evolutionary Theory
abstract: This theoretical paper introduces a novel mathematical framework for evolutionary biology by applying concepts from functional analysis to model continuous phenotypic traits. Moving beyond the traditional finite-dimensional vector spaces of quantitative genetics, the work proposes that traits such as growth curves, morphological shapes, and other function-valued phenotypes are more naturally described as elements of infinite-dimensional Banach and Hilbert spaces (e.g., L2L2 and Sobolev spaces). The core of the framework models the phenotypic covariance structure as a compact, self-adjoint operator. A central mathematical result proves that under standard biological assumptions, this operator is compact, allowing for a spectral decomposition. This decomposition identifies orthogonal "evolutionary modes" (eigenfunctions) ranked by their associated variance or "evolvability" (eigenvalues). The rate of decay of these eigenvalues formally quantifies the strength of developmental constraints and the effective dimensionality of the accessible phenotypic space.

title: Distributional AI: A Unified Framework for Uncertainty Quantification and Robust Decision-Making
abstract: Traditional Artificial Intelligence (AI) models often focus on point predictions, providing a single best estimate for a given input without explicitly quantifying the inherent uncertainty in their predictions. This limitation significantly hinders their applicability in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems, where understanding "how sure" a model is and how it might perform under unforeseen circumstances is paramount. This paper introduces Distributional AI, a unified framework designed to address this critical gap by explicitly modeling and predicting the full probability distribution of outcomes, rather than merely point estimates. By embracing a distributional perspective, our framework enables comprehensive uncertainty quantification, offering calibrated prediction intervals and capturing various sources of uncertainty, including epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. Furthermore, this distributional understanding forms the bedrock for robust decision-making. We demonstrate how integrating risk measures, robust optimization techniques, and worst-case scenario analysis within the distributional paradigm can lead to AI systems that are less susceptible to adversarial attacks, data shifts, and out-of-distribution inputs, thereby improving reliability and trustworthiness. The proposed framework provides a coherent theoretical and practical approach for developing AI systems that are not only accurate but also transparent about their limitations and resilient in challenging environments. We present a detailed exposition of the underlying mathematical principles, algorithmic formulations, and potential applications, illustrating how Distributional AI represents a significant advancement towards building more responsible and dependable intelligent agents.

title: Structure-Induced Cosmology: A Minimal Structural Framework for Time and Diversity
abstract: This work proposes a minimal structural framework in which time is not assumed as a prior coordinate, but emerges as an accumulated effect of structural fluctuations. A scalar quantity F defined as the square root of effective energy density generates a natural expression of time:t = F^2/2This expression is interpreted as a post–condensation relation of structural stabilization. A minimal action formulation based on a scalar field is provided, yielding dynamical equations consistent with the intuitive notion: fluctuations → damping → stabilization → diversity. The framework is not intended to replace existing cosmology, but to provide a structural viewpoint that connects physical evolution with emergent patterns of complexity.

title: Beyond Optimality: Risk-Sensitive Bellman Equations for Robust Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) that moves beyond traditional optimality by incorporating risk sensitivity into the Bellman equation. Traditional RL methods often focus on maximizing expected returns, which can lead to suboptimal or even dangerous behavior in environments with high uncertainty or potential for catastrophic outcomes. Our proposed framework, Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning (RSRL), addresses this limitation by allowing agents to explicitly model and manage risk preferences. We formulate a risk-sensitive Bellman equation that incorporates a risk parameter, enabling the agent to adjust its policy based on its aversion or affinity for risk. We explore different risk measures, including entropic risk and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), and derive corresponding update rules for policy optimization. Furthermore, we present a theoretical analysis of the convergence properties of RSRL and demonstrate its effectiveness through empirical evaluations on benchmark RL tasks. The results show that RSRL outperforms traditional RL algorithms in environments with high uncertainty or potential for large negative rewards, achieving more robust and reliable performance. We also investigate the trade-off between risk and reward, providing insights into how to choose the appropriate risk parameter for different applications.

title: "Approximation Algorithm for Minimum Weight $(2,m)$-Connected Dominating Set"
abstract: "Using a connected dominating set (CDS) as a virtual backbone of a wireless sensor network can effectively save energy, reduce interference, and extend network lifespan, which also has wide applications in geometric routing algorithms and network topology control. A fault-tolerant virtual backbone can be modeled as a $k$-connected $m$-dominating set (abbreviated as a $(k,m)$-CDS) in a graph. In this paper, we present an approximation algorithm for the minimum weight $(2,m)$-CDS problem in a general graph, which achieves approximation ratio at most $5.164H(n-1)$, where $H(\\gamma)=\\sum_{i=1}^{\\gamma}1\/i$ is the $\\gamma$th Harmonic number and $n$ is the number of nodes in the graph. This ratio improves previously best known ratio by a factor of at least $3.87$."

title: Optimal Control Theory for Deep Learning Dynamics and Generalization
abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success across diverse domains, yet a comprehensive theoretical understanding of its underlying mechanisms, particularly regarding optimization dynamics and generalization capabilities, remains a significant challenge. This paper explores optimal control theory as a powerful and unifying framework for analyzing and understanding deep neural networks. We propose viewing deep neural networks as discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems, where information propagates through layers, and the training process, driven by optimization algorithms, is recast as an optimal control problem. This perspective allows for a rigorous analysis of how network parameters evolve over time, the impact of learning rates, and the role of various regularization techniques. By formulating the training objective as a cost function to be minimized by a controller (the optimizer), we can leverage established tools from control theory to investigate convergence, stability, and robustness. Furthermore, we delve into how optimal control principles can shed light on the elusive generalization properties of deep networks, including the phenomenon of implicit regularization and the non-overfitting puzzle in overparameterized models. We discuss how studying the stochastic dynamics of optimization algorithms within this framework can reveal insights into how networks find solutions that generalize well to unseen data. This theoretical alignment provides a principled avenue for hyper-parameter tuning and extending deep learning theory to complex scenarios like Bayesian learning, adversarial training, and meta-learning, thus offering a deeper, more systematic understanding of deep learning's efficacy.

Time is Money: The Role of Reallocation Speed Under Capital Constraints
abstract: Capital-constrained businesses often decide between supporting additional blockchains or maintaining higher liquidity for their protocols across existing blockchains. This paper develops a general model to quantify how the speed and cost of cross-chain capital allocation affect capital efficiency gains. We introduce a conservative estimate for per-period gains that can be constructed with two inputs: the cost differential between reallocation options and the incremental revenue unlocked by faster allocation at potentially less capital. Under this model, businesses obtain capital efficiency gains when the value of newly accessible opportunities from faster cross-chain speeds outweighs the additional costs of reallocation.

title: Development of an Ex Vivo Osteochondral Biomimetic Platform for Mechanistic Investigation of Cartilage Regeneration
abstract: Articular cartilage possesses limited intrinsic healing capacity due to its avascular and aneural nature, posing a significant challenge for treating focal chondral defects. While regenerative strategies employing biomaterials and stem cells have progressed, their mechanistic evaluation is hindered by the lack of physiologically relevant in vitro models. This study aimed to establish and characterize a human ex vivo osteochondral explant model to assess cellular and extracellular matrix responses to cartilage repair strategies. Osteochondral explants (10 mm diameter, n = 61) were harvested from femoral condyles of patients undergoing knee arthroplasty. Standardized full-thickness chondral defects (4 mm) were created and assigned to six treatment groups: native control, untreated defect, fibrin glue, collagen type I hydrogel (ChondroFiller®), fibrin glue + MSCs, and ChondroFiller® + MSCs. Explants were cultured for 7, 14, or 21 days, followed by metabolic, biochemical, and histological assessments. Explants remained viable for 21 days. Notably, the ChondroFiller® group showed a 2.4-fold increase in DNA content by day 14, while MSC-treated groups enhanced collagen deposition and GAG production. Significant correlations between DNA and collagen levels were observed in scaffold-based treatments. This ex vivo model offers a reproducible and translational platform to investigate cartilage regeneration with temporal resolution, supporting preclinical testing of emerging therapeutic approaches.

title: Method Development And Validation For The Estimation Of Ritonavir And Nirmatrelvir In Pharmaceutical Dosage Form By RP-HPLC
abstract: Aim and Objectives: The present study aimed to develop and validate a simple, precise, and accurate Reverse Phase–High Performance Liquid Chromatographic (RP-HPLC) method for the simultaneous estimation of Ritonavir (RTV) and Nirmatrelvir (NMV) in bulk and tablet dosage forms as per ICH Q2(R2) guidelines. Background: Ritonavir, an HIV protease inhibitor, and Nirmatrelvir, a SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibitor, are co-formulated as antiviral agents for COVID-19 therapy. A reliable analytical method is essential for routine quality control and dosage form evaluation. Materials and Methods: Chromatographic separation was achieved on a Shimadzu Shim-pack C8 column (4.6 × 250 mm, 5 μm) using acetonitrile and water (70:30 v/v) as the mobile phase at a flow rate of 1.0 ml/min. Detection was carried out at 239 nm for Ritonavir and 228 nm for Nirmatrelvir. The developed method was validated for linearity, accuracy, precision, robustness, limit of detection (LOD), and limit of quantitation (LOQ) as per ICH guidelines. Results: The retention times for RTV and NMV were 3.14 and 4.97 min, respectively. Linearity was observed in the range of 10–60 µg/ml for RTV and 10–50 µg/ml for NMV, with correlation coefficients of 0.9997 and 0.997. LOD/LOQ values were 0.141/0.427 µg/ml for RTV and 0.098/0.297 µg/ml for NMV. The %RSD values for accuracy and precision were within acceptable limits. Conclusion: The developed RP-HPLC method is simple, robust, and reproducible, making it suitable for routine quality control of combined antiviral formulations containing Ritonavir and Nirmatrelvir.

abstract: Abstract Deep brain stimulation is an effective method for Parkinson's patients with poor drug treatment outcomes. During the surgery, the presence of friction can cause deviations between the implanted target and the preoperative planned position. In order to effectively reduce the friction during the puncture process, this article attempts to combine vibration-assisted and surface microtexture techniques in the process of brain implantation. The results showed that without immersion in artificial cerebrospinal fluid, textured needles with a spacing of 0.1mm exhibited an average friction reduction of 14% under axial vibration assistance, while when immersed in cerebrospinal fluid, textured needles with a spacing of 0.1mm and 0.3mm exhibited 26% and 16% friction reduction characteristics under axial vibration assistance, respectively.

The Effect of Tube Current Variations on Cranium Radiograph Images Using the MATLAB Program
abstract: Matrix Laboratory (MATLAB) is a software based on matrices, which is easy to use for solving various mathematical and computing problems. This study aimed to determine how variations in tube current (mA) affect the radiographic image of the cranium using the MATLAB program and to assess the program's quantification of this effect. The sample in this study consisted of 3 volunteers who performed AP projection cranial radiography examinations with varying tube current at Pelamonia TK. II Hospital, Makassar. Each sample had the same treatment in patient preparation, examination position, examination projection, and the same exposure factor value, which differed only in the use of tube current values, ​​where the volunteer 1 with 200 mA, the volunteer 2 with 250 mA and volunteer 3 with 320 mA. Measurement of the quality of the AP projection cranium image with tube current of 200 mA, the percentage was 96.11%. At 250 mA, the percentage was 95.00%; at 320 mA, it dropped to 92.78%. It was determined that the optimal tube current variation was 200 mA with the highest percentage in measuring the image quality (density, contrast, sharpness, and detail) of the AP projection Cranium against variations in tube current is almost perfect.
