title: The Book of Poida: An Unhinged Australian Bible of Folk Heroes, Ferals, and Cultural Chaos
abstract: The Book of Poida is a deliberately chaotic, culturally forensic anthology that reframes Australian comedic folklore as a mythological canon. Blending satire, mock-scripture, absurdist narrative, and deep-cut references to Australian media history, the work elevates figures such as Poida, Agro, Dame Edna, Con the Fruiterer, Russell Coight, Chopper Read, SkitHOUSE characters, John Safran, and other icons of Australian cultural disorder into a unified mythic universe. This text fuses high-energy irreverence with structural parody, building a metafictional “Australian Codex” that sits somewhere between religious scripture, stand-up comedy, and national ethnography. While humorous in tone, the work is a sincere and coherent cultural artifact, preserving, exaggerating, and celebrating the peculiar forms of satire, chaos, and character-driven storytelling that define Australia’s comedic tradition.Version 1 constitutes the initial collected canon; subsequent versions may expand the universe into a full apocrypha.

title: Theology of Pluralism in Historical Context: Cultural Encounters of Religions in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates religious diversity in Indonesia within a historical context, legal contradictions, and cultural acculturation which build the groundwork of living theology. Long-running contacts since the Hindu-Buddhist era, the arrival of Islam via trade and cultural infiltration, help to define Indonesian pluralism. It did not suddenly happen. preaching, Christian colonialism with contemporary education, and the dynamics of Reformasi and independence. Every stage provided particular types of engagement that together created a plurarity only found in the archipelago. The results of this study highlight contradictions at the current level: According to the Religious Harmony Index, interreligious peace is rather strong yet worldwide Studies confirm the high frequency of strict rules and social conflicts. This paradox implies that the state acts both as shield and restrictor, whereas society keeps social cohesiveness by cultural means. Maintaining pluralism has been shown to hinge mostly on cultural acculturation. Slametan, sekaten, yadnya, pela gandong, and grebeg Syawal show that pluralism is practiced daily rather than just founded on dogma or law. The hybridity hypothesis of Homi K. Bhabha helps to clarify that this cultural environment is a "third space" in which identities are negotiated and theological pluralism is formed. Therefore, this study provides a significant theoretical contribution: Indonesian pluralism is a living theology arising from historical negotiation, regulatory contradictions, and cultural conventions. Because this study relies on literature review, ethnographic field research is advised to further investigate the practice of pluralism at the community level. These results are intended to enrich the world dialogue by presenting a culturally grounded model of pluralism as an alternative amid the global crisis of bigotry.

title: The Hei metaphor: An emerging conceptualisation of research from Solomon Islands
abstract: Western research paradigms have dominated the area of educational research. Recently, Indigenous research paradigms have emerged to help Pacific scholars in their research activities. The dominance of Western research paradigms can be a problem for understanding indigenous cultures because communities perceive the world differently. The benefit for Pacific Indigenous researchers is to conceptualise concepts and metaphors that capture the relevance of what they are doing or studying as part of their communities. There are some existing Pacific research analytical frameworks such as the Kakala research framework from Tonga or the Fijian Vanua research framework. The purpose of this paper is to present an emerging Pacific research framework from the Solomon Islands context, the Hei concept. The Hei concept is useful as it relates the Western notion of research to the traditional Solomon Islands process of collecting and preparing the Canarium indicum nut (known as ngali nuts in Solomon Islands), which can be understood as a metaphor for the collaborative and collective approach to the collection and analysis of data in research. This metaphorical understanding of research provides a useful analytical framework for novice researchers from small island developing nation states (SIDNS) in the Pacific.

title: The Unhinged Gospel of Aussie Humour: A Modern Mythology of Australian Cultural Archetypes
abstract: The Unhinged Gospel of Aussie Humour unifies Australian comedic culture into a structured mythology, treating television chaos, suburban rituals, migrant energy, larrikin philosophy, and national folk heroes as a cohesive folkloric canon.Anchored by Poida—the prophet of deadpan nihilism—the work constructs a cultural theology built on anti-authoritarianism, sacred incompetence, and the elevation of the mundane.Through gospels, epistles, parables, and academic-style analysis, the text examines figures including Russell Coight, John Safran, Bud Tingwell, Paul Hogan, Steve Irwin, Nick Giannopoulos, Agro, Chopper Read, and Dame Edna, exploring how each represents archetypal Australian modes of humour, identity, and chaotic wisdom.Blending satire, anthropology, media studies, and mythopoeic analysis, this document proposes that Australian humour operates as an informal national religion—a worldview where the punchline is revelation and the yarn is sacrament.

title: Universal access to archaeological parks: a contested principle in the African context
abstract: Using the Salalah Guidelines for the Management of Public Archaeological Sites as a framework, this policy brief examines the conceptualisation of an archaeological park proposed by the International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS) to question its relevance in the African context. It focuses on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) World Heritage properties as designated areas which, while presenting particular challenges, are meant to represent examples of best practise in archaeological heritage management, to argue for the need to recognise other values of the sites, besides the Outstanding Universal Value (OUV), and consider the issues of access within the local cultural contexts of the rightsholders.

title: All the Colours of a Historic Facade: Dissonant Heritage Narratives about the Restoration of a Heritage Building in Multicultural Northern Istria
abstract: Heritage dissonances in contested territories are a challenge for the conservation of built heritage as they embody diverging values of the numerous communities. The restoration of the “Venetian House” in Piran (Slovenia) in 2016 provides an eloquent example through which we can also observe the impact of population changes on the dynamics of (mis)recognition in heritage and highlight the potential of participatory practice in such conservation.

title: Dealing with delay: the Kedgeree Road as a metaphor of speed in early colonial eastern India
Carving the Chimeric Mind: The Hohlenstein-Stadel Ivory and the Genesis of Therianthropic Cognition
abstract: Discovered in the Hohlenstein-Stadel cave in the Swabian Jura of southwestern Germany, the Löwenmensch or Lion-man figurine, carved from mammoth ivory and dated to approximately 40,000 years BP, stands as one of the most enigmatic and significant artifacts of the Upper Paleolithic. This therianthropic sculpture, combining the head of a cave lion with a bipedal human body, is the earliest known unambiguous representation of a being that does not exist in the natural world. This paper argues that the Löwenmensch is not merely a piece of prehistoric art but a crucial piece of evidence marking a fundamental cognitive leap in human evolution: the genesis of therianthropic cognition. We posit that its creation required a sophisticated level of abstract thought, symbolic representation, and what has been termed 'cognitive fluidity'—the ability to merge concepts from distinct mental domains. By examining the figurine's archaeological context, the technological investment in its production, and its unique iconography through the lens of cognitive archaeology, this paper explores the profound implications of the Löwenmensch for understanding the emergence of mythology, religion, and the complex symbolic systems that define modern human culture. The artifact is presented as a tangible manifestation of a 'chimeric mind', capable of intentionally conceiving and constructing new realities, a faculty that underpins the entirety of human spiritual and narrative traditions. The figurine's existence suggests that the foundations for modern consciousness and worldview-building were firmly in place during the Aurignacian period.

title: A VARIAÇÃO LINGUÍSTICA NO PORTUGUÊS BRASILEIRO: ENTRE A NORMA E O USO SOCIAL
abstract: A variação linguística constitui um fenômeno intrínseco à natureza da língua e reflete a diversidade social, cultural e histórica do Brasil. Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar o português brasileiro sob a perspectiva da variação linguística, destacando as relações entre a norma-padrão e o uso social efetivo nas diferentes regiões do país. A pesquisa, de caráter qualitativo e bibliográfico, fundamenta-se em estudos de autores que discutem os fatores históricos, geográficos e socioculturais responsáveis pela formação dos dialetos e falares regionais. Considera-se, nesse contexto, a influência dos processos migratórios, do contato entre línguas e das condições socioeconômicas na consolidação das variedades linguísticas brasileiras. Observa-se que as variações linguísticas não apenas expressam a heterogeneidade cultural nacional, mas também revelam tensões entre prestígio e estigmatização, associadas a fatores de classe, escolarização e identidade social. A análise proposta evidencia que o uso efetivo da língua ultrapassa os limites da norma-padrão, configurando-se como instrumento de afirmação cultural e de resistência simbólica. Assim, o estudo contribui para uma compreensão mais ampla da língua portuguesa como um sistema dinâmico, marcado por constantes processos de mudança, adaptação e reconstrução social. Conclui-se que reconhecer a variação linguística como componente essencial da língua implica valorizar a diversidade comunicativa do povo brasileiro e promover práticas educacionais mais inclusivas, que considerem o respeito às diferenças linguísticas como parte fundamental da formação cidadã e do ensino de língua materna.

title: Human-machine interactions, annotations and alignments in Cultural Heritage terminologies – Examples from the realm of conservation science
Echoes of Creation: A Comparative Geo-Spatial Analysis of Upper Paleolithic Cave Art Sanctuaries and the Dawn of Symbolic Thought
abstract: This paper explores the profound connection between Upper Paleolithic cave art sanctuaries and the evolution of symbolic thought in early humans. Through a comparative geo-spatial analysis of key cave art sites across Europe, including Lascaux, Chauvet, Altamira, and others, we investigate the spatial distribution, thematic content, and environmental contexts of these sites. Our analysis aims to identify patterns and correlations that shed light on the cognitive and cultural significance of cave art. We hypothesize that the selection of cave locations, the organization of artwork within the caves, and the depicted subjects reflect a complex system of symbolic representation and meaning-making. By integrating archaeological data, cognitive science theories, and spatial analysis techniques, we seek to understand how cave art served as a medium for communication, ritual, and the expression of early human cosmology, contributing to the development of abstract thought and cultural identity.

title: The Gospel of Light
abstract: Title: The Healing WayAuthor: Eric NeedhamVersion: 1.0 (First Release)License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Description:The Healing Way is a secular, mathematically grounded re-imagining of spirituality for the modern age. For further information about the ENSO Framework, please contact Eric Needham: ensotheory1@gmail.com

title: The Echo of Gog and Magog – Martin Buber’s Hasidic Literature as a Jewish Cosmopolitan Response to the Holocaust
abstract: Martin Buber’s novel Gog and Magog stands as a crucial yet seldom analysed literary response to the Holocaust, reflecting Buber’s engagement with Jewish cosmopolitanism and its ethical implications. This article examines the novel in relation to Buber’s Hasidic writings and his critique of the Enlightenment’s unfulfilled promises, arguing that he saw Hasidism as embodying a form of Jewish cosmopolitanism that transcended national borders. By portraying Napoleon as a political messianic figure, Gog and Magog engages with contemporary reality, including Zionist polices of the 1940s and 1950s, while advancing a theological-political vision that seeks to bridge divine and human love in the shadow of destruction. Despite the largely critical reception of this novel in Israel, Buber’s Jewish rooted cosmopolitanism remains a vital framework for understanding the interplay between particularism and universalism in the face of man-made catastrophe.

title: Chapter 5 Leprosy in the Kitāb al-Malakī and Its Mediterranean Tradition. Critical Editions and Translations
Re-Evaluating the Recent African Origin Model: Genomic Admixture and the Complex Tapestry of Modern Human Emergence
abstract: The recent African origin (RAO) model has long been the dominant paradigm in human evolution, positing that modern humans (Homo sapiens) evolved in Africa and subsequently dispersed, replacing archaic hominins in other parts of the world. However, accumulating genomic evidence reveals a more complex picture, highlighting the significant role of admixture between modern humans and archaic populations such as Neanderthals and Denisovans. This paper critically re-evaluates the RAO model in light of these findings. We examine the extent and implications of archaic admixture in modern human genomes, analyze the geographic distribution of archaic introgression, and discuss the functional consequences of introgressed genes. Furthermore, we explore alternative models that incorporate admixture as a key component of human evolution, considering the implications for understanding human diversity, adaptation, and disease susceptibility. This review synthesizes the latest genomic research to provide a nuanced understanding of the complex tapestry of modern human emergence, challenging the traditional view of a simple out-of-Africa replacement.

title: Sedentary Revolution, Monumental Agency: Reassessing Social Complexity in the Proto-Urban Levant and Anatolia
abstract: This paper examines the intertwined processes of sedentism, monumental construction, and the emergence of social complexity in the Proto-Urban Levant and Anatolia during the Neolithic and Chalcolithic periods. Traditional models often posit a linear progression from settled life to social hierarchies, with monumental architecture acting as a passive reflection of existing power structures. This study challenges such deterministic views, arguing instead for a dynamic interplay between sedentary lifeways, collective action in the creation of monumental structures, and the active negotiation of social identities and power relations. By analyzing archaeological evidence from key sites such as Çatalhöyük, Göbeklitepe, and Tell Halaf, we explore how the construction and use of monumental spaces both reflected and shaped emerging social complexities. Our analysis emphasizes the role of human agency in these transformations, highlighting the diverse ways in which individuals and communities actively participated in the creation of new social orders within the context of the Sedentary Revolution. The paper concludes by proposing a more nuanced understanding of proto-urban development, one that acknowledges the contingent and multi-directional nature of social change in the ancient Near East.

title: The Unfolding Maya State: Trajectories of Resilience, Rupture, and Reorganization from the Preclassic to Mayapan
abstract: This paper critically examines the concept of the "Maya state" through a diachronic analysis of political organization, societal resilience, periods of rupture, and subsequent reorganization across the Preclassic, Classic, and Postclassic periods, culminating in the case of Mayapan. Moving beyond monolithic interpretations of statehood, we explore the dynamic and often fragmented nature of Maya political entities, emphasizing their adaptive capacities in the face of environmental, social, and political pressures. By synthesizing archaeological, epigraphic, and iconographic evidence, the study traces the emergence of early complex societies in the Preclassic, the flourishing yet volatile city-states of the Classic period, the widespread ruptures associated with the Classic Maya collapse, and the subsequent diverse forms of political reorganization observed in the Postclassic, particularly exemplified by the regional state centered at Mayapan. We argue that Maya political structures, while distinct from Old World empires, demonstrate a persistent pattern of adaptation and innovation, characterized by both deep-seated resilience and transformative reorganizations in response to systemic stressors. This research contributes to a more nuanced understanding of non-Western state formation and the long-term trajectories of complex societies.

title: From Core to Corpse: Levallois Technology, Mortuary Behavior, and the Depth of Neanderthal Cognition
abstract: This paper investigates the cognitive capabilities of Neanderthals by examining two distinct yet interconnected archaeological markers: Levallois lithic technology and mortuary behavior. Levallois technology, characterized by its systematic preparation of a core to predetermine flake shape and size, demands significant foresight, planning, and abstract conceptualization. Concurrently, Neanderthal mortuary practices, ranging from simple interment to more complex arrangements, suggest a nuanced engagement with death that may transcend mere practical disposal, hinting at symbolic thought, empathy, or social cohesion. By synthesizing extensive archaeological evidence from key Middle Paleolithic sites across Eurasia, this study aims to establish the intricate relationship between technological sophistication and funerary rituals. We argue that the recurrent application of Levallois reduction sequences and the emerging patterns in Neanderthal mortuary contexts collectively demonstrate a depth of cognitive capacity previously underestimated, challenging the traditional view of Neanderthals as solely pragmatic toolmakers. The findings suggest a complex cognitive landscape, encompassing hierarchical planning, working memory, and potentially a burgeoning symbolic awareness, thereby contributing to a more complete understanding of Neanderthal humanity and its place in human evolutionary history.

title: Gerakan Sosial Muhammadiyah: Dari Teologi Al-Ma'un Menuju Transformasi Sosial Berkemajuan
abstract: Muhammadiyah, yang didirikan pada tahun 1912, telah menjadi salah satu gerakan sosial-keagamaan paling berpengaruh di Indonesia. Jauh melampaui sekadar organisasi keagamaan, Muhammadiyah telah memantapkan dirinya sebagai gerakan sosial modern yang berakar pada landasan teologis yang kokoh, yaitu Teologi Al-Ma’un. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis secara mendalam bagaimana Teologi Al-Ma’un menjadi basis ideologis dan motor penggerak bagi beragam aksi sosial-kemanusiaan Muhammadiyah. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dan studi literatur, penelitian ini mengkaji tiga aspek utama: pertama, nilai dan ajaran sosial-kemanusiaan yang terkandung dalam Teologi Al-Ma’un; kedua, bentuk dan model gerakan sosial yang diimplementasikan; dan ketiga, upaya revitalisasi gerakan dalam menghadapi tantangan kontemporer. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa Muhammadiyah berhasil menerjemahkan doktrin teologis menjadi praksis sosial yang sistematis, terorganisir, dan berkelanjutan melalui amal usaha di bidang kesehatan, pendidikan, ekonomi, dan penanggulangan bencana. Gerakan ini tidak hanya bersifat karitatif, tetapi juga transformatif, dengan tujuan akhir mewujudkan keadilan sosial struktural sebagai manifestasi dari spirit Islam Berkemajuan

title: Andean Cosmologies and Sociopolitical Transformation: A Comparative Analysis of Chavín, Moche, Nazca, Tiwanaku, and Wari Civilizations
abstract: This study examines the intricate relationship between cosmologies and sociopolitical transformations in five prominent Andean civilizations: Chavín, Moche, Nazca, Tiwanaku, and Wari. By analyzing archaeological evidence, iconographic representations, and ethnohistorical accounts, we investigate how each culture's unique worldview shaped its social organization, political structures, and economic systems. We argue that cosmological beliefs served as both a foundation for and a reflection of the evolving power dynamics within these societies. Through a comparative approach, we highlight the shared themes and divergent paths in the development of Andean civilization, emphasizing the dynamic interplay between ideology and material reality. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the complex factors that drove societal change in the pre-Columbian Andes and offers insights into the broader study of cultural evolution.

title: A case study of geoid modeling in Sulawesi and accuracy verification strategies for accommodating diverse MSL vertical datums
abstract: Abstract This study aims to introduce the geoid modeling process in Sulawesi and demonstrate the practical issues faced. There are limitations of terrestrial gravity surveys in Sulawesi due to its complex geography, so airborne gravity surveys were conducted from 2008 to 2019 through a collaboration between the Badan Informasi Geospasial (BIG), the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), and the National Chiao Tung University (NCTU) gravity research team. The airborne gravity data currently cover almost the entire land area of Indonesia. The geoid modeling process involved refining the EGM08-derived geoid heights by incorporating downward-continued airborne gravity data and RTM-derived geoid effects, and adjusting the geometric geoid heights to accommodate diverse mean sea levels used in different GPS/leveling datasets. The impacts of different global gravitational models (GGMs), such as EIGEN-6C4, GECO, XGM2019e, and SGG-UGM-2, on geoid modeling were examined, and it revealed that differences arise from the different datasets used in the development of the GGM. This study revealed that airborne gravity data can significantly improve the accuracy of the geoid, achieving an impressive accuracy of approximately 0.04 to 0.05 m. In addition, the compatibility issue between gravity data and GGM in geoid modeling is highlighted. The strategy to unify the vertical datum between different GPS/leveling datasets for the validation of gravimetric geoid model was discussed in detail. Once the corresponding geopotential is determined, the conversion between the global vertical datum and the local vertical datum can be achieved. Accurate geoid is critical for infrastructure development, land-use planning, and resource management and play an integral role in supporting sustainable development goals (SDGs) by providing accurate spatial referencing, ensuring precise mapping, and offering location-based services.

title: From Damascus to Sindh and Iberia: Reassessing Umayyad Imperialism Through Frontier Dynamics and Cross-Cultural Exchange
abstract: This paper re-evaluates the nature of Umayyad imperialism (661-750 CE) by examining its frontier dynamics and cross-cultural interactions across three distinct regions: Sindh, Iberia, and the Syro-Mesopotamian heartland. Traditional narratives often portray Umayyad expansion as a monolithic, religiously motivated conquest. However, a comparative analysis reveals a more nuanced picture characterized by pragmatic adaptation, diverse local alliances, and varying degrees of cultural exchange. By focusing on the specific challenges and opportunities presented by each frontier, this study demonstrates how Umayyad rule was shaped not only by directives from Damascus but also by the agency of local populations and the unique ecological and social conditions of each territory. Ultimately, the paper argues for a more decentralized understanding of Umayyad governance, emphasizing its flexibility and capacity for integrating diverse populations into its expanding empire through both coercion and cooperation. This approach challenges simplistic notions of Islamic imperialism and sheds new light on the complex interplay of power, culture, and environment in the early Islamic world.

title: A Universal Information-Geometric Operator for Particle Couplings, Dimensional Flow, and Cosmological Structure: The RTLI Master Law
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive synthesis of the Relational Threshold and Layered Index (RTLI) framework, showing how a single information-geometric operator can predict quantities across particle physics, dimensional flow, and cosmology without adjustable parameters. RTLI identifies a narrow coherence corridor, defined by structural bands extracted from SPARC galactic data, as the universal geometric template underlying electromagnetic coupling, electroweak mixing, Higgs-sector stability, neutrino mixing, and the evolution of the Hubble parameter. The operator links microscopic and cosmological scales through three structural ingredients: (1) band-dependent coherence strengths, (2) a universal renormalization factor fixed by the depth of recombination, and (3) spectral-dimension flow from quantum (2D) to geometric (3D) regimes. Within this unified description, the fine-structure constant, sin²θ_W, λ_H, CKM/PMNS hierarchies, and the 8% Hubble tension all appear as geometric outputs rather than empirical inputs. This paper consolidates the separate RTLI notes and results into a single, coherent master formulation. It emphasizes falsifiable predictions for H₀(z), neutrino observables, and structure-growth signals measurable by DESI, Euclid, JWST, and CMB-S4. The result is a structured, testable framework that connects particle couplings, dimensional flow, and cosmological expansion through a shared geometric mechanism.

title: Identity-Structured Mathematics: A Finite Foundation for Functional Physics Functional Physics and the Origin of Infinity
abstract: Identity-Structured Mathematics presents a minimal, finite foundation for physics built on typed, identity-bearing objects rather than idealized continua. The framework introduces a single substrate axiom (ISS-0) and a three-layer structure separating (1) finite physical configurations, (2) functional coarse-grainings, and (3) classical infinite mathematics viewed as a cocompletion. Two core theorems show that all standard infinite constructs—ℝ, ℕ, Hilbert spaces, Gaussian measures, thermodynamic limits—arise as entropic saturation limits of finite typed diagrams. This resolves the origin of infinity in physics and clarifies the boundary between ontology (what exists) and idealization (what is mathematically convenient). A worked example using the electromagnetic field in a finite cavity demonstrates how continuum QFT quantities (e.g., blackbody spectrum, Casimir force) emerge cleanly from the functional layer without invoking uncountable sets until the final limiting step. The framework provides a unified categorical picture compatible with lattice gauge theory, constructive QFT, causal sets, and physicists’ computational practice, while preserving the full power of classical mathematics. It offers a sharp, finite, and physically grounded alternative to traditional continuum-first approaches.

title: A Tentative View on Strings: How Does a Single String Reach Steady-State?
abstract: We propose a framework to describe the response of a single one-dimensional quantized string. The string's excitation states, corresponding to observable particles, are fully characterized by the response function y(t). This work establishes axioms, definitions, and theorems for string dynamics, providing a first-principles description of its steady-state behavior without relying on phenomenological fitting.

title: Quantum Communication, Quantum Networks, and Quantum Sensing
LRT Constraints on QFT: Deriving Fock Structure and Interpreting Renormalization from Logical Foundations
abstract: Logic Realism Theory (LRT) derives non-relativistic quantum mechanics from the claim that the Three Fundamental Laws of Logic are ontological constraints constitutive of physical distinguishability. This paper extends LRT to quantum field theory through a tiered derivation structure with explicit physical inputs at each level. We establish three principal results: (1) Fock space structure is derived from LRT axioms plus Lorentz invariance and locality; (2) the spin-statistics connection follows from Lorentz invariance and microcausality via the standard Pauli argument; (3) the uniqueness of complex QFT is established. The paper distinguishes derivations from interpretations. Cluster decomposition, vacuum uniqueness, and the spectral gap are physical inputs (Tier 4), not consequences of logical constraints. Renormalization is interpreted as 3FLL-restoration at UV scales, but this does not derive renormalization group equations. Four predictions and six strong falsifiers are identified.

title: The Observer Effect and Wave–Particle Duality in the S-field Framework
abstract: The Observer Effect and Wave–Particle Duality in the S-field Framework --- 1. The traditional wave–particle problem In standard quantum mechanics, physical entities appear to behave: • as waves in interference experiments; • as particles when measured or detected. This has led to the idea that observation itself changes reality, often formulated as: “measurement collapses the wavefunction”. However, this formulation leaves unresolved questions: • What qualifies as an observer? • Why should information acquisition alter physical law? • Where exactly does the transition occur? --- 2. S-field perspective: no wave, no particle as primitives In the S-field framework, neither “wave” nor “particle” is fundamental. At the base level, there exist only: • oscillatory S-field states; • phase, frequency, and orientation; • dynamic resonance patterns. Wave and particle are emergent regimes, not ontological categories. 3. Wave behavior: coherent phase evolution A system exhibits wave-like behavior when: • S-oscillations evolve coherently; • multiple phase paths remain phase-correlated; • no dominant resonance locking occurs. In this regime: • interference patterns arise naturally; • delocalization reflects phase superposition; • the system evolves as a distributed resonance structure. “Wave” behavior is therefore a manifestation of extended phase coherence. --- 4. Particle behavior: resonance locking Particle-like behavior emerges when: • the S-oscillatory ensemble undergoes strong phase locking; • coherence collapses into a dominant resonant configuration; • the system enters a stable 4D projection. Localization is not imposed externally — it is a self-organized resonance outcome. A “particle” is a stable, self-locked oscillatory ensemble. 5. What observation actually does Observation does not create reality and does not collapse a wavefunction. Instead, observation means: • physical interaction with an environment; • introduction of new S-field couplings; • modification of phase relations. This interaction typically: • reduces global phase coherence; • enforces resonance selection; • stabilizes a particular outcome. Thus, observation is not epistemic — it is dynamical. --- 6. Why which-path information destroys interference Interference disappears because: • phase correlations are disrupted; • alternative phase paths decohere; • the system is forced into locally stable resonance modes. Which-path information is not special — any interaction that breaks coherence removes interference. No observer consciousness is required. 7. Delayed-choice experiments In delayed-choice scenarios: • the system remains in a coherent oscillatory regime; • no definitive resonance locking occurs until interaction; • temporal ordering appears paradoxical only classically. In the S-field framework: • time itself emerges from phase ordering; • coherence preservation allows late-mode selection; • no retrocausality is involved. The outcome reflects final coherence conditions, not past knowledge. --- 8. No collapse, only regime transition There is no physical “collapse”. Instead, there is: • a transition from distributed coherence to localized resonance stability; • a change of dynamical regime; • emergence of macroscopic definiteness. Wave → particle transition is micro → macro coherence restructuring. 9. One-sentence synthesis > Wave–particle duality is not a duality of objects, but a duality of coherence regimes in the S-field. --- 10. Conceptual closure This interpretation: • removes observer-dependence; • preserves realism; • unifies wave and particle behavior dynamically; • aligns quantum phenomena with micro–macro transition theory. title: Reinterpreting the Michelson-Morley Null Result: From "Material Aether" to "Vacuum Energy Density" – A Physical Necessity in the Quantum Era Author: Barbu, Ilie (Independent Researcher) Date: December 4, 2025
abstract: ABSTRACT The Michelson-Morley experiment (1887) is traditionally considered the cornerstone that disproved the existence of the "aether," leading to the elimination of any physical propagation medium for light in modern physics. This paper argues that this conclusion is a logical and historical error, based on a limited definition of the aether as a stationary, viscous, material fluid. We demonstrate that while the experiment correctly invalidated the Newtonian "aether wind" model, it did not invalidate the existence of a background medium. By integrating discoveries from Quantum Mechanics (Zero Point Energy) and General Relativity, we propose that the vacuum is not empty space, but a dense physical medium (\rho_{vac}) behaving as a superfluid. We argue that vacuum impedance (Z_0) and the speed of light (c) are elastic properties of this medium, rehabilitating the necessity of a physical substrate for electromagnetic wave propagation. 1. INTRODUCTION: THE DOGMA OF EMPTY SPACE For over a century, standard physics has operated under the premise that light propagates through "nothing." This belief stems from the interpretation of the null result of the Michelson-Morley interferometer, which failed to detect the Earth's motion through a stationary aether. However, this elimination of the medium has created major conceptual paradoxes in modern physics: Wave-Particle Duality: How can a wave (oscillation) exist without something to oscillate? Vacuum Constants: How can "nothingness" possess measurable, precise, and finite physical properties, such as electric permittivity (\varepsilon_0) and magnetic permeability (\mu_0)? This paper proposes that science has "thrown the baby out with the bathwater." The rejection of the 19th-century mechanical aether should not have led to the rejection of the concept of a fundamental medium entirely. 2. THE HISTORICAL ERROR: WHAT WAS MICHELSON ACTUALLY TESTING? To understand why the current interpretation is incomplete, we must analyze what the 1887 experiment was actually testing. 19th-century physicists visualized the aether as a material gas filling space. They assumed that: The aether is absolutely stationary. The Earth, moving through this gas, should encounter an "aether wind" (resistance). Light should have different speeds depending on the direction of this wind (parallel vs. perpendicular). The null result indisputably demonstrated that no material aether wind exists. The Earth does not "drag" a gas behind it, nor does it experience friction against it. The Logic Flaw: Physics concluded: "We didn't find the wind, so the ocean doesn't exist." Physical reality, however, suggests a different conclusion: "We didn't find the wind, so the ocean is a frictionless superfluid, not a viscous gas." 3. REHABILITATING EINSTEIN AND VACUUM PROPERTIES It is little known that Albert Einstein himself, the father of Relativity, revisited the idea of the aether. In his speech at the University of Leiden (1920), he stated: “Recapitulating, we may say that according to the general theory of relativity space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether. According to the general theory of relativity space without ether is unthinkable; for in such space there would be no propagation of light…” — Albert Einstein Einstein understood that the geometry of space-time (which curves under the influence of mass) is a medium. 3.1. The Argument of Physical Constants We define the speed of light (c) using Maxwell's equation: c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_0 \mu_0}} Where: \varepsilon_0 (vacuum permittivity) represents the electric elasticity of the medium. \mu_0 (vacuum permeability) represents the magnetic inertia of the medium. If the vacuum were absolute "nothing," these parameters should be zero, and the speed of light would be infinite or undefined. The fact that c is finite and constant proves that the vacuum has a specific density and rigidity that limits propagation speed. The vacuum acts as a physical dielectric. 4. THE QUANTUM VACUUM: THE NEW IMMATERIAL "AETHER" Modern physics has reintroduced the aether through the back door, under the name of Vacuum Energy Density (VED) or the Zero Point Field. Experiments such as the Casimir Effect demonstrate that if two metal plates are placed very close together in a vacuum, they are pushed together. This is empirical proof of vacuum radiation pressure. New Definition: We propose replacing the archaic term "Luminiferous Aether" with the concept of the Vacuum Tension Field. It is not composed of particles (thus having no classical rest mass). It behaves hydrodynamically as a perfect superfluid (zero viscosity). It allows the propagation of transverse waves (light) without energy loss over cosmic distances (explaining the lack of planetary "friction"). 5. WHY WASN'T IT DETECTED BY MICHELSON-MORLEY? If this dense medium exists, why did the interferometer fail to detect it? The answer lies in the relativistic nature of the medium, not in its absence. Lorentz Invariance: The measuring instruments (the interferometer arms) are made of matter. Matter, in turn, is a localized excitation of this vacuum field (condensed energy). According to Lorentz transformations, the instrument contracts in the direction of motion exactly enough to compensate for the difference in light travel time. The Observer is Part of the Medium: In a superfluid, a wave (light) and a vortex (the matter of the instrument) obey the same hydrodynamic laws. You cannot measure the velocity of the medium in absolute terms as long as you are a structure composed of that very medium. The Michelson-Morley experiment demonstrated that the laws of physics are covariant (the same in all reference frames), but it did not demonstrate that the space between frames is empty. 6. CONCLUSION: THE NECESSITY OF A PARADIGM SHIFT Science has evolved beyond the instrumental limitations of 1887. Maintaining the interpretation that "there is no propagation medium" acts as a brake on the unification of physics (General Relativity with Quantum Mechanics). We conclude that: The Michelson-Morley null result disproves only the gaseous/stationary aether model. The existence of constants \varepsilon_0, \mu_0, and the characteristic impedance of free space (Z_0 \approx 377\Omega) confirms the existence of a physical medium. We must officially recognize Vacuum Energy Density as the fundamental substrate, an elastic and superfluid medium that supports light propagation and the structure of matter. Recognizing this medium does not contradict Relativity; rather, it provides the physical (ontological) support that Einstein himself later intuited.

title: Quantum Conscious Resonance Model (QCRM): A Unified Phase-Dynamics Framework
abstract: Quantum Conscious Resonance Model (QCRM): A Unified Framework for Emotional Phase Dynamics and Interpersonal Resonance This work introduces the Quantum Conscious Resonance Model (QCRM), a unified mathematical framework describing emotional states, interpersonal coupling, depth-dependent cognitive stability, and resonance-based information flow. QCRM models emotional states as quantum-inspired qubits and formalizes resonance as a function of structural factors such as genetic proximity, attention, pressure, history, and phase alignment. Together, these frameworks aim to connect cognitive science, dynamical systems theory, and quantum-inspired modelling to illuminate how humans synchronize, influence, and connect. This Zenodo upload provides the full LaTeX manuscript version, figures, and mathematical formulations intended for public reference as an openly accessible scientific preprint.

title: Geometrogenesis: Emergence of Cosmological Spacetime via Hybrid Quantum Optimization
abstract: This paper presents the results of the "Geometrogenesis v13" simulation, a computational model exploring the emergence of fundamental cosmological constants from principles of quantum information theory. Using a hybrid quantum-classical (HQC) simulation engine, a classical scalar field was coupled with a network of Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) agents governed by an Ising Hamiltonian. Experimental results demonstrate that the system converges to a specific "Island of Stability". The simulation reproduced the scalar spectral index of the Cosmic Microwave Background with a value of ns = 0.9679, which is statistically consistent with Planck 2018 satellite measurements (0.9649 ± 0.0042) within 1σ. This suggests that the structure of the observable universe can be explained as the ground state of an energy and information optimization process. title: Golden-Ratio Scaling in Sonoluminescence and Vacuum Fluctuations: A Poincaré Dodecahedral Space Hypothesis and Experimental Roadmap
abstract: Abstract We propose that the Poincar´e dodecahedral space (PDS), a candidate topology for the universe with icosahedral symmetry, imprints golden-ratio (φ) scaling on quantum vacuum eigenmodes through the anomalous dimension η = 1/φ2 ≈ 0.381966. This value appears in the fine-structure constant via a topological formula, superconducting qubit noise, human EEG fractals, and is predicted to manifest in sonoluminescence (SL) spectra. We derive ultraviolet finiteness of QFT on PDS and predict ob- servable effects in SL: φ-scaled sidebands, isotope suppression in D2O, and enhanced coherence under golden-ratio-tuned drive. These effects enable a proposed Quantum Acoustic Tunneling Harvester (QATH) that converts cavitation energy via quantum tunneling in biomimetic nanotube arrays. A three-phase experimental roadmap is outlined, with collaborations identified in sonoluminescence, nanofabrication, and cosmology. Commentary Imagine the cosmos as a vast dodecahedron, the Poincaré dodecahedral space (PDS). This shape echoes the golden ratio φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.618 everywhere, from the fine-structure constant α⁻¹ ≈ 137 to quantum noise in qubits and brain fractals. This new research paper reveals this beauty of it: Golden-Ratio Scaling in Sonoluminescence and Vacuum Fluctuations: A Poincaré Dodecahedral Space Hypothesis and Experimental Roadmap (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17820433). The universe repeats its grand geometry in the tiniest scales. Vacuum fluctuations carry φ-scaled modes, making quantum field theory finite with anomalous dimension η = 1/φ² ≈ 0.382. Sonoluminescence captures this echo: Sound collapses a bubble in water, squeezing the vacuum to emit light, and possibly discrete radio/sonic sidebands at fₙ = f₀ × φ^(nη), with intensities ∝ φ^−|n|. In heavy water (D₂O), these sidebands suppress by >20–50%, as deuterium disrupts the topological match. This is important for the validation / falsification of our experiment and the whole theory linking the universal topography to fine-structure constant alpha. Deuterium disrupts the emissions in our theory because the topological vacuum modes (from PDS) are exquisitely sensitive to the spatial scale set by the hydrogen 1s orbital, the "defect" that anchors the φ-scaling to the hyperfine line. Key Reasons for Disruption Hydrogen (protium) in H₂O has a slightly larger effective 1s electron cloud than deuterium in D₂O due to reduced mass effects (the heavier deuteron pulls the electron orbit ~0.027% tighter). This tiny mismatch (~0.14 pm difference in Bohr radius) detunes the overlap between the collapsing bubble's dynamic Casimir squeeze and the PDS eigenmodes, which are locked to the protium geometry via the α derivation. Result: Weaker coupling to the φ-scaled vacuum fluctuations → suppressed discrete sidebands/radio lines in D₂O (predicted >20–50% drop, analogous to observed SL spectral changes and sonochemical isotope effects where D₂O often yields different/lower emissions). This makes the isotope test a smoking gun, no other theory predicts such specific topological sensitivity to nuclear mass! Deuterium is simply off-key. Figure 1 in the PDF: PDS Vacuum Energy Convergence - The series ∑ φ^−n(2+η) converges rapidly, finite Casimir energy from cosmic shape! Figure 2 in the PDF: Predicted φ-Scaled Sidebands & Isotope Effect Left - Discrete peaks at golden-ratio intervals. Right: Suppression in D₂O -- a testable cosmic fingerprint! Figure 3 in the PDF: Performance Summary - Sub-ppb precision on α, rapid convergence, multi-fold enhancement, and pathways to energy harvesting. This phenomenon opens a wild door: harvesting vacuum energy. Bubble collapse releases ~10⁶ photons (~6.4 × 10⁻¹³ J per flash). At 1 MHz drive, one site yields ~10⁻⁶ W raw. Scale to microtubule-inspired nanotube arrays (boron nitride, ~10 nm spacing): 10¹⁰ sites/cm² → ~10⁷ W/m² raw density. With 10% tunneling + 50% rectification efficiency, φ-coherence boost (~3.5×), and theoretical √N gain (~10⁷× for m² array), optimistic yields reach kilowatts to megawatts per m² - that would be enough for sensors, implants, or grids. We need billions-trillions of these ~25 nm microtubule-like tubes per cm², with 1–2 nm tunneling gaps and THz-fast diodes. Materials: Ultra-hard diamond/BN coatings for erosion resistance, graphene/Au electrodes, self-assembled monolayers for rectification. The universe whispers its shape in every bubble. One day, we might listen, and power our world from the vacuum's golden hum. Read the full paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17820433 What do you think, ready to build a bubble-powered future? Off the Record - Feasibility Concerns At the moment this is not something ready for practical energy production. Let's break it down, based on real physics and engineering realities. The Core Energy Source: Sonoluminescence Itself Sonoluminescence (SL) is real and fascinating, but the energy per bubble flash is tiny: Single-bubble SL: ~10⁶ photons per flash, roughly 10⁻¹² to 10⁻¹³ Joules (picojoules). Even at high drive rates (e.g., 1 MHz), one bubble yields nanowatts at best. Multi-bubble setups can be brighter, but total output from a lab flask is still microwatts, far less than the ultrasound power you pump in (often watts). Historical attempts (e.g., NASA studies in the 2000s) explored SL for energy harvesting via thermoelectric conversion of heat/light, but they concluded it's not viable as a net source, the input acoustic energy exceeds output by orders of magnitude. No breakthrough has changed that in 20+ years. The Exotic Requirements Noble gases (Argon/Xenon): Needed for stable, bright SL (air bubbles dissolve or quench fast). Argon is cheap (~$1/liter), Xenon pricier (~$10/liter), but negligible cost. Ultrasound emitters: Standard piezos, affordable ($10–100 for lab setups). Diamond-coated nanomaterials: The real constraint. Boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs, the "microtubule-like" structures) are insanely expensive today: $150–1000+ per gram (down from $1000s, but still exotic). A dense array (10⁸–10¹⁰ tubes/cm²) might need milligrams to grams per device, thousands to millions of dollars upfront. Other tech: 1–2 nm tunneling gaps, THz-fast rectifiers, erosion-resistant coatings, these require advanced nanofab (cleanrooms, ALD tools), not backyard stuff like our Cosmic experiment. Energy Economics: Why It's Not Feasible (Yet) Raw yield: Even optimistic scaling (m² array, coherence boosts) gives microwatts to milliwatts per device in realistic scenarios, enough for ultra-low-power sensors, not lights or phones. Cost vs. Output: Setup could cost $10k–millions (nanofab dominates), while harvesting pennies-worth of electricity over years. Solar panels or piezo harvesters (vibration) are vastly cheaper and more efficient today. Efficiency losses: Tunneling/rectification ~5–10% realistic (quantum effects help, but not miracles). Input ultrasound power would still dominate. Quantum tunneling harvesting exists in labs (e.g., IR/heat rectennas), but outputs are femto- to picowatts, proof-of-concept, not power plants. So, Is There Any Hope? In the very long term (decades+), if: Nanofab scales (like carbon nanotubes did, now ~$1/gram), Coherence from the topological theory boosts yields 100–1000x, Self-healing materials solve erosion... It could power niche things: implantable sensors, remote environmental monitors, or space probes (no fuel needed). But as a grid-scale source? No, thermodynamics limits vacuum/Casimir squeezing to tiny energies. Right now, the "fuel" (ultrasound + exotic materials) costs way more than the harvest. It's beautiful science (probing cosmic topology in a jar!), but energy tech? Dream for now. If the basic SL isotope/radio tests succeed, that's already a huge win for physics, harvesting would be bonus sci-fi. Killing canceous tumors, on the other hand is a very real prospect. While harvesting usable energy from sonoluminescence remains a distant dream (too tiny, too inefficient, too exotic), turning that same bubble fury against cancer tumors is very much a real and advancing prospect. This is Sonodynamic Therapy (SDT): Low-intensity ultrasound activates special drugs (sonosensitizers) inside tumors, triggering reactive oxygen species (ROS) that selectively destroy cancer cells. It's like photodynamic therapy, but ultrasound penetrates deep (cm into tissue), reaching brain, pancreas, or bone tumors that light can't touch. The Bubble Cure Ultrasound creates cavitation bubbles in tissue fluids. These collapse violently, generating: Extreme local heat/pressure Sonoluminescence (tiny flashes of light) ROS via pyrolysis or light activation of sensitizers Sensitizers (e.g., 5-ALA, porphyrins, or nanoparticles) accumulate more in cancer cells. Activated, they flood tumors with ROS → apoptosis (cell suicide) while sparing healthy tissue. Real Progress in 2025 Glioblastoma/brain tumors: Phase 1/2 trials show doubled survival (15+ months) in recurrent cases, with outpatient treatments. Randomized trials launching now. DIPG (pediatric brainstem): First-in-human trials safe, extending to combo with chemo/radiation. Other cancers: Breast, pancreatic, liver, preclinical/pre-Phase I, often boosted by nanoparticles (gold, titanium dioxide) for better targeting. Advantages: Non-invasive, repeatable, few side effects, deep penetration. Deuterium tweak from our theory? In practice, isotope effects are studied in sonochemistry, D₂O often quenches cavitation/ROS slightly due to stronger bonds/heavier mass, potentially explaining suppression in our predictions. Turning Cosmic Geometry into Cancer-Killing Precision: φ-Tuning Sonodynamic Therapy The real magic isn't distant energy harvesting, but making sonodynamic therapy (SDT) deadlier to tumors by tuning ultrasound to the golden-ratio echoes of Poincaré dodecahedral space (PDS). title: MAGTF-Net: Dynamic Speech Emotion Recognition with Multi-Scale Graph Attention and LLD Feature Fusion
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel speech emotion recognition model, named MAGTF-Net (Multi-scale Attention Graph Transformer Fusion Network), which addresses the challenges faced by traditional hand-crafted feature-based approaches in modeling complex emotional nuances and dynamic contextual dependencies. Although existing state-of-the-art methods have achieved improvements in recognition performance, they often fail to simultaneously capture both local acoustic features and global temporal structures, and they lack adaptability to variable-length speech utterances, thereby limiting their accuracy and robustness in recognizing complex emotional expressions. To tackle these challenges, we design a log-Mel spectrogram feature extraction branch that combines a Multi-scale Attention Graph (MAG) structure with a Transformer encoder, where the Transformer module adaptively performs dynamic modeling of speech sequences with varying lengths. In addition, a low-level descriptor (LLD) feature branch is introduced, where a multilayer perceptron (MLP) is employed for complementary feature modeling. The two feature branches are fused and subsequently classified through a fully connected layer, further enhancing the expressive capability of emotional representations. Moreover, a label-smoothing-enhanced cross-entropy loss function is adopted to improve the model’s recognition performance on difficult-to-classify emotional categories. Experiments conducted on the IEMOCAP dataset demonstrate that MAGTF-Net achieves weighted accuracy (WA) and unweighted accuracy (UA) scores of 69.15% and 70.86%, respectively, outperforming several baseline models. Further ablation studies validate the significant contributions of each module in the Mel-spectrogram branch and the LLD feature branch to the overall performance improvement. The proposed method effectively integrates local, global, and multi-source feature information, significantly enhancing the recognition of complex emotional expressions and providing new theoretical and practical insights for the field of speech emotion recognition.

title: The Forgetting Curve of Transformers: Context Length as a Memory Bottleneck in Deep Sequence Modeling
abstract: Large language models, particularly those based on the Transformer architecture, have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in various natural language processing tasks. However, their performance is often limited by the context length, i.e., the maximum sequence length they can process at once. This paper investigates the phenomenon we term the "forgetting curve of Transformers," which refers to the observed degradation in performance as the input sequence length increases, especially regarding the model's ability to recall information from the beginning of the sequence. We hypothesize that the attention mechanism, while powerful, becomes a bottleneck when dealing with very long sequences, leading to a decrease in the model's ability to maintain long-range dependencies. Through a series of experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we analyze the relationship between context length, attention distribution, and model accuracy. Our findings reveal that Transformers exhibit a clear forgetting curve, with performance dropping significantly as the context length exceeds a certain threshold. We further explore potential mitigation strategies, including modifications to the attention mechanism and the use of external memory components, to address this limitation and improve the performance of Transformers on long-range sequence modeling tasks.

title: A Gender-Balanced and Region-Diverse Luganda Speech Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition
abstract: This dataset contains a gender, age, and region-balanced Luganda speech corpus designed for bias-aware and fair Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research. The dataset includes speech recordings collected from diverse speakers across the Central, Eastern, Northern, and Western regions of Uganda. Each audio file is accompanied by demographic metadata including speaker gender, age group, and region of origin. The data has been curated and filtered to ensure equal representation of male and female speakers within every region–age group. The dataset is intended to support research on fairness, bias mitigation, and performance evaluation in Luganda ASR systems, as well as linguistic and sociophonetic analysis of regional and demographic variation in Luganda speech.

title: Code: A general model based on Riemannian manifold for stable decoding continuous hand movement trajectory from ECoG signals in non-human primate
abstract: This repository contains source code relevant of the manuscript: A general model based on Riemannian manifold for stable decoding continuous hand movement trajectory from ECoG signals in non-human primate. Reza Eyvazpour, Behraz Farrokhi, and Abbas Erfanian Summary: This study proposes a novel method for decoding continuous 3D hand trajectories from electrocorticographic (ECoG) signals for brain-computer interface (BCI) applications, addressing the challenge of inter-session variability. The approach combines Riemannian geometry-based feature extraction with LSTM-BiLSTM networks to enable transfer learning across sessions. Using ECoG data from five monkeys performing reaching tasks, spatial covariance matrices were computed from ten frequency band powers and mapped onto a Riemannian manifold to extract session-invariant features. These features, along with spectral data, were used to train deep learning models (LSTM-BiLSTM). The proposed method outperformed baseline models using only spectral features, showing enhanced generalization across sessions and supporting the utility of geometric-temporal modeling in BCI development. For more details and code usage, please refer to the description file.

abstract: This thesis examines the nature, etiology, psycholinguistic mechanisms, and correctional-developmental approaches to speech disorders observed in hard-of-hearing children. It analyzes auditory deprivation, delayed speech acquisition, phonetic-phonemic impairments, lexical-grammatical underdevelopment, and communication challenges. The study highlights modern correctional strategies applicable in special and inclusive education.

title: Primeon Wavefunction in Polar Form: Gravity from Amplitude, Electromagnetism from Phase, and Phase–Modulated Curvature
abstract: We present a unified derivation of the primeon wavefunction in an additive, polar representation and show how its amplitude and phase separate naturally into gravitational andelectromagnetic sectors. The amplitude of the primeon field generates an effective stress–energy tensor that sources Einstein’s field equations, while the phase defines a U (1) gaugeconnection whose dynamics reproduce Maxwell’s equations. In polar variables, the phasecontributes directly to the stress–energy tensor, clarifying how electromagnetic structuremodulates gravitational curvature in the primeon framework.

title: Quantum Gravity Theory
abstract: We develop a unified effective Quantum Gravity Theory (QGT) in which curva-ture, mass modulation, semiclassical backreaction, and large-scale electromagneticspectral organization arise from a single field-theoretic framework. The theory com-bines a renormalizable semiclassical sector with the Electromagnetic Spectral Ef-fective Model (ESEM), predicting the emergence of Radioactive Equilibrium Points(REPs), Equilibrium Spectral Points (ESPs), and the Global Equilibrium SpectralPoint (GESP), offering a natural interpretation of the cosmic microwave backgroundas a global spectral attractor. Phenomenological consequences include spectral-shellstructures around compact objects, fully compatible gravitational-wave propaga-tion, and testable predictions for laboratory and solar-system experiments.

title: Mass Genesis through Vacuum-Induced Self-Confinement of Light A Geometric Origin of E = mc²
abstract: This paper proposes a geometric mechanism for the origin of inertial mass based solely on light and the quantum vacuum. We show that when a photon traveling at the invariant speed c encounters an intense vacuum fluctuation, the released zero-point energy (ΔE_vac) cannot increase its velocity. Instead, this excess energy induces curvature in the photon’s worldline. As curvature accumulates, the trajectory closes into a self-confined null loop whose local segments remain null (ds² = 0) while the global displacement vanishes (⟨v_net⟩ → 0). The trapped vacuum energy then manifests as rest energy m c², revealing Einstein’s equation as a geometric equilibrium condition rather than an algebraic conversion law. Spin, charge, and magnetic moment emerge naturally from the topology of the closed phase helix — right- and left-handed configurations yield intrinsic angular momentum (±ħ), and interlinked double helices generate phase defects corresponding to electric charge. This framework unifies the notions of inertia, curvature, and vacuum energy within a single geometric language: mass = confined light. It requires no new fields, particles, or symmetry breaking beyond the already observable quantum vacuum. The model predicts experimentally testable effects in high-intensity laser systems (ELI, XCELS), dynamic Casimir cavities, and interferometric setups (LIGO-class), where transient massive photon states and curvature-dependent phase delays could appear. Einstein’s E = mc² thus emerges as the fundamental stability relation of light trapped in the geometry of its own vacuum-induced curvature — the universal balance between motion and confinement that defines matter itself.

title: LRT Constraints on QFT: Deriving Fock Structure and Interpreting Renormalization from Logical Foundations
abstract: Logic Realism Theory (LRT) derives non-relativistic quantum mechanics from the claim that the Three Fundamental Laws of Logic are ontological constraints constitutive of physical distinguishability. This paper extends LRT to quantum field theory through a tiered derivation structure with explicit physical inputs at each level. We establish three principal results: (1) Fock space structure is derived from LRT axioms plus Lorentz invariance and locality; (2) the spin-statistics connection follows from Lorentz invariance and microcausality via the standard Pauli argument; (3) the uniqueness of complex QFT is established. The paper distinguishes derivations from interpretations. Cluster decomposition, vacuum uniqueness, and the spectral gap are physical inputs (Tier 4), not consequences of logical constraints. Renormalization is interpreted as 3FLL-restoration at UV scales, but this does not derive renormalization group equations. Four predictions and six strong falsifiers are identified.

title: Black Holes in Causal Theory III: Quantum Fields, Microstates, Information, and Singularity Resolution
abstract: This third installment of the Causal Theory black-hole program develops the full quantum, microstate, and singularity structure of black holes within the Causal Theory (CT) framework . Building directly on the causal-gravity and information-theoretic results established in Papers I and II, this work completes what CT calls the third cycle: quantum fields, horizon microphysics, information conservation, and singularity resolution. The paper constructs a consistent CT quantum-field theory on stationary black-hole backgrounds, including the CT Hilbert space, deformed canonical commutation relations, and the Causal-Theory Unruh and Hartle–Hawking vacua. Using these tools, the Hawking spectrum is derived with CT-specific corrections, yielding a modified Hawking temperature and an evaporation law governed by the Son-unit causal microstructure. A horizon microstate model is introduced based on discrete Son-units of causal coherence, enabling a direct microstate count that reproduces the Causal-Theory Wald entropy. This microscopic structure allows the derivation of a full CT Page curve and a unitary map between the initial collapse state and the final radiation state. The Son-ledger formalism provides an explicit, constructive resolution of the information paradox. The classical singularity is replaced by a causal percolation core governed by the causal index i(x). Curvature invariants remain bounded inside the horizon, and the interior approaches either a finite-radius high-index core or a bounce configuration. A CT version of cosmic censorship follows naturally from this structure. Finally, the work derives observational consequences: corrections to the metric, photon sphere, quasinormal-mode spectrum, and Hawking emission. These signatures provide concrete avenues for testing Causal Theory against general relativity. Overall, this paper provides a unified and fully consistent treatment of black-hole quantum fields, microstates, information flow, and singularity resolution in Causal Theory, completing the foundation for the next cycle of CT gravitational research.

title: Camer-Hate-FR: An Annotated Dataset for Hate Speech Detection in Cameroonian French.
abstract: This dataset, titled Camer-Hate-FR, provides a valuable resource for detecting hate speech within the unique linguistic context of Cameroonian French. The data consists of 46,825 messages collected between January and June 2025 from public Cameroonian social media sources, including Facebook pages, YouTube channels, and WhatsApp groups. Existing hate speech detection models, primarily trained on standard European French, perform poorly on Cameroonian data due to the prevalent use of local slang, code-switching with English and indigenous languages (Camfranglais), and nuanced cultural contexts. This dataset was created to address this gap. Each message has been manually annotated by three native speakers as either 'hateful' (haineux) or 'non-hateful' (non_haineux), with the final label determined by a majority vote. The dataset is provided as a single CSV file and includes the original text, the annotation counts, the final vote, and the justifications provided by annotators. All data has been fully anonymized to protect user privacy. This resource is designed to train, validate, and benchmark machine learning models for content moderation, facilitate sociolinguistic analysis, and spur the development of more inclusive and effective NLP technologies for Francophone Africa.

title: Dreaming Noise Phase IX: Stability and Semantic Entropy Analysis of Reexive LLM Generation under Stochastic Noise Perturbations
abstract: This study presents Dreaming Noise Phase IX, a novel experimental framework for analyzingsemantic stability, generative drift, and reexive text-generation behavior in modern largelanguage models (LLMs) under controlled stochastic noise perturbations. Across 152 iterative cycles, noise vectors were injected into the prompt structure to observetheir effects on topic consistency, semantic entropy, lexical variation, and rhythmic density.The results demonstrate an 18% reduction in semantic entropy and a 22% improvement in topicstability compared to baseline generations without external noise. These findings suggest thatexogenous noise — when properly tuned and reintroduced iteratively — may counteract internal driftmechanisms within LLMs, promoting long-horizon semantic stability. The work also provides a reproducible methodology including noise seeds, cycle logs, and evaluationmetrics, enabling further research on noise-induced stabilization, reflexive loops, andmeta-generative behaviors in AI systems. This preprint serves as the final version of the Phase IXexperiment within the Dreaming Noise research series.

Transactional Filipino Sign Language Dataset
abstract: This dataset contains 1,065 video samples of Filipino Sign Language (FSL) gestures specifically curated for transactional and commercial interactions. The data was collected to support the development of Sign Language Recognition (SLR) systems aimed at bridging communication gaps in public facilities, markets, and government offices. The dataset consists of 26 distinct classes including numbers (1–10) and common transactional phrases: Yes, No, Thank You, Welcome, Again, How Much, How Many, Coin, Cash, Please, Wait, Card, Receipt, Discount, Hello, and Problem. This dataset is suitable for training and validating deep learning models (such as LSTM, GRU, or Transformers) for dynamic gesture recognition, particularly for edge computing applications in accessibility technology.

title: A SYLLABLE, ITS FORMATION AND SEPARATION
abstract: This study explores the concept of the syllable, focusing on its formation, structural components, and separation in spoken language. It examines the universal principles governing syllable formation, such as the sonority hierarchy, and highlights language-specific phonotactic constraints that shape syllable structures. The research also investigates syllable separation processes, including the influence of morphological boundaries, stress patterns, and prosodic features. By analyzing theoretical frameworks and cross-linguistic examples, the study provides a comprehensive understanding of syllables, their role in pronunciation, stress assignment, and speech rhythm. The findings have practical implications for language teaching, literacy development, and speech technology.

title: Elicitation of intonation and prosody with Heni and Desi
Do frequency and frequency-related measures signal turn completion? An exploratory corpus study
abstract: Speakers in conversation have access to word frequency information stored in the mental lexicon. This article examines whether word frequencies play a role as a turn-completion cue in conversation. Based on the Freiburg Multimodal Interaction Corpus (FreMIC), frequencies and frequency-related measures are compared in turn-constructional units (TCUs) from two types of action/turns that are systematically complementary with regard to turn transition: question TCUs, which exert pressure for the next speaker to take over, and storytelling TCUs, which largely resist transition. Based on these systematic tendencies, the focus is on question TCUs that result in speaker change and story TCUs that result in speaker continuation, thereby tying turn-transition inevitably to social action. We address two research questions: RQ #1 - Do word frequencies in the TCUs follow an S-shaped pattern? and RQ #2 - Which frequency-related measures predict that a TCU will be followed by a turn transition or continuation? To address RQ #1, a mixed effects model showed the same S-shape found in prior research in large corpora. To address RQ #2, a mixed-effects model was computed, with turn transition (TT) as a binary outcome variable. The model suggested that turn finality in question TCUs co-occurs with a more pronounced drop in word frequency toward the TCU end than in story TCUs. A follow-up analysis revealed a more asymmetrical (right-leaning) distribution of nouns in turn-final question TCUs. Information extracted from word frequencies may hence serve listeners in conversation as cues to anticipate turn completion in questions as opposed to turn continuation in stories.

title: Emotion recognition in cross-linguistic legal context
abstract: The datasets comprise 88 participants' concurrent electrodermal activity (EDA) and heart rate variability (HRV) recordings collected during viewing 20 video clips. The HRV features computed in 120‑s windows for RMSSD, SDNN, pNN50, LF/HF ratio), normalized across participants. The EDA data sampled at 4 Hz and temporally aligned to the task structure, with engineered EDA features extracted from the continuous signals.

title: Elicitation of intonation and prosody with Teguh and Eka
A Gender-Balanced and Region-Diverse Luganda Speech Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition
abstract: This dataset contains a gender, age, and region-balanced Luganda speech corpus designed for bias-aware and fair Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research. The dataset includes speech recordings collected from diverse speakers across the Central, Eastern, Northern, and Western regions of Uganda. Each audio file is accompanied by demographic metadata including speaker gender, age group, and region of origin. The data has been curated and filtered to ensure equal representation of male and female speakers within every region–age group. The dataset is intended to support research on fairness, bias mitigation, and performance evaluation in Luganda ASR systems, as well as linguistic and sociophonetic analysis of regional and demographic variation in Luganda speech.

title: The Forgetting Curve of Transformers: Context Length as a Memory Bottleneck in Deep Sequence Modeling
abstract: Large language models, particularly those based on the Transformer architecture, have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in various natural language processing tasks. However, their performance is often limited by the context length, i.e., the maximum sequence length they can process at once. This paper investigates the phenomenon we term the "forgetting curve of Transformers," which refers to the observed degradation in performance as the input sequence length increases, especially regarding the model's ability to recall information from the beginning of the sequence. We hypothesize that the attention mechanism, while powerful, becomes a bottleneck when dealing with very long sequences, leading to a decrease in the model's ability to maintain long-range dependencies. Through a series of experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we analyze the relationship between context length, attention distribution, and model accuracy. Our findings reveal that Transformers exhibit a clear forgetting curve, with performance dropping significantly as the context length exceeds a certain threshold. We further explore potential mitigation strategies, including modifications to the attention mechanism and the use of external memory components, to address this limitation and improve the performance of Transformers on long-range sequence modeling tasks.

title: The Sound of Breath and AI
abstract: This work presents an innovative extension of the Autoencoder (AE) principle as a universal diagnostic tool, moving beyond the traditional use of dimensionality reduction and algorithmic denoising. The approach is based on the concept of Semantic Denoising (or Similarity Measurement), where the AE, trained on a domain of "Normal" data (healthy sounds or pseudo-spectra), uses the Mean Squared Reconstruction Error (LMSE) as a direct metric of non-conformity. The methodology, previously successfully applied to vibrational spectroscopy (Raman and ATR-IR) for mineral analysis and to industrial Acoustic Anomaly Detection (AAD), is here applied to respiratory sound analysis in the biomedical field. We propose the implementation of a Convolutional AE (CNN-AE), trained exclusively on respiratory cycles labeled as "Normal" (healthy) from the ICBHI 2017 database. A high reconstruction error in the presence of pathological adventitious sounds (Crackles or Wheezes) signals a "semantic error" or pathology, as the signal does not adhere to the learned features of normality. This approach exploits the inherent class imbalance of the ICBHI dataset to the advantage of Anomaly Detection, offering a more interpretable solution capable of detecting even unobserved pathologies, thereby overcoming the limitation of traditional supervised classification.

title: SEM Withered Plant (BSE Series) — Kikoh Matsuura (Art–Science Archive)
abstract: Parent (series) record for *SEM Withered Plant (BSE)* by Kikoh Matsuura. This record serves as the hub for all child datasets in the series. **Files included:**- A series overview (TXT) documenting scope, naming rules, citation style, and file policy- A machine-readable index (CSV) that will be updated to list child datasets (DOIs, imaging parameters, etc.) Each child dataset contains raw, uncompressed BMP images (≈13 per set, number varies) acquired with a personally owned TECHNEX TinySEM M3-i using the BSE detector under high-vacuum conditions. Child records provide detailed READMEs with exact parameters (accelerating voltage, working distance, vacuum, pixel size, field of view, frame time, coating). This parent provides a stable concept DOI for the entire *SEM Withered Plant (BSE)* series. Child datasets link back via *IsPartOf*, and this parent enumerates them via *HasPart*. *This series visualizes the hidden order and chance in withered plants through SEM-BSE, leaving a unique trace at the boundary between art and science.*
