title: Muslim Cosmopolitanism and Urdu History Writing: The Ideas of Shibli Nu’mani c. 1880-1914
abstract: This thesis is a study of the thought and writings of the Muslim reformer, Shibli Nu’mani (1857-1914). It sets him in the intellectual context within which he was working and analyzes his contribution to discourses on Muslim selfhood and qawm (community) in nineteenth- and twentieth-century India. Employing Nu’mani as my guide, I use his writings to think through the broader project of Urdu history writing in North India during this period and to examine his contribution to Muslim modernity in India. The dissertation builds upon recent scholarship on Islam in South Asia which shows that modern Muslim intellectuals, activists and writers inhabited a global ‘Muslim world’. Challenging the dominant narrative that ‘secular’ Indian and ‘religious’ Hindu and Muslim nationalisms were the only anticolonial projects in operation, it demonstrates how Nu’mani envisioned India’s Muslims as part of a historically transnational Muslim qawm which assimilated and integrated elements of pre-Islamic and non-Islamic societies and extended to cultures and traditions outside of the subcontinent. It argues that Nu’mani imagined India’s Muslims as part of a global arena of shared Islamic traditions and articulated a cosmopolitan sense of Muslim selfhood and identity, one that was also grounded in Indian geography and culture. In so doing, it evokes the possibilities of a plural, non-territorial vision of self and society and complicates the opposition between communalism and nationalism which has shaped our understanding of Muslim identity in late colonial India. Chapter one studies the wider project of history writing in India in this period, and considers the methods employed by North Indian Muslim historians writing in Urdu. It illustrates the ways in which they both adopted and challenged the empirical techniques channelled by colonial historians when writing their own histories. Chapter two looks Nu’mani’s writings on the ‘Golden Age’ of Muslim history: the Abbasid period. It argues that his historical writings on the classical period of Islam sought to integrate the ideas, cultures and traditions of ancient Greece, pre-Islamic Persia and Egypt, India and Babylonia into modern Muslim thought and learning, a feature of his thought which I argue becomes representative of his cosmopolitan approach to Muslim selfhood. Chapter three turns to his essays on Mughal history and examines how Nu’mani fashioned a historical discourse of Muslim belonging through the concepts of adab and tamaddun, one which challenged colonial and upper caste Hindu claims about the ‘foreignness’ of Muslims to India. The fourth chapter is a study of Aurangzeb Alamgir par ek Nazar, Nu’mani’s history of the last great Mughal emperor, Aurangzeb. It analyzes the ways in which Nu’mani rewrote the history of Aurangzeb’s reign at a time when there was a growing tension between Hindu and Muslim elites around questions of representation. Revising the image of Aurangzeb as a symbol of Islamic despotism, Nu’mani devised his own notion of secular rule to cast him as a politically astute ruler whose actions were not motivated by his personal views but determined by the political, economic and social situations that confronted him. The final chapter looks at Nu’mani’s political poetry and essays and argues that he sought to bring together ideas of pan-Islamic cosmopolitanism with Hindu-Muslim unity to fashion a politics of Muslim belonging in India.

title: Gerakan ZIS dalam Muhammadiyah: Membangun Kesejahteraan Umat Melalui Filantropi Islam Profesional
abstract: Gerakan zakat, infaq, dan shadaqah (ZIS) merupakan instrumen utama dalam Islam untuk mendukung kesejahteraan sosial dan ekonomi umat. Muhammadiyah sebagai organisasi Islam modern menempatkan pengelolaan ZIS sebagai bagian penting dari misi sosial keagamaannya, terutama melalui lembaga amil zakat resmi, LAZISMU. Artikel ini menelaah konsep dasar ZIS, nilai-nilai Islam yang mendasari, tujuan dan hikmah pelaksanaan, histori perkembangan gerakan ZIS Muhammadiyah, serta bagaimana LAZISMU menjadi wujud konsistensi gerakan tersebut. Artikel menggunakan kajian dokumen resmi Muhammadiyah, literatur ilmiah, dan data empiris manajemen zakat untuk menegaskan peran sentral Muhammadiyah dalam menggerakkan filantropi Islam berbasis kelembagaan yang professional dan transparan

title: Is God for Revolution?
abstract: Abstract Is God for Revolution? is a book about social change in a time of political upheaval and uncertainty, specifically the relationship between affect, politics, and Islam. Based on interviews with (upper) middle-class Muslim Egyptians in 2018 and 2019, this work explores the ways in which political participation in a revolution and the emotions that the liminal democratic moment in Egypt evoked changed the landscape of religious discourse and practice. Before the 2011 revolution, for much of their early lives, the interviewees found themselves in structures of culturally agreed-upon forms of religiosity. They were brought up during what scholars call the “Islamic Awakening” of the late twentieth century and heeded the advice of religious figures that circulated freely in mass media. Visible markers of piety, such as the veil for women and beards for men, became commonplace. In the wake of the 2011 uprising and its perceived political defeat, interlocutors broke free of many of these structural conceptions of Islam. The book shows how, for many youth, revolutionary affects, notably hope, disappointment, doubt, shock, and anger, transformed their understandings of what it means to identify as pious Muslims. This is a story about agency in a post-revolutionary moment, the emotional toll going through this democratic experiment had on those who believed in the revolution and its ideals, and the transformative power of this agency and emotion on young revolutionaries’ attitudes toward religious authorities and religious beliefs and practices.

title: "Dr. Walter Homolka is neither a rabbi nor a Jew." Statement of Conference of Rabbis in Germany, 22 January 1998
abstract: Mitteilung of the Rabbis’ Conference of Germany (22 January 1998)Primary historical source edition Editor: Yiftach Fehige, Professor, University of TorontoOriginal Date: 22 January 1998Original Location: Stuttgart, GermanyOriginal Author: Rabbi Joel Berger, Landesrabbiner of Württemberg, Spokesperson of the Rabbis’ Conference of Germany Document type: PDF of a copy of a faxed copy of a Handwritten communication on official letterhead Source Transcription Mitteilung.Die Rabbinerkonferenz Deutschlands möchte darauf aufmerksam machen, daßHerr Dr. Walter Homolka weder Rabbiner noch Jude ist. Diese Mitteilungstützen einhellig alle Mitglieder der RK. Joel BergerSprecher der RK.(22.01.1998, Stuttgart) (Transcribed verbatim from primary source) Translation: Statement.The Rabbis’ Conference of Germany [RC, YF] would like to draw attention to the fact thatDr. Walter Homolka is neither a rabbi nor a Jew. This statement is unanimously supportedby all members of the RC. Joel BergerSpokesperson of the RC.(Dated 22 January 1998, Stuttgart) Provenance Statement This document was provided to the editor in 2025 as part of ongoing academic research into the institutional development of Jewish theology in Germany. Its authenticity and textual accuracy were discussed in conversation with Rabbi Joel Berger on 3 December 2025, who confirmed the wording and context of the statement, including the fact that the liberal rabbis at the time fully supported the statement, including Rabbi Ernst Max Stein z”l, who had admitted Dr. Walter Homolka into the Jewish people. For transparency: questions remain as to whom the original “Mitteilung” was sent in 1998. That historical detail is currently under investigation. Historical Context Note: The document published here represents a concise but significant historical source related to the internal governance and rabbinical oversight of Jewish identity claims in post-reunification Germany. It reflects a formal position of the Rabbis’ Conference of Germany (Rabbinerkonferenz Deutschlands), delivered by Landesrabbiner Joel Berger on 22 January 1998, and affirms unanimous support among the liberal, conservative, and orthodox rabbis present at that time, including the late Rabbi Dr. Ernst Max Stein z’’l. The “Mitteilung” concerns the status of Dr. Walter Homolka, who later became a central figure in the creation of academic Jewish theology at the University of Potsdam. Because Homolka subsequently acquired major leadership positions in university, rabbinical, and communal life, this document has ongoing relevance for historians, scholars of religion, and researchers studying academic transparency, institutional formation, and rabbinic authority in Germany between 1990 and 2025. Publishing this primary document provides researchers with a traceable, verifiable source that has hitherto been seldom available in public archives. It supports scholarly efforts to reconstruct procedural histories and to study relationships between rabbinical bodies, university administrations, and state ministries. title: The Significance of Warfare Prayers Among African Independent Churches in South-West Nigeria and its Relevance to African Society
abstract: This paper examines the significance of warfare prayers among African Independent Churches in South-West Nigeria and its relevance to African society. Independent Churches are Churches that are independently started in Africa by Africans rather than chiefly by missionaries from another continent. The African Independent Churches usually engage in warfare prayers. This warfare prayer is one of their distinguishing features. Warfare prayer is a common ritual practiced among members of African Independent Churches in South-West Nigeria. It entails visualization of a supposed enemy or battle and the utilization of warfare prayers, songs and Bible verses to supposedly neutralize opposing forces. Warfare prayers as employed by African Independent Churches had gone a long way to contribute to the growth and expansion of these churches in Nigeria. The paper employs the use of library sources, archival materials and internet in gathering data for it. Findings reveal that warfare prayers in African Independent Churches have a strong connection with the foundation and beliefs of traditional African society that gives spiritual undertone to every situation confronting Africans. Therefore, it is recommended that Christians can adopt this type of warfare prayers as a means of finding solutions to problems confronting them spiritually.

title: Are There Notions of Human Dignity in Japanese Religions? An Inquiry Into Folk Religion, Buddhism, and Christianity
On the Specific Character of the Buddhist Pantheon in China: The Xinlong Temple as a Case Study
abstract: The relevance of this study arises from the need, within Russian historiography, to examine Buddhist cult architecture in order to identify the specific characteristics and distinctive features of temple complexes and the Buddhist pantheon. The history of research on Chinese Buddhism occupies a central place in the broader study of ancient Chinese religions and belief systems. The author investigates the ancient Buddhist pantheon as represented in Chinese temples. Based on fieldwork conducted in northeastern China, the study focuses on the ancient Buddhist temple Xinlong, identifying its principal deities — Guanyin, the Buddha, the arhats, and the warrior deities. The source base of the research consists of this Buddhist temple, built during the Qing dynasty, and the representations of the Buddhist pantheon within its complex. The study concludes that the artistic configuration of the Buddhist pantheon in China plays a central role in understanding the religious cult and its influence on both culture and society.

PEMIKIRAN SUFISTIK DAN KETAREKATAN
abstract: ABSTRAK Penelitian ini membahas perkembangan pemikiran sufistik dan ketarekatan dalam sejarah Islam, mulai dari tasawuf akhlaki pada abad awal, kemunculan tasawuf teoritis dan falsafi pada periode klasik, hingga fase integratif yang memadukan syariat, teologi, dan spiritualitas melalui tokoh seperti al-Ghazali, Ibn Taimiyah, dan Ibn Qayyim. Kajian ini juga mengulas lahirnya tarekat-tarekat besar seperti Qadiriyyah, Naqsyabandiyyah, Syadziliyyah, serta perannya dalam pendidikan, dakwah, dan dinamika sosial-politik, termasuk kontribusinya di Nusantara. Melalui metode studi pustaka dan analisis deskriptif, penelitian ini menegaskan relevansi tasawuf sahih sebagai solusi krisis spiritual modern, sarana pembinaan akhlak, sekaligus fondasi etika sosial yang mampu menjawab tantangan zaman tanpa kehilangan kemurnian ajaran. Kata Kunci: Tasawuf, Ketarekatan, Sufisme, Tazkiyah, Tarekat Qadiriyyah, Naqsyabandiyyah, Ibn Taimiyah, Pemikiran Islam Modern.

title: Interconnection of Rigveda, Mandukya Upanishad and Yoga Sutra for Spiritual Growth
abstract: According to ancient principles of Sanatana(eternal) dharma, the four Purusharthas include Dharma (righteous), Artha(just means for acquiring wealth), Kama (fulfilling basic desires and needs of human life), and Moksha i.e enlightenment, be one with the Paramatma. The ultimate goal for human birth is described as Moksha or being one with Paramatma in Adi Shankaracharya's VivekaChudamani. One needs to go through each Purusharthas in a dharmic way to achieve moksha. The Manu Smriti proclaims that the fundamental foundation of Dharma is Veda. वेदोऽखिलो धर्ममूलं स्मृतिशीले च तद्विदाम् । vedo'khilo dharmamūlaṃ smṛtiśīle ca tadvidām | -Verse 2.6 Manusmriti. It can also be inferred that the attainment of other three modes of Purushartha also emanated from the Veda. Veda as a source is reinforced in Brahma Sutra by sage Badarayana in this Sutra शास्त्रयोनित्वात् ॥ १.१.३॥śāstrayonitvāt. Which states that Paramatma or ParaBrahma can be known only through Vedas. For the ease of consumption Veda is categorized by Sage Veda Vyasa into four parts Rigveda, Yajur Veda, Sama Veda and Atharva Veda. Each of these Veda has an end part called Upanishad. There are 10 principal Upanishads and 108 main Upanishads Along with Veda, there are six ancient texts called darshanas or schools of thought. One such preeminent darshana is Maharishi Patanjali's Yoga Sutra. This study extracts and provides a vision of underlying connection across Rigveda, Mandukya Upanishad and Yoga Sutra to seek Paramatma. The Mandukya Upanishad having only twelve verses, represents the quintessence of the entire Upanishadic teaching. It analyzes the whole spectrum of human consciousness through the three states of waking (Jagrat), dream (Svapna), and dreamless sleep (Susupti). This Upanishad provides a great symbol for the meditation and the realization of the supreme reality, a mono-syllable AUM. It is considered as “the word of all words”, with three sounds -A, U, M- each one is a representation of the divine entity i.e., deva, Vaisvanara, Taijasa and Prajna respectively. Each of these deities are visualized by Rig Vedic sages, in some instances with the same name as described in Mandukya Upanishad, in other times in derived forms based on the traits associated with each syllable of AUM. In order to contemplate and meditate on this symbol and realize the truth, one needs strong physical and mental health. Sage Patanjali in his pioneering work in Yoga Sutras has indicated the systematic paths in four padas - Samadhi Pada, Sadhana Pada, Vibhuti Pada and Kaivalya Pada. īśvarapraṇidhānādvā -Yoga Sutra 1.23, tasya vācakaḥ praṇavaḥ - Yoga Sutra 1.27. These sutras in the Samadhi pada signify that surrender to īśvara with the sacred word is Om. The Rigveda describes īśvara and its various forms, while the Mandukya upanishad describes praṇavaḥ (Aum) and how to achieve spiritual growth through its contemplation. This paper highlights interconnectivity of these ancient texts which were not explored or studied in detail. In this study, our approach to spiritual growth unearthed a practical guideline for spiritual seekers, drawing from the rich traditions of Vedic philosophy, meditation, and yoga practice, where the seekers can find a structured path toward spiritual enlightenment.

Exiled Representatives of the Catholic Clergy in Western Siberia (1880s — Early 20th Century)
abstract: The topic of political exile to Siberia is one of the most significant and relevant issues in contemporary historical scholarship. The current complexity of international relations highlights the need to turn to the historical experience accumulated through centuries of interaction among the peoples of different nations. In this context, the study of the conditions of coexistence among representatives of various nationalities and religious denominations in Siberia is of particular interest. This article examines the presence of members of the Catholic clergy in Western Siberia during the 1880s and the early 20th century. These individuals had been exiled for their participation in the Polish national liberation movement of the 1860s. The study explores their numbers, places of residence, material conditions, and occupations, supplemented by biographical information. Catholic priests served in local churches (kostyols), engaged in educational and missionary activities, and provided moral support and unity to the Polish community in Siberia, thereby exerting a noticeable influence on the region’s social and cultural life.

The Sacral State: Henry VIII, Elizabeth I, and the Political Theology of English Sovereignty
abstract: This paper explores the evolution and consolidation of the "Sacral State" in England under the reigns of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, focusing on the political theology that underpinned their assertion of sovereignty. Henry VIII's break with Rome fundamentally redefined the relationship between temporal and spiritual power, establishing royal supremacy and vesting the monarch with ultimate authority over the English Church. This transformation was driven by both dynastic necessity and a desire for absolute control, laying the groundwork for an unprecedented fusion of church and state. Elizabeth I, while inheriting a kingdom deeply divided by religious turmoil, skillfully navigated these challenges by refining her father's legacy. Her adoption of the title "Supreme Governor" and the implementation of the Elizabethan Religious Settlement sought to establish a comprehensive yet moderate Anglican identity. Crucially, Elizabeth employed a sophisticated political theology, including the "cult of Elizabeth" and the concept of the "King's Two Bodies," to legitimize her rule and elevate the monarchy to a divinely sanctioned institution beyond mere temporal power. By examining the legislative, theological, and performative aspects of their reigns, this study argues that both monarchs, despite their distinct styles, were instrumental in forging a uniquely English form of sacral sovereignty, where the monarch was not merely God's anointed ruler but an integral, divine head of the nation's spiritual and temporal life. This analysis illuminates how political theology served as a critical tool for centralizing power, stabilizing the realm, and shaping the enduring identity of the English state.

"Multi-Factor SSVEP EEG Dataset"
abstract: "This dataset contains electroencephalography (EEG) recordings collected in a multi-factor steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) brain\u2013computer interface (BCI) experiment. Fifteen healthy adults (10 males, 5 females; 20 \u00b1 2 years), all with normal color vision and no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, participated after providing written informed consent. Visual stimuli followed a full-factorial design crossing three attributes: color (red, orange, white), shape (circle, square), and spacing ratio between stimulus size and center-to-center distance (1:1, 2:1, 10:1), yielding 18 stimulus conditions. Four flickering targets were displayed simultaneously on a 60 Hz LCD monitor at 10.25, 11.25, 12.25, and 13.25 Hz. Each condition contained 10 blocks, and each block comprised four 9-s trials (1.5-s cue, 6-s stimulation, 1.5-s rest), resulting in 40 trials per condition and 720 trials per subject. EEG was acquired with a DSI-24 wireless dry-electrode system (24 channels; 19 scalp electrodes plus 2 ear references and 3 auxiliary channels; 10\u201320 montage; 300 Hz sampling rate). Each block file provides a continuous 36-s EEG segment (4 consecutive trials) with channel labels. The data are organized by subject, stimulus condition, and block index.This resource enables systematic evaluation of stimulus design and decoding algorithms in SSVEP-BCI. It is particularly suitable for benchmarking classical machine-learning methods and modern deep neural networks, for studying multi-factor stimulus effects (shape, color, spacing), and for developing robust SSVEP decoding, transfer learning, and data-augmentation strategies."

title: LOGORHYTHMIC TRAINING FOR CHILDREN WITH SPEECH DISORDERS
abstract: This thesis examines the role, structure, and pedagogical value of logorhythmic exercises in the correction and development of speech in children with speech disorders. Integrating movement, rhythm, and speech stimulation, logorhythmics acts as a multisensory intervention that strengthens phonation, breathing, articulation, and prosodic components of speech. The study highlights the theoretical foundations, methodological principles, and practical recommendations for implementing logorhythmic sessions in special education.

The Worms Ultimatum: Luther, Empire, and the Reimagination of Authority
abstract: The Diet of Worms in 1521 stands as a pivotal moment in European history, marking a profound shift in the conceptualization and exercise of authority. This paper examines Martin Luther's defiant stand before Emperor Charles V and the imperial assembly, arguing that his refusal to recant his theological propositions fundamentally challenged both the ecclesiastical supremacy of the Pope and the political universalism of the Holy Roman Empire. By asserting the primacy of individual conscience guided by Scripture over established hierarchical structures, Luther inadvertently initiated a radical reimagination of authority, contributing to the fragmentation of Christendom and the emergence of new models of religious and secular governance. This analysis delves into the immediate and long-term consequences of the Edict of Worms, exploring how Luther's actions catalyzed a redefinition of sovereignty, fostered the development of territorial churches, and laid groundwork for modern notions of religious freedom and the state's role in society. The study concludes that the "Worms Ultimatum" was not merely a theological dispute but a critical nexus that reshaped the very foundations of political and religious power in early modern Europe.

title: Invisible Religion Amidst the Visible Struggles: The Reception of Thomas Luckmann in Iranian Sociology
The Vertical and the Divine: Aksumite Obelisks and the Christianization of Ezana's Royal Ideology
abstract: The ancient Aksumite civilization, flourishing in the Horn of Africa, left an indelible mark on history through its monumental stelae, often referred to as obelisks. These towering granite structures, intricately carved to mimic multi-storied buildings, served as potent symbols of royal power, ancestral veneration, and a connection to indigenous sky deities in the pre-Christian era. This paper investigates the profound transformation of Aksumite royal ideology during the reign of King Ezana (circa 320-360 CE), a pivotal period marked by the kingdom's conversion to Christianity. Drawing upon archaeological evidence, numismatics, and Ezana's trilingual inscriptions, we analyze how the pre-existing symbolic framework of the obelisks, particularly their inherent verticality, was reinterpreted and integrated into a new Christian theological paradigm. While the practice of erecting new monumental stelae ceased after Christianization, their enduring presence necessitated a recontextualization. We argue that Ezana strategically leveraged the established cultural reverence for these vertical monuments, re-framing their ascent towards the divine from a polytheistic cosmic order to a monotheistic Christian heaven, thereby reinforcing his divinely sanctioned Christian kingship. This study illuminates the dynamic interplay between inherited architectural symbolism and evolving religious belief in the construction of royal authority.

title: The Counter-Reformation's Affective Turn: Jesuits, Trent, and the Baroque Reshaping of Religious Experience
abstract: The Counter-Reformation, a period of profound spiritual and institutional renewal within the Catholic Church, is often understood through its doctrinal reaffirmations and institutional reforms. This paper argues for a critical re-evaluation, positing that a significant, deliberate "affective turn" in religious experience was central to its success. Challenging the Protestant emphasis on the intellect and individual reading of scripture, Catholic reformers, particularly the Jesuit order and the decrees of the Council of Trent, actively cultivated emotional and sensory engagement to foster a deeper, more personal, and communal piety. This reshaping of religious experience found its most potent artistic expression in the Baroque style. Through a systematic analysis of Jesuit spiritual exercises, Tridentine decrees on images and sacraments, and the immersive aesthetics of Baroque art and architecture, this study reveals how the Counter-Reformation harnessed sight, sound, touch, and imagination to create a dramatic, emotionally resonant faith. This strategic engagement of the senses and emotions was not merely a superficial embellishment but a fundamental theological and pastoral imperative designed to re-anchor the faithful in Catholic doctrine and devotion, leaving an enduring legacy on global Catholicism.

title: Sovereignty, Sacrament, and Separatism: Crafting Competing Christianities in Reformation Europe
abstract: The Reformation era in Europe (16th-17th centuries) witnessed a profound fragmentation of Christian unity, giving rise to diverse and often conflicting religious identities. This paper investigates the intricate interplay of three pivotal forces—political sovereignty, sacramental theology, and the emergence of separatist movements—in shaping these competing Christianities. It argues that the assertion of secular rulers' authority over religious affairs, deep doctrinal disagreements concerning the nature and efficacy of sacraments, and the determined pursuit of religious autonomy by radical groups were not merely parallel developments but mutually constitutive elements. These factors collectively forged distinct confessional landscapes, redefined the relationship between church and state, and laid the groundwork for modern religious pluralism and state sovereignty. Through comparative analysis of key regions and movements, this study illuminates how the competition over religious truth and political power irrevocably altered the spiritual and political fabric of early modern Europe.

title: Script, Image, and State: Remaking Humanism in the Northern Renaissance
abstract: The Northern Renaissance represents a pivotal era where the ideals of humanism, originating in Italy, underwent profound transformation through the intricate interplay of script, image, and the evolving nature of the state. This paper argues that these three forces were not merely channels for the dissemination of ideas but active agents in shaping a distinctly Northern European humanism, characterized by its Christian emphasis, commitment to social reform, and a new public intellectual sphere. The advent of the printing press revolutionized the accessibility and authority of classical and biblical texts, profoundly influencing literacy and theological discourse. Concurrently, a vibrant visual culture, propelled by innovations in printmaking and oil painting, served as a powerful medium for articulating humanist thought, religious devotion, and political propaganda. The emerging centralized states, with their need for educated bureaucrats and their capacity for patronage and control, further integrated and manipulated these new forms of communication. By examining the symbiotic relationships between written word, visual representation, and political power, this study demonstrates how Northern humanism was remade into a dynamic, reform-oriented movement that laid critical groundwork for the Protestant Reformation and the modern European identity. The unique synthesis of these elements fostered a widespread intellectual and artistic awakening, redefining the individual's relationship to God, society, and the burgeoning political landscape.

title: Psychological Instability and Madness in Anne Bradstreet's Representative Poems: An Analysis
abstract: ÖZ Bu çalışma, protofeminist Amerikalı şair Anne Bradstreet’in (1612–1672) temsili şiirlerini ayrıntılı biçimde analiz ederek, bu şiirlerin Bradstreet’in bir kadın şair olarak delilik, istikrarsızlık, duygusal kırılganlık ve yaşam, ölüm, annelik, inanç ile sanatçılık etrafında şekillenen karmaşık mücadelelerini nasıl yansıttığını incelemektedir. Bu bağlamda, Bradstreet’in eserlerinin yalnızca estetik bir üretim olarak değil, aynı zamanda şairin zihinsel süreçlerini, duygusal tepkilerini, kişisel korkularını ve toplumsal konumunu görünür kılan bir ifade alanı olarak değerlendirilmesi önem taşır. Şairin metinleri, okuyucuyu hem bireysel hem de kültürel düzeyde etkileyen içsel çatışmalar, varoluşsal sorgulamalar, dini tereddütler ve ruhsal sarsıntılarla yüzleştirir. On yedinci yüzyılda kadınların edebi alanda ciddi biçimde kısıtlandığı düşünüldüğünde, Anne Bradstreet’in erkek egemen otoriteye karşı “yazar” kimliğini ısrarla sahiplenmesi ve kendini ifade etme çabası özellikle dikkat çekicidir. Bu makale, onun özgün şiirsel sesinin bu meydan okumayı hangi temalar, imgeler ve anlatım stratejileri üzerinden somutlaştırdığını tartışmakta; metinlerinde görülen delilik, kuşku, öz-farkındalık ve yaratıcı kimlik arayışını ayrıntılı biçimde analiz etmektedir. Anahtar kelimeler: Şiir, Anne Bradstreet, Amerikan Edebiyatı, Delilik, Zihinsel Durumlar, Kadın Edebiyatı ABSTRACT This study analyzes in detail the representative poems of the protofeminist American poet Anne Bradstreet (1612–1672) and examines how these poems reflect Bradstreet’s complex struggles as a woman poet, shaped by madness, instability, emotional fragility, and life, death, motherhood, faith, and artistry. In this context, it is significant to evaluate Bradstreet’s works not only as aesthetic productions, but also as a field of expression that makes visible the poet’s mental processes, emotional reactions, personal fears, and social position. The poet’s texts confront the reader with internal conflicts, existential questionings, religious hesitations, and spiritual turmoil that affect both individual and cultural levels. Considering that women were severely restricted in the literary sphere in the seventeenth century, Anne Bradstreet’s persistent embrace of the identity of “writer” against male-dominated authority and her struggle for self-expression are particularly striking. This article discusses the themes, images, and narrative strategies through which her unique poetic voice embodies this challenge; it analyses in detail the madness, doubt, self-awareness and creative search for identity seen in her texts. Keywords: Poetry, Anne Bradstreet, American Lliterature, Madness, Mental States, Women’s Writing

Wave Period Variability in a Quiescent Solar Prominence
abstract: Abstract On 2022 September 26, we observed a quiescent solar prominence with H α imaging spectroscopy using the Solar Dynamics Doppler Imager (SDDI) on board the Solar Magnetic Activity Research Telescope (SMART). Unlike earlier works that detected 4 and 15 minute oscillations through long-slit, 1D wavelet methods, we adapt the wavelet analysis to 3D data to explore the full prominence structure. Complementary data from Solar Dynamics Observatory/Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (304, 171 Å) STEREO-A Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUVI; 304 Å), and Solar Orbiter Extreme Ultraviolet Imager/Full Sun Imager (304, 174 Å) enable a multiview, multithermal investigation of wave periodicity across the prominence. Our aim is to characterize how oscillatory periods are distributed in plasma at different temperatures and viewing angles, thereby assessing wave propagation and variability throughout the prominence body. We analyze time series of Doppler signal from SMART/SDDI H α observations alongside extreme-ultraviolet intensity variations from space-based instruments. We detect oscillatory plasma motions with periods spanning 3–74 minutes. Strong periodicity at 20, 31, and 53 minutes dominates in neutral plasma (H α ), while 13 and 74 minute oscillations are pronounced in the 304 Å passband, concentrated mainly in the central prominence. Additional short-period fluctuations include weaker 3–6 minute oscillations and rapid 30 s transverse waves in Doppler signals near the solar surface. These findings highlight the richness of wave periodicity in quiescent prominences, revealing a dynamic superposition of long- and short-period oscillations and kink-like disturbances. This multi-instrument, 3D perspective advances our understanding of how prominence plasma supports and modulates diverse wave modes.

title: 'Benedictus' 'Maledictus': The Discourse of the Other and the Emergence of the Subject of the Unconscious
abstract: A Journey Through the Word that Alienates and Liberates In this fundamental work, the reader is invited to traverse the paths of the word in its dual face: that which captures the subject in the signifiers of the Other (Maledictus) and that which, resignified, becomes an instrument of liberation and self-invention (Benedictus). Through a rigorous investigation that articulates Freud and Lacan, the book unveils how the same word that constitutes us in alienation can become a vehicle for subjective emancipation. From the capture mechanisms of the Discourse of the Master to the ethics of the Discourse of the Analyst, from the petrified word of the symptom to the creative act of the subject, this work offers a theoretical compass to navigate the complex territories of psychoanalytic clinic. Ideal for psychoanalysts in training, experienced professionals, and scholars of the humanities, "Benedictus" "Maledictus" represents an essential contribution to understanding the destinies of the contemporary subject and the ethical possibilities of its emergence in the face of the determinations of discourse. A work that transforms our understanding of the therapeutic power of the word and its radical limits.

abstract: December 4, 2025 — The 4:32 Corpus: Autological Witness, Attachment Physics, Pop-Catholic Iconography, and the INRI Reversal I just do this every day until the CIA starts paying me. This unified entry collects the full set of research works produced on December 4, 2025, Day 32 of a forty-day fast offered for Pontius Pilate. Across scientific, theological, narrative, and iconographic genres, the works collectively illustrate how a single lived day can function as an autological lab: a site where inner state, symbolic action, scientific modeling, and theological interpretation cohere into one structure. The corpus includes: • Autological Papers in the Age of AI — a methodological treatise arguing that modern scientific and theological writing must foreground the author’s phenomenology and belief-change as primary data, establishing the “autological stack” as a new scholarly norm. • Bond Fields: A Multi-Scale Control-Theoretic Model of Human Attachment — a synthesis of attachment theory, biobehavioral synchrony, predictive processing, and control theory that formalizes interpersonal “bond fields” as distributed regulatory structures across dyads, families, groups, and crowds. • Applied Illusionism and Relational Reality — a physics-to-phenomenology bridge showing how quantum relationalism, emergent spacetime, and perceptual interface theories jointly imply that lived reality is a layered interface, not a direct view of fundamental structure. • Pontius Pilate and the Stations of the Cross — a theological-structural analysis treating Pilate not merely as a historical agent but as a narrative gear whose constrained agency participates in Christ’s kenotic trajectory. • Handing Back INRI: Pilate, Buddy Christ, and the Ledgered Dead in a Pop-Catholic Icon — an icon-theological study of the digitally composed image in which Amelia returns the INRI inscription to Jesus, symbolically reversing Roman blame and enacting John 1:29 within a meme-era visual grammar. • Amelia & Pontius — The INRI Time-Hop Adventure — a children’s narrative reframing Pilate’s conscience through playful catechesis, using humor, empathy, and time-travel motifs to teach the logic of mercy. Together, these works form the foundation of The 4:32 Day paper, which interprets December 4 as a patterned event: a moment when Deuteronomy 4:32, Luke 4:32, John 4:32, and Acts 4:32 converge with fasting, authorship, pop iconography, AI-assisted research, and a ritual act (handing back INRI) to reveal a unified theological psychology of doubt-removal and covenant participation. A public NotebookLM research notebook accompanies the corpus and is open for all readers to explore, ask questions, and follow the reasoning across documents: https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/4429b01d-8787-433a-823f-229779624485

title: A DIMENSÃO EMOCIONAL DO ACOLHIMENTO FAMILIAR: UM ESTUDO COM FAMÍLIAS ACOLHEDORAS
abstract: Em um cenário marcado por múltiplas violações de direitos na infância e adolescência, o acolhimento familiar se apresenta como uma medida protetiva prevista no Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente (ECA), configurando-se como uma alternativa humanizada de cuidado para crianças e adolescentes que precisam ser temporariamente afastados de suas famílias de origem. Muito além de uma previsão legal, trata-se de uma vivência que se constrói no cotidiano de famílias que, voluntariamente, oferecem seu lar, afeto e cuidado para acolher um sujeito em situação de vulnerabilidade. Ao disponibilizarem seu espaço doméstico e afetivo para o cuidado de crianças ou adolescentes em situação de vulnerabilidade, essas famílias vivenciam experiências complexas, que envolvem sentimentos de afeto, empatia e realização pessoal, mas também enfrentam desafios emocionais relacionados às mudanças em sua dinâmica cotidiana e ao término do acolhimento. Nesse contexto, o presente estudo teve como objetivo entender como as experiências emocionais vivenciadas pelas famílias que participam do serviço de acolhimento familiar influenciam a vinculação com os acolhidos, a dinâmica familiar interna e os impactos vivenciados individualmente pela pessoa que acolhe. A análise dos dados resultou na identificação de três categorias centrais: a solidariedade como dispositivo de motivação para acolher e os impactos emocionais positivos para aqueles que acolhem; desafios emocionais e reorganização da vida familiar durante e após o acolhimento; e a equipe técnica e a rede de serviços como pilares de proteção emocional para as famílias acolhedoras. Os resultados indicaram que o acolhimento é uma prática voltada à solidariedade e ao desejo de contribuir socialmente, mas também uma experiência marcada por desafios e transformações emocionais, que impactam a dinâmica familiar e exige preparo e suporte técnico contínuo.

From the capture mechanisms of the Discourse of the Master to the ethics of the Discourse of the Analyst, from the petrified word of the symptom to the creative act of the subject, this work offers a theoretical compass to navigate the complex territories of psychoanalytic clinic. Ideal for psychoanalysts in training, experienced professionals, and scholars of the humanities, "Benedictus" "Maledictus" represents an essential contribution to understanding the destinies of the contemporary subject and the ethical possibilities of its emergence in the face of the determinations of discourse. A work that transforms our understanding of the therapeutic power of the word and its radical limits.

title: Advancing biodiesel production from milk scum oil: a deep learning and synthetic data approach with ablation study for process optimization
abstract: <title>Abstract</title> This study proposes a novel framework for optimizing biodiesel production from high free fatty acid (FFA) milk scum oil, a major waste stream, by applying deep learning models to high-fidelity synthetic process data. It demonstrates that deep learning can accurately predict complex process outcomes and provides interpretability via ablation analysis. A two-step biodiesel production process is mathematically modelled to generate a comprehensive synthetic dataset. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) model is trained on this dataset to predict biodiesel yield and intermediate FFA content, and an ablation study examines the contribution of key input features and network layers to performance. The methodology is implemented in Python with code provided for reproducibility. The MLP model achieves high accuracy in predicting biodiesel yield and FFA reduction from synthetic data, showing that deep learning can capture complex nonlinear relationships. Ablation results highlight critical process parameters (e.g., reaction temperature, catalyst concentration) and specific neural network layers that significantly affect prediction accuracy. These insights enhance the interpretability and trustworthiness of the model in a chemical engineering context. This work is the first to combine high-fidelity synthetic data generation, deep learning modelling, and systematic ablation analysis for biodiesel optimization from high-FFA milk scum oil. It offers both strong predictive capability and transparent interpretability for process optimization. The framework provides a cost-effective, safe alternative to extensive lab trials, giving engineers a computational tool to design and refine biorefineries while promoting waste-to-fuel enhancement in India.

title: Full waveform inversion for a long-wavelength velocity model using a regenerated wavefield based on the SWEET method
abstract: In full waveform inversion (FWI), long-wavelength velocity models are essential for accurately estimating subsurface physical parameters. However, building long-wavelength velocity models with low-frequency components is challenging due to mechanical limitations in seismic data acquisition. We propose a novel FWI method that utilizes a regenerated wavefield derived from the Suppressed Wave Equation Estimation of Traveltime (SWEET) algorithm. The regenerated wavefield in our approach was obtained by convolving the arbitrary source wavelet with a Green&rsquo;s function, which is represented by the first-arrival traveltime and amplitude extracted from the SWEET algorithm. Our approach can build long-wavelength velocity models, provided that a low-frequency wavelet is used. Furthermore, the potential for multi-scale inversion was demonstrated by gradually increasing the frequency of the source wavelet, leading to the acquisition of high-resolution models. In numerical examples, our proposed algorithm was validated using both synthetic and field data sets. We also assessed the noise sensitivity of the proposed method, confirming its applicability in practical scenarios. These results demonstrate that the proposed method is a robust and versatile tool for constructing long-wavelength and high-resolution velocity models from band-limited seismic data.

title: The Vijay Flux–Shadow Gravity Model: A Unified Alternative to Dark Matter
abstract: This work presents the Vijay Flux–Shadow Gravity Model, a gravitational framework that eliminates the need for particle dark matter while preserving dark energy as the driver of cosmic expansion. The model is constructed from two physical components:(1) a cosmic flux term arising from large-scale vacuum expansion, and(2) a baryon-linked shadow term that modifies local gravitational potentials through geometric flux obstruction rather than unseen matter. The formulation satisfies all major consistency requirements, including the Poisson equation, Friedmann equations, Raychaudhuri equation, Jeans stability, stress–energy conservation, and Maxwell-type constraints. It exactly recovers Newtonian gravity in spherical systems, produces flat galactic rotation curves, and reproduces key features of weak lensing and cluster dynamics. The effective mass profile generated by the shadow field yields logarithmic mass growth without invoking non-baryonic matter. This version also incorporates covariant shadow dynamics, a full action-based derivation, early-universe behavior consistent with CMB acoustic-peak formation, and a geometric interpretation of relativistic effects such as time dilation and length contraction. The model integrates smoothly into relativistic cosmology and offers a clear mechanism for structure formation and gravitational enhancement that remains consistent with the standard role of dark energy. We present numerical tests showing solar-system consistency at the 10⁻⁹ level and a numerical reproduction of the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation. The deposition invites the scientific community to perform independent numerical tests—such as CMB transfer-function evaluation, perturbation-growth analysis, and Boltzmann-code simulations—to further assess the model’s viability.

title: Hubble Tension Resolved By Geometry: Aperture Well Unification Theory
abstract: We present a fully geometric resolution of the Hubble tension within the Aperture–Well Unifica- tion Theory (AWUT). In this framework, spacetime is constructed from three coupled harmonic media—Blue (expansion), Red (curvature wells), and Purple (a mediating band)—all emerging from the Ka–Boom and Planck–Stop initial conditions. Cosmic expansion is encoded in the effective oscillation of the Blue medium. As structure forms, coagulated Red wells and a broadening Purple band distort Blue rails, increasing the effective path length of expansion modes. Early–universe probes (CMB) observe Blue in a nearly uniform state, while late–universe probes measure Blue rails deformed by a fully developed cosmic web. This naturally produces two different inferred values of H0 without modifying early–universe physics or introducing new fields. From AWUT first principles we derive the rail–wrinkling equation, which connects the frac- tional Hubble shift to the Blue–Red harmonic gap (fB−fR)/fB , the baryon fraction ΩR, and a single dimensionless coagulation factor Ceff summarizing the degree of curvature concentration: ∆H = λR ΩR Ceff. H0 Using only the observed Hubble tension and the measured baryonic fraction, we infer a present– day coagulation factor Ceff(0) = 6.8 ±0.8. This single empirically determined quantity is then held fixed and used to predict a reduced late–time BAO sound horizon, environment– dependent shifts in lensing–based H0, a mild low–redshift Hubble anisotropy, and an upward tilt in chronometer H(z) reconstructions. The same harmonic structure has previously matched galaxy rotation curves, lensing locks, atomic structure, and the muon anomalous magnetic moment. Here we show that the Hubble tension is another natural emergent property of AWUT’s geometric spacetime, and we outline clear falsification tests for upcoming surveys.

title: The ACORN Cosmology Suite: A Unified Geometric Solution to Dark Matter, Dark Energy, Black Holes, and the Big Bang
abstract: The ACORN Cosmology Pentapoly (2025) presents a unified geometric framework in which all physical phenomena arise from the finite curvature structure of a smooth, compact 5D manifold. The observable 4D universe is interpreted as a projection (or slicing) of this higher-dimensional geometry, and all particles, fields, forces, constants, and cosmological phenomena emerge as different sectors of its curvature spectrum. Across five papers, the Pentapoly develops: • Paper I — A finite-curvature reformulation of electromagnetism, inertia, and rest mass through the mass-partition relation and the 5D projection metric. • Paper II — A 5D extension of General Relativity, yielding the unified Einstein–Maxwell system as a 4D projection of the higher-dimensional geometry. • Paper III — Curvature quantisation across the proton–Planck boundary, generating the discrete curvature modes that correspond to the spectrum of elementary particles. • Paper IV — ACORN (A Curvature–Origin Reality Network), which identifies electromagnetic inertia, charge, and quantum-like behaviour as 5D curvature oscillations and projection effects. • Paper V — The cosmological completion of the framework: the Big Bang is shown to be a projection singularity (a caustic) rather than a physical beginning. Cosmic expansion arises from the motion of the 4D hypersurface through 5D rather than from metric creation, dark energy fluids, or inflation. Dark matter emerges from high closed curvature modes, and dark energy from the transverse curvature gradient of the manifold. The combined result is a singularity-free, finite, falsifiable cosmological model that replaces the standard Big Bang paradigm. All infinities and singularities are removed; all dark-sector behaviours arise from geometry; and early-universe structure occurs via curvature-mode phase rather than quantum fields or inflation. The ACORN Cosmology Pentapoly offers a unified geometric interpretation of all observed physics, grounded in five logically connected, standalone research papers, and proposes a testable alternative to ΛCDM cosmology.

title: The Breathing Universe - A Multi-Mode Temporal Coherence Analysis of the NANOGrav 12.5-Year Pulsar Timing Residuals
abstract: We present a time-domain coherence analysis of the NANOGrav 12.5-year pulsar timing residuals, focusing on the presence of deterministic low-frequency structure beyond standard red-noise and power-law interpretations. Using uniformly binned residuals, inverse-variance weighting, global and per-pulsar harmonic fitting, circular phase analysis, and sliding-window time–frequency tracking, we identify a compact set of persistent temporal modes in the ≈12–17 year range, together with additional low-frequency components at nominal periods ≳20 years. Although the longest components exceed the observational baseline and cannot be treated as fully resolved oscillations, they act as stable low-frequency trends that significantly improve the description of the residuals. A single sinusoid accounts for ~22% of the global variance, whereas a six-mode harmonic model captures ~55% and suppresses ultra-low-frequency power by a factor of ~350. Individual pulsars display distinct phase clustering—primarily around –80° with a minority in anti-phase—indicating a shared, sky-spanning temporal signal. The combined frequency–phase structure suggests that the modes form a coherent helical pattern in phase–frequency space, representing an emergent geometric organization of the temporal field. We discuss these results in the context of dynamical-time-field frameworks in which small oscillatory variations in the clock-rate field, H(t), generate multi-frequency “breathing” behavior. The inferred fractional modulation amplitude is ε ~ 10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹⁴. These findings highlight the importance of discrete temporal coherence as a complementary class of PTA observables and outline observational targets for upcoming PTA datasets.

abstract: This work introduces the Theory of Macrity, a universal repulsive force acting opposite to gravity, characterized by the coupling constant . title: The Maturity Hypothesis
abstract: Modern astronomy has peeled back the darkness with instruments of extraordinary subtlety.We track near-Earth asteroids the size of garages.We resolve Kuiper Belt objects glinting at the scattered fringe of the solar system.Amateur astronomers with backyard setups discover comets years before they grace perihelion.Our gravitational wave detectors — LIGO, Virgo, KAGRA — hear spacetime itself ring when black holes collide in distant galaxies. We are living through a golden era of cosmic sensitivity. The void has never been more thoroughly scanned. And yet: nothing.No craft drifting between stars.No blueshifted signatures of incoming visitors.No warped gravitational corridors marking repeated travel.No anomalous structures silhouetted against starlight.Not a single unambiguous indication of interstellar traffic. Traditional replies offer pace and patience: the galaxy is vast, civilizations rare, and our search short. But this paper proposes a deeper and more unsettling interpretation:We do not see interstellar travellers because mature civilizations do not traverse interstellar space. They have no rationale to do so, no incentive to brave the hostility of the void, no reason to endure journeys that erase time and identity. Interstellar travel is not a technical barrier awaiting breakthrough; it is an evolutionary dead-end abandoned by every civilization that survives long enough to understand the real architecture of the universe. Drawing on the torsion-rich geometry of Einstein–Cartan theory, and on holographic boundary principles that regulate the deep vacuum, we argue that advanced civilizations discover a more fundamental mode of motion: dimensional traversal, using the fiber structure latent in spacetime’s torsion degrees of freedom. These fibers offer directions that are not spatial yet remain physically navigable allowing entities to vanish, reappear, or shift configuration without crossing physical distance. This framework reinterprets the long, perplexing, and cross-cultural record of anomalous encounters: beings that appear and vanish without acceleration; craft that blink rather than fly; forms suspiciously biologically compatible with Earth. Such features are poorly matched to extraterrestrial visitation but beautifully consistent with dimensional adjacency neighbours separated by a phase angle rather than by light years. The Maturity Hypothesis states that civilizations progress not outward across space but inward into the geometry of reality itself. The Fermi Paradox dissolves when we abandon the misconception that stars are destinations. The void is silent not because it is empty but because nobody uses it. The universe is not an ocean.It is a structure with many rooms.The silence of space is not evidence of absence it is evidence of transcendence.

abstract: This work demonstrates that the Stellar–to–Halo Mass Relation (SHMR) across cosmic time encodes the same universal coherence threshold predicted by the Relational Thermodynamic Layered Index (RTLI). Using the SHMR parameters (A, M_{\rm A}, \beta, \gamma) from nine redshift bins, I construct coherence curves \eta(M_h,z) and identify a stable structural transition aligned with the SHMR knee mass. The analysis reveals four core RTLI signatures: Universal Coherence Threshold: The SHMR inflection point corresponds to a stable coherence boundary, consistent with the RTLI critical threshold \eta_{\rm crit} \approx 1.7. Mass–Coherence Ratio: The stellar-mass amplification across the transition yields R_{\rm mass} \approx 1.6–2.0, matching the universal RTLI corridor (\sim 1.7) observed across CMB, SPARC rotation curves, BAO structure, and prior RTLI simulations. Slope Bifurcation: The SHMR slopes show the expected quantum–geometric asymmetry, with \beta/\gamma \approx 1.5–1.8, in agreement with RTLI’s predicted coherence asymmetry. Variance–Fold Signature: The variance of the coherence proxy \eta exhibits a sharp minimum preceding the transition, followed by rapid growth—mirroring the RTLI variance-collapse behavior. These results show that galaxy formation efficiency inherits a universal geometric constraint, linking stellar assembly, dark-matter halo growth, and large-scale cosmic coherence through a single relational principle. The SHMR thus provides a strong astrophysical confirmation of the RTLI framework.

title: Pyrgus andromedae (Wallengren, 1853)
Controlling Data Systematics in Euclid Spectroscopy with Simulations and Observations
abstract: Parallel talk presented at the XXI International Workshop on Neutrino Telescopes - Padova 29 September - 3 October 2025 (https://agenda.infn.it/event/44606/) Abstract: Euclid is a mission of the European Space Agency (ESA), designed to investigate the content and evolution of the Universe. Launched in July 2023, the satellite will collect data for at least six years, covering one-third of the sky. Euclid holds the promise to provide crucial new constraints on relevant cosmological parameters, including the sum of the neutrino masses. Accurate cosmological inference from Euclid data requires careful treatment of observational systematics, which could bias the measured galaxy distribution and distort parameter estimation. Galaxy clustering analyses, in particular, depend on a detailed understanding of the purity and completeness of the cosmological sample. The idea is to assess these properties using two complementary approaches: simulations and deep observations of reference fields. While simulations offer a controlled environment with known inputs, they must be computationally efficient and account for instrumental effects that are not fully understood. Indeed, certain detector non-idealities, such as persistence and snowballs, remain difficult to model accurately, limiting the realism of such simulations. However, deeper observations are confined to small sky regions and present complex selection functions, limiting their representativeness of the data sample. We first present a fully simulated pipeline to assess the systematic effects, such as spectral overlap, which is one of the main challenges of Euclid's slitless spectroscopic technique. We also present a complementary approach in which we simulate only the spectra; those are then injected into real Euclid images and then processed through the full data pipeline. This method naturally inherits instrumental systematics from real data, offering a more realistic characterisation of purity and completeness. Though computationally intensive, it enables the assessment of systematics over larger sky areas and provides a valuable complementary strategy for robust cosmological analyses and neutrino mass investigations.

title: RTLI Coherence Structure in the Stellar–to–Halo Mass Relation: A Universal 1.7 Threshold Across Cosmic Time
abstract: This work demonstrates that the Stellar–to–Halo Mass Relation (SHMR) across cosmic time encodes the same universal coherence threshold predicted by the Relational Thermodynamic Layered Index (RTLI). Using the SHMR parameters (A, M_{\rm A}, \beta, \gamma) from nine redshift bins, I construct coherence curves \eta(M_h,z) and identify a stable structural transition aligned with the SHMR knee mass. The analysis reveals four core RTLI signatures: Universal Coherence Threshold: The SHMR inflection point corresponds to a stable coherence boundary, consistent with the RTLI critical threshold \eta_{\rm crit} \approx 1.7. Mass–Coherence Ratio: The stellar-mass amplification across the transition yields R_{\rm mass} \approx 1.6–2.0, matching the universal RTLI corridor (\sim 1.7) observed across CMB, SPARC rotation curves, BAO structure, and prior RTLI simulations. Slope Bifurcation: The SHMR slopes show the expected quantum–geometric asymmetry, with \beta/\gamma \approx 1.5–1.8, in agreement with RTLI’s predicted coherence asymmetry. Variance–Fold Signature: The variance of the coherence proxy \eta exhibits a sharp minimum preceding the transition, followed by rapid growth—mirroring the RTLI variance-collapse behavior. These results show that galaxy formation efficiency inherits a universal geometric constraint, linking stellar assembly, dark-matter halo growth, and large-scale cosmic coherence through a single relational principle. The SHMR thus provides a strong astrophysical confirmation of the RTLI framework.

Predictive two-loop fractional-order control law for industry-oriented integrating type chemical processes and reactors
abstract: Abstract Integrating processes with time delays is commonly found in many industrial systems, especially in chemical, thermal, and fluid-level applications. These processes pose significant control challenges due to their inherent tendency toward instability and their delayed response to input changes. For such processes, 1-degree-of-freedom (1-DOF) controllers have limitations: either they are capable of providing good set-point tracking or disturbance rejection, but not both. This paper presents a Smith-predictor-based effective two-loop fractional-order control law for such processes. Here, a fractional-order PD controller is employed in the inner loop to provide stability and robustness, while an outer loop controller is designed to control the entire inner loop, thereby achieving a desirable closed-loop response. A set-point filter is also employed in the framework to minimize overshoot in set-point tracking, which may be caused by a sudden change in the set point. The controllers are tuned using stability margin and maximum sensitivity (Ms) criteria, and analytical solutions for the same are derived. The proposed control law is evaluated through theoretical analysis and simulations on various chemical process models, including a heat exchanger, a distillation column, a continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR), and a boiler steam drum. In addition, robust stability analysis confirms stable performance even under parametric uncertainties. Finally, a performance comparison is presented based on different error indices.

abstract: We present a novel black hole formation and evolution scenario within the frame-work of stiffness field cosmology, where both the effective gravitational constant andthe universal maximum energy density increase monotonically with cosmic time. Inthis picture, black holes do not form simultaneously across mass scales, but insteademerge in a stratified sequence with redshift: superheavy bodies collapse first at highredshift and produce extremely energetic outflows, while lower-mass black holes formonly later, with progressively weaker emission. The excess-energy ejection causedby surpassing the epoch-dependent density limit provides a unified explanation forthe extreme luminosity of early quasars, the decline of AGN activity toward thepresent epoch, and the redshift evolution of relativistic jets.

title: TACHYONIC FIELD CONDENSATION AS A COSMOLOGICAL SOURCE OF DARK MATTER
abstract: We present the tachyonic dark matter condensation model by connecting it explicitly tocosmology, structure formation, and observational signatures. An initially tachyonic scalarfield with a negative mass-squared term condenses into a stable vacuum through symmetrybreaking. After condensation, small excitations acquire a positive mass and behave as cold,gravitationally clustering dark matter. We show how the model integrates consistently withFLRW cosmology, affects the matter power spectrum, modifies small-scale structure, andmay leave observable imprints. Practical uses in cosmology, astrophysics, computation, and laboratory analogs are discussed

title: RPM DISPLAY FOR BLDC MOTOR WITH SPEED CONTROLLER USING ARDUINO UNO
abstract: This project presents a real-time RPM monitoring and control system for a BLDC motor using the Arduino UNO. The motor speed is measured using a Hall-effect sensor, IR sensor, or optical encoder that produces pulses during rotation. The Arduino counts these pulses to calculate RPM, which is shown on a 16×2 LCD or OLED display. Speed control is achieved through a PWM signal generated by the Arduino and supplied to an ESC or motor driver. A potentiometer allows manual adjustment of the motor speed. The system is designed to be low-cost, efficient, and suitable for applications requiring accurate and reliable BLDC motor control.

title: A Novel Data-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach for Voltage Control Under Weak Grid Support
abstract: To address active voltage control in photovoltaic (PV)-integrated distribution networks characterized by weak voltage support conditions, this paper proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL)-based coordinated control method for PV clusters. First, the voltage control problem is formulated as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP), and a centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) framework is adopted, enabling each inverter to make independent decisions based solely on local measurements during the execution phase. To balance voltage compliance with energy efficiency, two barrier functions are designed to reshape the reward function, introducing an adaptive penalization mechanism: a steeper gradient in violation region to accelerate voltage recovery to the nominal range, and a gentler gradient in the safe region to minimize excessive reactive regulation and power losses. Furthermore, six representative MADRL algorithms—COMA, IDDPG, MADDPG, MAPPO, SQDDPG, and MATD3—are employed to solve the active voltage control problem of the distribution network. Case studies based on a modified IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate that the proposed framework ensures voltage compliance while effectively reducing network losses. The MADDPG algorithm achieves a Controllability Ratio (CR) of 91.9% while maintaining power loss at approximately 0.0695 p.u., demonstrating superior convergence and robustness. Comparisons with optimal power flow (OPF) and droop control methods confirm that the proposed approach significantly improves voltage stability and energy efficiency under model-free and communication-constrained weak grid conditions.

title: Design and Validation of a Mamdani-Type Fuzzy Inference System for Dynamic Indoor Climate Balancing
abstract: The goal of this research is the design, simulation, and validation of a stable and energy-efficient Mamdani-type-1 FLC that controls an indoor climate balancing system by overcoming the drawbacks of conventional linear control in handling the intrinsic nonlinearity and complexity of the system. The main objective will be to dynamically control crucial climate parameters such as Fan Speed and Cooling Rate based on crisp input values of Temperature in the range [8 44] and Relative Humidity in the range [0 90]. The operational intelligence of the FLC relies on a comprehensive fuzzy rule base of thirty-five (35) IF-THEN rules that connect seven fuzzy sets for temperature and five for humidity to their corresponding output actions. The simulation also highlights the capability of the FLC to smoothly offer nonlinear control transitions from minimum to maximum effort, thus avoiding abrupt on/off behavior that wastes energy. This research validates the FLC as an effective, feasible, and energy-efficient control solution, laying a very firm foundation for further research.

title: Development of Walrus Optimization Algorithm-Tuned Integral-Proportional Derivative Temperature Control for Cashew-Kernel Dryer
abstract: Precise temperature control in cashew kernel drying is critical for achieving the required 5% final moisture content while preventing roasting, discoloration, and overall quality degradation; however, conventional PID controllers often struggle to maintain this precision due to the nonlinear and time-varying behaviour of batch drying systems. To overcome these limitations, this study develops a Walrus Optimization Algorithm (WaOA)-tuned Integral–Proportional Derivative (I-PD) controller specifically designed for cashew kernel dryers. The drying process was modelled using Fick’s equation, and WaOA was employed to optimally tune the controller parameters. The performance of the proposed controller was compared with MATLAB-tuned PID, MATLAB-tuned I-PD, and Ziegler–Nichols PID controllers in MATLAB R2021a SIMULINK using rise time, settling time, steady-state error, and maximum overshoot as evaluation metrics. The WaOA-tuned I-PD controller achieved a rise time of 0.0479 s, settling time of 0.1398 s, and overshoot of 0.6672, outperforming all comparative controllers in stability and transient response. These findings demonstrate the potential of bio-inspired optimization techniques for enhancing temperature regulation in agricultural drying systems.

title: Transformers are Universal Approximators of Sequence-to-Sequence Functions
abstract: This paper investigates the capacity of Transformer networks to approximate any continuous sequence-to-sequence function. We present a theoretical framework demonstrating that Transformers, with sufficient architectural capacity, can uniformly approximate any such function to arbitrary precision. Our analysis leverages concepts from functional analysis and approximation theory, extending existing results on the universal approximation capabilities of feedforward neural networks to the more complex Transformer architecture. We explore the role of key components, including attention mechanisms and feedforward layers, in enabling this approximation property. Furthermore, we provide insights into the required network size and training data characteristics necessary to achieve effective approximation in practice. Empirical results on a range of sequence-to-sequence tasks, including machine translation and time series prediction, corroborate our theoretical findings, highlighting the practical relevance of Transformers as universal approximators.

title: Aircraft Stability and Safety: Practical Applications of Control Lyapunov and Barrier Functions
abstract: Ensuring stability and safety is an indispensable priority in the aerospace industry, even though the persistent loss of control remains a major cause of fatal accidents. Hence, the necessity of flight envelope protection algorithms arises to prevent an aircraft from deviating from a safe and reliable flight regime. Within this context, the designs of control Lyapunov functions and control barrier functions are discussed to address the stability and safety issues of an aircraft. The stability of the aircraft during agile and abrupt maneuvers is guaranteed through the use of a control Lyapunov function, while safety is maintained by the flight envelope protection algorithm designed with control barrier functions specific to the angular rates, angle of attack, and load factor. The mathematical derivations of the control Lyapunov function and control barrier functions are presented. The efficacy of the proposed structure is demonstrated through simulations under various circumstances using a 6-degree-of-freedom nonlinear flight dynamics model, and consequently, the promising features of the control Lyapunov function and control barrier function in mitigating the loss of control are discussed.

title: Practical Predefined-Time Sliding-Mode Adaptive Resilient Control for PMSM Cyber–Physical Systems
abstract: The permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is extensively utilized in the power drive systems of Cyber–Physical Systems (CPSs). In scenarios where control signals are subjected to malicious attacks within the network, ensuring that the PMSM achieves its designated speed within a specified timeframe serves as a critical metric for evaluating the efficacy of security control strategies in networked systems. To address practical challenges arising from updates to controlled objects at the physical layer and limitations of control layer algorithms—wherein convergence time for system trajectory tracking errors (TTEors) may extend indefinitely—we have developed a novel resilient control algorithm with predefined-time convergence (PreTC) tailored for uncertain PMSMs susceptible to cyber threats. Firstly, we introduce an innovative Lyapunov stability criterion characterized by an adjustable gain reaching law alongside PreTC. Following this, we design an SMS (SMS) that incorporates PreTC and employ an extreme learning machine (ELM) to facilitate real-time identification of both physical layer models and malicious cyber-attacks. A sliding-mode adaptive resilient controller devoid of explicit physical model information is proposed for CPSs, with Lyapunov stability theory substantiating the system’s predefined-time (PDT) stability. This significantly enhances resilience against malicious cyber-attacks and other uncertainties. Finally, comparative simulations involving four distinct resilient control algorithms demonstrate that our proposed algorithm not only guarantees predetermined convergence times but also exhibits robust resistance to cyber-attacks, parameter perturbations, and external disturbances—notably achieving a motor speed tracking error accuracy of 0.008. These findings validate the superior robustness and effectiveness of our control algorithm against malicious cyber threats.

Preferential Taxation and the Retained Earnings Bias: A Premise-Conditions Theory
abstract: This paper formalizes a premise-conditions theory explaining why preferential tax incentives for large firms (e.g., investment tax credits, accelerated depreciation) do not translate into domestic capital deepening or wage growth but instead raise retained earnings and shareholder payouts. The mechanism hinges on cross-border return differentials, governance priorities, and tax arbitrage constraints. We derive testable implications and policy diagnostics under which GDP fails to increase while GNI and payouts rise. The model extends the classical user cost of capital framework (Jorgenson, Hall-Jorgenson) by incorporating governance bias and cross-border leakage, and is supported by empirical evidence from the United States, Japan, and Germany. This work contributes to the institutional diagnosis of tax policy and proposes a standardized theoretical framework for evaluating preferential taxation outcomes. To ensure global applicability, we extend the diagnostic framework into a standardized international filing regime. Firms applying for preferential tax treatment would be required to submit harmonized disclosure forms detailing domestic and foreign after‑tax return rates, retained earnings growth, and shareholder payout ratios. Refunds or credits would be granted only when inequality conditions demonstrate that domestic investment contributes positively to GDP rather than merely increasing GNI or retained earnings. All submitted data would be published in an open‑access repository, enabling independent verification by researchers, civil society, and international organizations. By embedding transparency and comparability, this regime transforms preferential taxation from a blanket subsidy into a conditional, evidence‑based instrument, aligning fiscal incentives with genuine national income growth and preventing recurrent policy failures. In practice, rigid threshold rules risk creating inequities when domestic and foreign return differentials hover near the boundary. To safeguard fairness while preserving diagnostic rigor, the framework should employ smoothing techniques such as frequency‑domain (FD) filtering or Gaussian‑based weighting. Instead of granting or denying preferential treatment on the basis of a single estimate, eligibility would be proportionally scaled to the probability that domestic after‑tax returns exceed foreign alternatives within a rolling window. This probabilistic design mitigates short‑term volatility and measurement error, ensuring that firms with sustained domestic contributions receive full benefits, while those relying on temporary or noisy advantages obtain reduced support. By embedding statistical smoothing into credit allocation, the regime reconciles theoretical precision with operational equity, avoids cliff‑edge outcomes, and strengthens the legitimacy of preferential taxation as a conditional, evidence‑driven policy instrument.

title: Optimal design of a robot gripper arm using the chaotic animated oat optimizer
abstract: Abstract This study presents a modified version of the Animated Oat Algorithm (AOA), enhanced through the integration of chaotic maps, termed the Chaotic Animated Oat Algorithm (CAOA). Inspired by the seed dispersal mechanisms of the oat plant, AOA offers a population-based metaheuristic framework suitable for complex global optimization tasks. The proposed CAOA was evaluated across four real-world engineering optimization problems: pressure vessel design, bolted rim coupling, gear train cost minimization, and robot gripper arm weight reduction. Results demonstrate that CAOA consistently outperforms traditional and state-of-the-art metaheuristics in terms of solution quality, convergence stability, and robustness, affirming its potential for widespread engineering applications.
