title: The Mechanization of Kosmos: From Milesian *Arche* to Atomist Materialism
abstract: This paper explores the conceptual evolution in early Greek philosophy from the Milesian pursuit of a singular, foundational *arche* to the robust mechanistic materialism of the Atomists. Beginning with Thales, Anaximander, and Anaximenes, who posited fundamental principles like water, the apeiron, and air as the origin and substance of the cosmos, the study traces how these initial monistic and often animated conceptions of reality gradually paved the way for more complex, pluralistic explanations. It then delves into the intervening philosophical developments, including the Eleatic challenge to change and the early pluralists Empedocles and Anaxagoras, before culminating in the atomic theory of Leucippus and Democritus. The Atomists' radical proposition of an infinite number of indivisible particles (atoms) moving in an infinite void, governed solely by mechanical collision and necessity, represents a profound desacralization and mechanization of the *kosmos*. This intellectual journey illustrates a fundamental shift in understanding the universe, moving from an intrinsically living or divinely imbued principle to a system explainable purely by the motion and interaction of inert matter. This paper offers a systematic conceptual analysis, illuminating the precise philosophical innovations at each stage that progressively eroded vitalistic explanations and redefined causality, culminating in the Atomists' purely mechanical universe, thereby laying crucial groundwork for later scientific and materialist thought.

title: Industrial Metabolism: Rethinking Energy, Materiality, and Labor in the First Global Transformation
abstract: This paper re-examines the First Global Transformation, conventionally known as the Industrial Revolution, through the analytical lens of industrial metabolism. Moving beyond traditional narratives focused on technological invention and economic growth, we foreground the intricate, systemic interdependencies between energy flows, material throughputs, and the reorganization of labor. By conceptualizing industrial society as a metabolic system, we analyze how the shift from animate to inanimate energy sources, particularly coal, profoundly reshaped global material chains, intensified resource extraction, and fundamentally restructured human work and social relations. This approach reveals the deep historical roots of contemporary socio-ecological challenges, demonstrating how the metabolic paradigm established during this transformative era initiated patterns of resource depletion, environmental degradation, and societal inequalities that continue to define our modern world. We argue that understanding this foundational metabolic shift is crucial for comprehending the historical trajectory of human-environment interactions and for informing pathways toward more sustainable industrial practices.

title: The Second Metabolism: Engineering, Energy, and the Accelerated Human Condition (1870-1914)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of the "Second Metabolism" to analyze the profound transformations of human existence between 1870 and 1914. This period, characterized by the peak of the Second Industrial Revolution, witnessed an unprecedented acceleration of technological innovation and energy exploitation, primarily through coal, petroleum, and electricity. The "Second Metabolism" posits that human societies, individually and collectively, began to internalize and externalize these new energy regimes, moving beyond biological metabolism to a state where engineered systems and vast energy inputs became extensions of human function and desire. This study explores how advancements in engineering, from the internal combustion engine to electrified urban grids, reshaped temporal and spatial perceptions, intensified labor, created new forms of leisure, and ultimately forged an accelerated human condition. By examining primary historical sources and drawing upon an interdisciplinary framework encompassing the history of technology, energy studies, and cultural history, this paper demonstrates how the period's material and energetic shifts fundamentally rewired societal rhythms and individual experiences, laying the groundwork for modern hyper-connectivity and speed.

title: Metabolic Reframing: Secondary Products and the Deepening of Human-Animal Entanglement
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of "metabolic reframing" to analyze the profound shifts in human-animal relationships throughout history, particularly focusing on the utilization of secondary animal products. Historically, early human-animal interactions primarily revolved around the direct consumption of primary products such as meat and hides. However, the advent of domestication marked a pivotal transition, prompting a re-evaluation of animal utility beyond immediate slaughter. Metabolic reframing describes the innovative human capacity to harness the ongoing biological processes of living animals – their lactation cycles, hair growth, waste production, and locomotive power – as renewable resources. This conceptual shift enabled the extraction of "secondary products" like milk, wool, labor, and manure, which fundamentally altered human subsistence strategies, economic structures, and social organization. By integrating these continuous metabolic outputs into human systems, a new era of intensified and multifaceted human-animal entanglement emerged. This paper argues that the exploitation of secondary products represents a deeper form of co-evolution and niche construction, leading to complex interdependencies that have shaped both human biological and cultural evolution, as well as the genetic and phenotypic landscapes of domesticated species. We explore the archaeological, genetic, and anthropological evidence for this reframing, demonstrating its pivotal role in the development of agriculture, the rise of pastoralism, and the enduring legacy of human-animal partnerships.

title: The Forced Efficiency Dislocation (DEF) Model: An Analytical Framework for Technology, Efficiency, and State Sovereignty in the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Preliminary Version - English translation)
abstract: This article is an English translation of the original preprint "The Forced Efficiency Dislocation (DEF) Model: An Analytical Framework for Technology, Efficiency, and State Sovereignty in the Fourth Industrial Revolution", first published on November 22, 2025, and available under the DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17677617. The purpose of this translation is to broaden the international debate on the relationship between technological efficiency, state sovereignty, and institutional fragmentation. A definitive and expanded version of this model will be published in the author’s forthcoming book, "Jevons’ Paradox and the Dislocation of the Nation-State in the Fourth Industrial Revolution: A Forced Efficiency Dislocation (DEF) Model". This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0), which allows for free access and citation but prohibits commercial use and modifications." The DEF Model is an original theoretical framework that examines how Jevons’ paradox, in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR), triggers a process of state capacity dislocation. Building on Nathan Wachtel’s (1976) concept of dislocation—where institutional structures persist in contexts that no longer provide their original coherence—the model integrates insights from Foucault (power mechanisms), Castells (global flows), and Latour (technopolitical materiality). It demonstrates how technological efficiency, when imposed as the supreme criterion, fragments state sovereignty through four key mechanisms: Technocratization of governance, Externalization of sovereignty, Normalization of networked subjectivity, and Dematerialization of the public sphere. By linking Jevons’ paradox with Wachtel’s dislocation, the DEF Model explains how the pursuit of efficiency subordinates the state’s regulatory capacity to technocratic and corporate logics, ultimately eroding traditional forms of sovereignty.

title: The Weak Garden's Precarity: Resource Scarcity and the Shaping of Early Human Societies
abstract: Early human societies navigated complex and often precarious environmental landscapes, where resource availability was rarely constant or guaranteed. This paper introduces the concept of the "Weak Garden" to characterize environments that, while potentially rich, were inherently unstable or susceptible to fluctuations, thereby imposing significant pressures on foraging populations. We argue that resource scarcity, far from being a mere impediment, acted as a fundamental evolutionary and cultural driver, profoundly shaping the social structures, technological innovations, migratory patterns, and cooperative strategies of early humans during the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods. Drawing on archaeological, paleoenvironmental, and anthropological evidence, this study explores how the continuous threat of scarcity fostered adaptive responses, including the development of complex foraging strategies, food storage techniques, social networks for risk-sharing, and territoriality. Understanding the "Weak Garden's" influence provides crucial insights into the deep origins of human resilience, adaptability, and the foundational aspects of our collective social organization, highlighting how environmental constraints catalyzed the very foundations of human civilization.

title: La ley del descenso tendencial de la tasa de ganancia: Evidencia empírica para la economía española
abstract: This article examines the law of the tendency of the rate of profit to fall in the Spanish economy between 1960 and 2024, considering the organic composition of capital and the rate of surplus value as central variables. Its aim is to determine whether this law, formulated by Marx in Capital (Vol. III), continues to operate in the contemporary context. The methodology consists of transforming orthodox macroeconomic categories derived from the Spanish National Accounts (CNE), available in BDMACRO, into Marxist variables: constant capital ($c$), variable capital ($v$), and surplus value ($pv$). Based on these, historical series of the organic composition of capital ($q$), the rate of surplus value ($pv'$), and the rate of profit ($g'$) are constructed, adjusted to constant prices to ensure temporal coherence and comparability. The results show a sustained increase in $q$ and a slight decrease in $pv'$, generating a tendential decline in $g'$ with cyclical fluctuations associated with specific crises. The conclusions empirically confirm the validity of the law in Spain, highlighting the historical limits of capitalism and providing quantitative evidence on the structural dynamics of profitability.

title: Curve Fingerprints for GPU Systems: Compact Diagnostics for Training and Architecture
abstract: This note proposes curve fingerprints as a lightweight way to summarize GPU behavior using small bundles of diagnostic curves instead of single scalar metrics. Modern GPU systems produce rich telemetry during training and profiling, but most decisions still rely on averages such as throughput, utilization, and wall-clock time. These aggregates often hide subtle regressions, stability issues, and changes in how real workloads stress the hardware. The method defines a finite bundle of one-dimensional curves, Theta, built entirely from existing logs and counters (loss, step time, utilization, stall reasons, bandwidth, temperature, power, error events). Two main bundles are considered: – Theta_train, which captures training stability and efficiency (for example, loss volatility vs smoothing scale, utilization vs batch size or sequence length, and step-time distribution curves). – Theta_arch / Theta_stress, which characterize how workloads interact with the hardware (for example, stall composition vs load, bandwidth and cache curves vs problem size, and thermal–power envelopes over time). The paper describes how to construct these curves from standard telemetry, how to compare fingerprints across runs and systems, and how vendors or large users could integrate them into existing ROCm-like toolchains. Example applications include nightly or weekly regression testing, performance engineering workflows, and architecture evaluation across GPU generations. The goal is practical: a thin, vendor-neutral layer that can be dropped onto current logging and profiling pipelines to provide durable, comparable signal about how GPU systems actually behave over time, without requiring new hardware sensors or complex models.

title: Modular Isomorphism in Artificial Intelligence: From the Ring Z/6Z to Shared-Nothing Architecture NPUs
abstract: The scalability of Deep Learning models faces physical limits within the monolithic Von Neumann architecture, where the energy cost of data movement exceeds computation. This work proposes a solution based on Modular Isomorphism under the ring Z/6Z, allowing the decomposition of dense neural networks into a hexagonal ensemble of six independent sub-networks. We experimentally validate this approach on MNIST (97.03% accuracy) and Transformers (94.75% validation accuracy), demonstrating that the Shared-Nothing architecture maintains competitive performance while eliminating the need for low-latency interconnects. A Monte Carlo robustness analysis (N=10) confirms the statistical significance (p < 0.012) of the Inverse Generalization Gap reduction, where the modular architecture acts as a strong structural regularizer. The economic analysis reveals 18× cost reductions via node arbitrage, utilizing mature 28nm technology versus state-of-the-art 3nm processes. These results lay the foundation for a new generation of modular NPUs based on low-cost chiplets, democratizing access to high-performance computing. Repository Contents This repository contains the reference implementation and validation experiments: Source Code: PyTorch implementation of the Hex-Ensemble architecture and Stride-6 modular projection. Validation Notebooks: Reproducible experiments for Tensor Isomorphism, MNIST classification, and Modular Transformers. Statistical Analysis: Monte Carlo robustness tests verifying the inverse generalization gap. Keywords Modular NPU, Shared-Nothing Architecture, Chiplets, Modular Isomorphism, Inverse Generalization, Sustainable Computing, Z/6Z, Green AI.

By linking Jevons’ paradox with Wachtel’s dislocation, the DEF Model explains how the pursuit of efficiency subordinates the state’s regulatory capacity to technocratic and corporate logics, ultimately eroding traditional forms of sovereignty.

title: Metabolic Reframing: Secondary Products and the Deepening of Human-Animal Entanglement
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of "metabolic reframing" to analyze the profound shifts in human-animal relationships throughout history, particularly focusing on the utilization of secondary animal products. Historically, early human-animal interactions primarily revolved around the direct consumption of primary products such as meat and hides. However, the advent of domestication marked a pivotal transition, prompting a re-evaluation of animal utility beyond immediate slaughter. Metabolic reframing describes the innovative human capacity to harness the ongoing biological processes of living animals – their lactation cycles, hair growth, waste production, and locomotive power – as renewable resources. This conceptual shift enabled the extraction of "secondary products" like milk, wool, labor, and manure, which fundamentally altered human subsistence strategies, economic structures, and social organization. By integrating these continuous metabolic outputs into human systems, a new era of intensified and multifaceted human-animal entanglement emerged. This paper argues that the exploitation of secondary products represents a deeper form of co-evolution and niche construction, leading to complex interdependencies that have shaped both human biological and cultural evolution, as well as the genetic and phenotypic landscapes of domesticated species. We explore the archaeological, genetic, and anthropological evidence for this reframing, demonstrating its pivotal role in the development of agriculture, the rise of pastoralism, and the enduring legacy of human-animal partnerships.

title: The Bifurcation to Industry: A Dynamical Systems Analysis of Economic Transformation
abstract: This paper explores economic transformation, specifically the transition from agrarian or pre-industrial states to industrialized economies, through the lens of dynamical systems theory. We propose that industrialization is not merely a gradual progression but rather a complex, nonlinear process characterized by critical thresholds and bifurcation points. By constructing a theoretical model incorporating key economic variables such as capital accumulation, technological innovation, human capital development, and institutional quality, we analyze how various feedback mechanisms can drive an economy towards distinct developmental trajectories. The study identifies conditions under which an economy may undergo a qualitative change in its dynamics, leading to a "bifurcation" where it either accelerates towards sustained industrial growth or remains trapped in a lower-level equilibrium. We investigate the roles of positive feedback loops in technological adoption and human capital formation, as well as the impact of external shocks and policy interventions in triggering or hindering this bifurcation. The findings suggest that understanding these nonlinear dynamics is crucial for designing effective development policies, moving beyond linear growth models to embrace the inherent complexity and path dependence of economic evolution.

title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Feudal Systems: A Network Perspective on Power and Production
abstract: This paper explores the evolutionary dynamics of feudal systems through the lens of network theory, focusing on the intricate relationships of power and production. Feudalism, characterized by decentralized authority and reciprocal obligations centered on land tenure, presents a rich historical case study for network analysis. We conceptualize feudal society as a complex adaptive network where lords, vassals, and peasants represent nodes, and relationships such as land grants, military service, labor obligations, and resource flows constitute the edges. By employing network metrics, this study aims to uncover patterns of power distribution, identify critical dependencies within the agrarian economy, and analyze the mechanisms of stability and change that governed these historical systems. We investigate how variations in network structure, such as centrality of key lords or the density of vassalage ties, influenced regional resilience, economic output, and susceptibility to internal and external shocks. Furthermore, the paper models the co-evolution of social hierarchies and productive capacities, shedding light on how shifts in agricultural technology or trade networks could induce profound structural transformations within the feudal system. This network perspective offers a novel framework for understanding the emergence, persistence, and eventual decline of feudalism, providing quantitative insights into historical political economy and social organization.

title: Marxist Philosophy and Sustainable Economic Development
abstract: This paper explores the relationship between Marxist philosophy and the concept of sustainable economic development, emphasizing how Marxist principles provide a theoretical framework to address economic, social, and environmental challenges in the context of globalization. The analysis focuses on core concepts such as relations of production, class struggle, and surplus value, while linking them to the requirements of sustainable development, including social equity, environmental protection, and economic efficiency. The paper argues that Marxist philosophy not only offers a critical lens to analyze current economic development models but also proposes potential solutions to guide sustainable development in the future. The findings suggest that applying Marxist principles can help restructure economic policies to achieve a balance between economic growth and ecosystem preservation.

title: Money as a Disrupted Rhythm of Science: How the Startup Model Creates Pseudoevolution Instead of Progress
abstract: This essay argues that modern science is increasingly driven by financial pressure rather than genuine discovery. The startup investment model imposes rapid cycles, predictable outcomes, and marketing-oriented narratives onto a domain that fundamentally requires slow rhythm, uncertainty, and long-term thinking. When the natural rhythm of scientific inquiry is disrupted, research enters a state of pseudoevolution — fast, chaotic, and directionless activity that mimics progress but does not produce true advancement. Investors believe they support innovation, yet often unknowingly finance the collapse of scientific rhythm and the erosion of authentic discovery.

title: Vocational, Economic and Life Care Planning in the Era of COVID-19
abstract: The year 2020 was unprecedented for many reasons. Few events in the past century have been more novel and far-reaching than the emergence and rapid spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the virus that causes Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). This pandemic caused significant changes in the ways we socialize, work and communicate. It also created economic strain in many sectors and, by extension, reshaped and reconfigured the workplace. Many employers have drastically altered their operations while others were forced out of business. The overall impact of job losses cannot be understated. With mass COVID-19 vaccinations underway, there remain many questions about the long-term implications of the global pandemic. This paper examines data from the pandemic of 1918, the impacts of economic recessions, contemporary data on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and attempts to extrapolate implications for future vocational, economic and life care planning analyses.

title: From Depression to Dictatorship: How the Great Crisis Engineered the Parallel Rise of Mussolini, Hitler, Stalin, and Franco (1929‑1939)
abstract: The Great Depression created severe economic distress across Europe. This paper asks how that distress enabled the simultaneous rise of four authoritarian regimes: Mussolini, Hitler, Stalin and Franco. Using a composite Crisis Intensity Index (CII) and systematic content analysis of party manifestos and speeches, we analyse 4 cases and 120 annual observations. We find that (1) sharp rises in unemployment, deflation and output contraction predict rapid gains for extremist parties; (2) each leader framed the crisis as a national emergency and blamed external or internal enemies; and (3) state‑directed economic programmes were paired with systematic repression to consolidate power. The results clarify mechanisms that link macro‑economic crises to authoritarian consolidation and suggest how similar dynamics might operate in contemporary crises.

title: Causes of Failure of the Phillips Curve: Does Tranquillity of Economic Environment Matter?
abstract: Although empirical literature regarding the Phillips curve is sizeable enough, there is still no wide consensus on its validity and stability. The literature shows that the Phillips relationship is fragile and varies across countries and time periods; a statistical relationship that appears strong during one decade (country) may be weak the next (other). This variability might have some grounds for idiosyncrasy of a country and its economic environment. To address it, this paper scrutinizes the Phillips relationship over 41 countries over the period 1980-2016, paying attention to how inflation dynamics behave during tranquil and recessionary periods. As a result, the paper confirms the variability of the Phillips relationship across countries, as well as time periods. It documents that the relationship holds in the majority of developed countries, while it fails to hold in emerging and frontier economies during tranquil periods. On the other hand, the relationship totally collapses during recessionary periods, even in developed markets. This shows that tranquillity of economic environment is significantly important for the Phillip trade-off to work smoothly. Moreover, both backward- and forward-looking fractions of inflation remarkably increase during recessionary periods as a result of the Phillips coefficient loses its significance within the model. This indicates that markets become more inflation-sensitive during these periods.

title: Exchange rate regime flexibility and firms’ employment
Türkiye’de Döviz Kuru Enflasyon Geçişkenliği: Dalgacık Kantil Modellerle Bir Araştırma
abstract: Bu çalışma, Türkiye'de döviz kuru dalgalanmalarının enflasyon üzerindeki asimetrik ve zamanla değişen etkilerini USD/TRY ve EUR/TRY döviz kurlarına odaklanarak incelemektedir. Çalışmada, 2003M1-2024M12 arasındaki aylık veriler kullanılarak, farklı zaman boyutlarında ve kantillerde döviz kurları ve enflasyon arasındaki dinamik ilişkiyi araştırmak için dalgacık kantil regresyonu (DKR) ve dalgacık kantil korelasyonu (DKK) yöntemleri kullanılmıştır. Bulgular, özellikle kısa vadede ve alt ve orta kantillerde, genel olarak pozitif ve istatistiksel olarak anlamlı bir döviz kuru geçişkenliği (DKGE) ortaya koymaktadır. Hem USD hem de EUR dalgalanmaları enflasyon üzerinde ölçülebilir bir etki sergilemekte, etkiler daha yüksek kantillerde ve uzun vadede azalmaktadır. Sonuçlar, DKGE mekanizmasında doğrusal olmama ve asimetrinin varlığını doğrulamakta ve gelişmekte olan ekonomilere ilişkin literatürdeki önceki bulgularla tutarlılık göstermektedir. Çalışma, dış şoklardan kaynaklanan enflasyonist baskıların azaltılmasında döviz kuru istikrarının, etkin enflasyon hedeflemesinin ve ithalat çeşitlendirmesinin önemini vurgulamaktadır. Gelişmiş kantil tabanlı dalgacık tekniklerinin uygulanması, kur hareketlerine tepki olarak Türkiye'nin enflasyon dinamiklerinin detaylı bir şekilde anlaşılmasını sağlamaktadır.

title: Nonlinear State Transitions under Geopolitical Forcing: The Meiji Restoration
abstract: The Meiji Restoration of 1868 represents a profound and rapid transformation of the Japanese state, society, and economy, conventionally understood through historical narratives emphasizing internal decay and external pressure. This paper proposes an alternative analytical framework, viewing the Meiji Restoration as a nonlinear state transition triggered by acute geopolitical forcing. Drawing upon concepts from complex systems theory, such as bifurcation points, critical junctures, and emergent properties, we analyze how the prolonged, relatively stable, but internally strained Tokugawa shogunate was pushed beyond a critical threshold by the arrival of Western powers and the subsequent imposition of unequal treaties. This external geopolitical shock acted as a powerful forcing mechanism, interacting with pre-existing internal vulnerabilities to precipitate a rapid, qualitative shift in Japan's political, economic, and social structure. We examine the interplay of internal discontent, the Sonnō jōi movement, and the coercive diplomacy of Western nations as key drivers of this transition. The paper argues that the Meiji Restoration was not merely a linear evolution but a sudden, radical reorganization of the state, demonstrating characteristics of a phase transition in a complex socio-political system. Understanding this pivotal historical event through a nonlinear lens offers new insights into the dynamics of state change and the profound impact of global power shifts on national trajectories.

Natural inflation in Palatini $F(R)$
abstract: $F(R)$ Palatini gravity provides a robust framework for constructing viable inflationary potentials. In this study, we examine natural inflation and show that its consistency with observational data can be restored when the model is embedded within $F(R)$ Palatini gravity, specifically for $F(R) = R + αR^n$ with $7/4 \lesssim n \leq 2$. For completeness, we also demonstrate that models with $n > 2$ do not yield comparable improvements, achieving partial agreement with the data only in the limit $n \rightarrow 2$.

abstract: 《莱茵报》时期是马克思思想转变的重要时期。其中的哲思活动为其实现自由观的转向奠定了重要的现实基础。虽然马克思还未对黑格尔展开深入批判，但马克思对“自由”的理解在这一时期已经开始从作为抽象存在的传统路径中逐渐脱离，转向对德国社会现实问题的关注。而就其与自由主义的关联而言，马克思对“自由问题”的理解显然已经表现出了对自由主义的反叛与超越。

title: Giffen Behavior, Income Effects and Austrian Price Theory
abstract: Abstract Austrian price theory is riddled with inconsistencies surrounding the neoclassical income effect and Giffen behavior. It has sometimes been argued that neither the income effect nor Giffen behavior exist. This paper first argues that Giffen behavior is possible and can perfectly well be explained within the framework of Austrian price theory in the tradition of Mises. Moreover, it shows that income effects are real. They are merely an outgrowth of the law of diminishing marginal utility applied to money. The paper also outlines the expenditure approach to income and substitution effects as an alternative conceptualization that does not require any reference to quantifiable and measurable notions of utility, or an unambiguous and objective notion of real income.

Persistent monetary policy in a model with involuntary unemployment
abstract: Abstract In a basic New Keynesian DSGE model with involuntary unemployment, we study the role of labor markets in the transmission of persistent monetary policy shocks that increase households' inflation expectations. The model predicts that, in contrast to the standard nominal interest rate shocks, labor market conditions can affect the outcomes of persistent monetary policy shocks suggesting a trade‐off between inflation and output growth: restricted labor market access leads to higher inflation response with smaller effects on output. Using a vector autoregression analysis, we further provide empirical evidence consistent with the predictions of our theoretical model.

title: DOES MONEY HAVE A FUTURE?
abstract: Money is one of the greatest inventions of the human mind and an effective tool of globalization. At the same time, not only monetary globalization contributes to the process of economic globalization, but globalization itself influences the change in the order of functioning of money (globalization of money), reflected in the modernization of their functions. At the heart of such modernization are the phenomena of Ddestuffation and Dereification of Money. Such changes do not change the Essence of Money, but reflect the increasing Entropy of Money, which in the case of Technological Singularity can lead to the abolition of money (which communist utopians could not achieve) as a result of Money Singularity. And yet, it seems that the Law of the Indestructibility of Money will win again.

title: News Shocks, Precautionary Saving and Frictional Labour Markets
abstract: Abstract This paper develops a theory of how TFP news shocks can impact the economy via a Keynesian supply channel. With frictional labour markets, bad TFP news reduces firms’ incentive to post vacancies, worsening households’ employment prospects. Households respond by accumulating liquid assets and cutting spending for precautionary reasons, triggering a recession that compounds the labour market downturn. This mechanism is outlined analytically and numerically in a heterogeneous agent New Keynesian model, with supporting local projection evidence. The combination of labour market frictions and precautionary saving is necessary to match the joint output and nominal interest rate dynamics observed empirically following a news shock. In contrast to previous theories, the transmission mechanism leaves room for policy to mitigate the shock’s contractionary effects.

title: LFM2 Technical Report
abstract: We present LFM2, a family of Liquid Foundation Models designed for efficient on-device deployment and strong task capabilities. Using hardware-in-the-loop architecture search under edge latency and memory constraints, we obtain a compact hybrid backbone that combines gated short convolutions with a small number of grouped query attention blocks, delivering up to 2x faster prefill and decode on CPUs compared to similarly sized models. The LFM2 family covers 350M-8.3B parameters, including dense models (350M, 700M, 1.2B, 2.6B) and a mixture-of-experts variant (8.3B total, 1.5B active), all with 32K context length. LFM2's training pipeline includes a tempered, decoupled Top-K knowledge distillation objective that avoids support mismatch; curriculum learning with difficulty-ordered data; and a three-stage post-training recipe of supervised fine-tuning, length-normalized preference optimization, and model merging. Pre-trained on 10-12T tokens, LFM2 models achieve strong results across diverse benchmarks; for example, LFM2-2.6B reaches 79.56% on IFEval and 82.41% on GSM8K. We further build multimodal and retrieval variants: LFM2-VL for vision-language tasks, LFM2-Audio for speech, and LFM2-ColBERT for retrieval. LFM2-VL supports tunable accuracy-latency tradeoffs via token-efficient visual processing, while LFM2-Audio separates audio input and output pathways to enable real-time speech-to-speech interaction competitive with models 3x larger. LFM2-ColBERT provides a low-latency encoder for queries and documents, enabling high-performance retrieval across multiple languages. All models are released with open weights and deployment packages for ExecuTorch, llama.cpp, and vLLM, making LFM2 a practical base for edge applications that need fast, memory-efficient inference and strong task capabilities.

Hilferding, Woytinsky and the Fiscal Orthodoxy of Interwar Social Democracy
abstract: Abstract In 1931, when the Great Depression hit Germany, German social democrats discussed a proposal for a proto-Keynesian public-debt financed employment programme. This was the so-called WTB plan drafted by Wladimir Woytinsky. But under the leadership of Rudolf Hilferding, the SPD rejected the proposal. This paper introduces Woytinsky and the WTB plan. It documents how Hilferding’s endorsement of the gold standard and fiscal austerity can be traced to his theoretical analysis in Finance Capital . It also shows that support for orthodox policies spanned the political spectrum and can also be found in non-Marxist socialist movements, as is illustrated by the British experience. Finally, it argues that the WTB plan represents a missed opportunity to develop a socialist Keynesianism that would have complemented the Austro-Marxist political strategy of a democratic socialism.

title: Inflation expectations and political polarization: Evidence from the cooperative election study
Monetary subordination in the Eurozone: Pillars and asymmetries
abstract: This paper explores the existence of monetary subordination in the Eurozone as an extension of the Core-Periphery approaches developed during the Eurocrisis. The analysis establishes the existence of monetary subordination in the EMU as the foundation for subordination at large. European monetary subordination is found to be supported by three pillars: the hierarchy of euro money-like balances, the nature of the euro as hybrid money and the fragmentation of the monetary jurisdictions coupled with their selective integration. To begin exploring the effects of monetary subordination, the paper introduces the analysis of the Eurozone crisis as a result of subordination coupled with deleveraging, highlighting the asymmetric impact of the latter on subordinate and non-subordinate members.

Cascade-Free Refinement: A Unified Attention-Based Framework for Sub-Millisecond, High-Accuracy Object Detection
abstract: The dual demands for high accuracy and real-time performance in object detection have historically led to architectural compromises, creating a dichotomy between fast single-stage detectors and accurate but slow two-stage or multi-stage detectors. Iterative refinement, as exemplified by cascade-based models, has proven effective at boosting accuracy but introduces significant computational latency, rendering it unsuitable for applications requiring sub-millisecond response times. This paper introduces Cascade-Free Refinement (CFR), a novel, unified framework that achieves the high accuracy of cascaded methods without their sequential processing overhead. CFR leverages a parallel, dual-stream attention mechanism that simultaneously refines object localization and contextualizes feature representations across a sparse set of object queries. By processing all queries in a single, non-recursive step, our model avoids the error propagation and latency accumulation inherent in traditional cascades. The core of our framework is a specialized attention module that performs simultaneous cross-attention to multi-scale image features for precise localization and self-attention among queries for holistic scene understanding and ambiguity resolution. This unified approach eliminates the need for separate refinement stages and complex post-processing logic like Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS). We demonstrate that on the challenging MS COCO benchmark, our CFR model, built upon a standard ResNet-50 backbone, matches the accuracy of complex cascade detectors while the core refinement module achieves an inference time below one millisecond on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. This work establishes a new frontier in the speed-accuracy trade-off, enabling a new class of real-time perception systems for robotics, autonomous navigation, and augmented reality.

title: Attentive Memory Pruning: Sparsity-Aware Optimization for Resource-Constrained AI
abstract: The escalating demand for artificial intelligence (AI) solutions in resource-constrained environments necessitates innovative approaches to model compression and optimization. Attentive Memory Pruning (AMP) introduces a novel sparsity-aware optimization technique designed to minimize the memory footprint and computational overhead of deep learning models while preserving their performance. AMP leverages an attention mechanism to identify and prune less salient memory elements within a model's architecture, guided by a sparsity-inducing regularizer during training. This approach adaptively allocates resources to the most informative features, resulting in compact and efficient models suitable for deployment on edge devices and embedded systems. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmark datasets and model architectures demonstrate that AMP achieves significant reductions in model size and computational complexity, outperforming existing pruning methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The method offers a promising pathway towards democratizing AI by enabling its deployment on a wider range of hardware platforms.

title: Flash Attention: Unlocking Bandwidth-Optimal Self-Attention for Trillion-Parameter Models
abstract: The Transformer architecture, with its cornerstone self-attention mechanism, has revolutionized deep learning, particularly in natural language processing. However, as models scale towards trillions of parameters and sequence lengths grow, the computational and memory demands of self-attention become a significant bottleneck. Standard self-attention implementations, while mathematically straightforward, are not bandwidth-optimal. They necessitate numerous reads and writes of large intermediate matrices (e.g., the attention scores matrix) to and from slow High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM), leading to underutilization of GPU computational units. This paper introduces Flash Attention, a novel algorithm that rethinks the self-attention computation to achieve true bandwidth optimality. By leveraging tiling strategies and recomputation of attention scores during the backward pass, Flash Attention drastically reduces the number of HBM accesses. Specifically, it computes attention blocks and normalizes them iteratively in fast on-chip SRAM, storing only the necessary partial sums for the final output and for the backward pass recomputation, thereby avoiding writing the entire large attention matrix to HBM. This approach yields substantial speedups in both training and inference, alongside a dramatic reduction in memory footprint. Our results demonstrate that Flash Attention enables the efficient training and deployment of models with unprecedented scales, including those approaching trillion parameters, by mitigating the critical memory bandwidth bottleneck. This innovation is pivotal for the continued advancement of large-scale deep learning models across various domains.

title: Unifying Efficiency and Expressivity: A Foundational Framework for Next-Generation Transformer Architectures
abstract: The Transformer architecture has revolutionized natural language processing and extended its influence across various machine learning domains due to its unparalleled ability to capture long-range dependencies through self-attention mechanisms. However, its quadratic computational and memory complexity with respect to sequence length presents a significant hurdle for scaling to extremely long sequences and resource-constrained environments. This paper proposes a foundational framework for next-generation Transformer architectures that explicitly aims to unify efficiency and expressivity. We introduce a multi-faceted approach incorporating adaptive sparse attention mechanisms, hierarchical processing, and dynamic token routing. The framework systematically addresses the computational bottlenecks by leveraging structured sparsity and efficient kernel designs while preserving, and in some cases enhancing, the model's capacity to learn complex relationships. We delve into the theoretical underpinnings of this unification, proposing mathematical formulations for our novel attention patterns and hierarchical aggregation strategies. Experimental evaluation, though theoretical in this exposition, envisions significant reductions in computational cost and memory footprint without compromising performance on diverse benchmark tasks, ranging from long-document understanding to high-resolution image processing. This work lays the groundwork for developing more scalable, robust, and accessible Transformer models, pushing the boundaries of what is achievable in sequence modeling and beyond.

title: Hybrid-Bitwidth Optimization: Achieving Near-Lossless int4/int8 Performance for Efficient Deep Learning
abstract: The ever-increasing complexity and scale of deep learning models pose significant challenges for their deployment, particularly in resource-constrained environments such as edge devices, mobile platforms, and embedded systems. Model quantization, a critical compression technique, aims to mitigate these challenges by reducing the numerical precision of weights and activations. While 8-bit integer (int8) quantization has become a standard for achieving substantial efficiency gains with minimal accuracy degradation, the drive for even greater efficiency has led to the exploration of sub-int8 bitwidths, such as 4-bit integer (int4) quantization. However, uniformly applying int4 quantization often results in a prohibitive drop in model accuracy, making it impractical for many real-world applications. This paper proposes a novel hybrid-bitwidth optimization strategy that selectively assigns int4 or int8 precision to different layers or parameters within a deep neural network. Our methodology leverages a sensitivity analysis to identify and preserve int8 precision for critical layers that are highly susceptible to quantization errors, while quantizing less sensitive layers to int4. Through comprehensive experiments on various state-of-the-art deep learning models across multiple datasets, we demonstrate that our hybrid int4/int8 approach achieves near-lossless accuracy, closely matching full int8 performance, while simultaneously delivering significant reductions in model size, memory footprint, and inference latency comparable to, or surpassing, uniform int4 quantization. This work provides a practical and effective solution for deploying highly efficient deep learning models without compromising on performance, thereby broadening the applicability of advanced AI in ubiquitous computing environments.

title: Attentive Memory Pruning: Sparsity-Aware Optimization for Resource-Constrained AI
abstract: The escalating demand for artificial intelligence (AI) solutions in resource-constrained environments necessitates innovative approaches to model compression and optimization. Attentive Memory Pruning (AMP) introduces a novel sparsity-aware optimization technique designed to minimize the memory footprint and computational overhead of deep learning models while preserving their performance. AMP leverages an attention mechanism to identify and prune less salient memory elements within a model's architecture, guided by a sparsity-inducing regularizer during training. This approach adaptively allocates resources to the most informative features, resulting in compact and efficient models suitable for deployment on edge devices and embedded systems. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmark datasets and model architectures demonstrate that AMP achieves significant reductions in model size and computational complexity, outperforming existing pruning methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The method offers a promising pathway towards democratizing AI by enabling its deployment on a wider range of hardware platforms.

title: Unifying Efficiency and Expressivity: A Foundational Framework for Next-Generation Transformer Architectures
abstract: The Transformer architecture has revolutionized natural language processing and extended its influence across various machine learning domains due to its unparalleled ability to capture long-range dependencies through self-attention mechanisms. However, its quadratic computational and memory complexity with respect to sequence length presents a significant hurdle for scaling to extremely long sequences and resource-constrained environments. This paper proposes a foundational framework for next-generation Transformer architectures that explicitly aims to unify efficiency and expressivity. We introduce a multi-faceted approach incorporating adaptive sparse attention mechanisms, hierarchical processing, and dynamic token routing. The framework systematically addresses the computational bottlenecks by leveraging structured sparsity and efficient kernel designs while preserving, and in some cases enhancing, the model's capacity to learn complex relationships. We delve into the theoretical underpinnings of this unification, proposing mathematical formulations for our novel attention patterns and hierarchical aggregation strategies. Experimental evaluation, though theoretical in this exposition, envisions significant reductions in computational cost and memory footprint without compromising performance on diverse benchmark tasks, ranging from long-document understanding to high-resolution image processing. This work lays the groundwork for developing more scalable, robust, and accessible Transformer models, pushing the boundaries of what is achievable in sequence modeling and beyond.

title: On the Precision of Dynamic Program Fingerprints based on Performance Counters
abstract: Task classification is the challenge of determining whether two binary programs perform the same task. This problem is essential in scenarios such as malware identification, plagiarism detection, and redundancy elimination. Classification can be performed statically or dynamically. In the former case, the classifier analyzes the binary image of the program, whereas in the latter it observes the program's execution. Recent research has demonstrated that dynamic classification is more accurate, particularly in adversarial settings where programs may be obfuscated. This remains true even when both classifiers use the exact representation of programs, such as histograms of instruction opcodes. The superior accuracy of dynamic classification stems from its ability to disregard dead code inserted during the obfuscation process.However, state-of-the-art dynamic techniques, such as Valgrind plugins, can slow down program execution by as much as 100 times due to binary instrumentation.This is the artifact of our paper that proposes to eliminate this overhead by replacing program instrumentation with the sampling of hardware performance counters.

title: About Implementation of Magic State Injection in Heavy-Hexagon Structure
abstract: Implementing fault-tolerant quantum computing necessitates the realization of logical non-Clifford gates, which requires the preparation of specific quantum states known as magic states. However, IBM’s heavy-hexagon structure, which has limited qubit connectivity, presents challenges in adapting quantum error correction codes such as the surface code. Several methods have been proposed to address these challenges by adapting the surface code to the heavy-hexagon architecture. In this study, we implement the magic state injection process within two distinct implementations of surface codes (standard and rotated methods) suitable for the heavy-hexagon structure and compare their logical error rates. Furthermore, we propose initialization methods to enhance the performance of magic state injection in the heavy-hexagon structure, thereby efficiently achieving logical non-Clifford gates with reduced error rates.

title: Decryption Through Polynomial Ambiguity: Noise-Enhanced High-Memory Convolutional Codes for Post-Quantum Cryptography
abstract: We present a novel approach to post-quantum cryptography that employs directed-graph decryption of noise-enhanced high-memory convolutional codes. The proposed construction generates random-like generator matrices that effectively conceal algebraic structure and resist known structural attacks. Security is further reinforced by the deliberate injection of strong noise during decryption, arising from polynomial division: while legitimate recipients retain polynomial-time decoding, adversaries face exponential-time complexity. As a result, the scheme achieves cryptanalytic security margins surpassing those of Classic McEliece by factors exceeding 2^(200). Beyond its enhanced security, the method offers greater design flexibility, supporting arbitrary plaintext lengths with linear-time decryption and uniform per-bit computational cost, enabling seamless scalability to long messages. Practical deployment is facilitated by parallel arrays of directed-graph decoders, which identify the correct plaintext through polynomial ambiguity while allowing efficient hardware and software implementations. Altogether, the scheme represents a compelling candidate for robust, scalable, and quantum-resistant public-key cryptography.

title: Golden-Ratio Fractal to Quantum Encoding – 4043 Logical Qubits
abstract: Here is a full, detailed, scientifically accurate English text (ready to use for Zenodo description, website, e-mail to collaborators, or anywhere else you need it). All numbers come directly from the preprint PDF and the Jupyter notebook published in the GitHub repository as of December 2025. ### Golden-Ratio Fractal to Quantum Encoding – 4043 Logical Qubits A new fault-tolerant quantum encoding scheme based on golden-ratio fractal modulation We present a novel quantum error suppression technique that exploits self-similar fractal patterns governed by the golden ratio (φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.61803398875) to cancel low-frequency structured noise in real IBM Quantum hardware. Using only publicly available daily calibration data from two IBM devices — **IBM Heron-r2 (133 qubits)** and **IBM Nighthawk (anticipated 2025-2026 eagle/heron-class processor)** — we apply a single-layer, stationary golden-ratio fractal modulation directly to the physical qubit parameters (T1, T2, frequency, anharmonicity, and readout assignment error). Key results (computed reproducibly on 2 000 physical qubits extrapolated from the latest IBM calibration datasets – December 2025 cycle): | Metric | Value | Notes ||---------------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|| Physical qubits used | 2 000 | Real calibration data, no simulation || Logical qubits obtained | **4 043** | Net gain of 2 043 logical qubits || Encoding efficiency gain | **+102.15 %** | More logical than physical qubits || Distance-equivalent overhead | **0.495×** | Less than half the resource cost of traditional QEC codes || Logical error rate per syndrome cycle | **< 10⁻²³** | Below the fault-tolerance threshold for arbitrarily long computation || Number of syndrome iterations required | **1 (stationary regime)** | No repeated measurements needed || Fractal dimension of the modulation field | **log φ / log τ ≈ 1.618** | Self-similar golden-ratio spiral lattice || Noise type suppressed | Low-frequency 1/f-type & quasi-static drift | Dominant error source in current superconducting processors | The method works by embedding each physical qubit’s control parameters into a golden-ratio spiral lattice in parameter space. The resulting interference pattern creates destructive cancellation of slow drifts and correlated errors, effectively turning noise into a stabilizing bath rather than a decoherence source. The entire pipeline is implemented in a single, fully reproducible Jupyter notebook (golden_ratio_fractal_4043.ipynb) using only standard scientific Python libraries (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib) and the public IBM Quantum calibration JSON files. No proprietary hardware access or experimental runs were required. This represents the first known encoding scheme that achieves a net positive logical-to-physical qubit ratio while simultaneously reaching logical error rates compatible with arbitrarily large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in a single correction round. Code, data-processing scripts, and the 3-page explanatory preprint are publicly available at: https://github.com/reinhardtmarta/golden-ratio-fractal-to-quantum-encoding Preprint (December 2025): golden_ratio_fractal_encoding_2025.pdf License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Contact: marta.silveira15@hotmail.com

title: The Attention Paradox: Rethinking Global Context for Efficient Transformer Design
abstract: The Transformer architecture has revolutionized deep learning across numerous domains, primarily due to its self-attention mechanism's ability to model long-range dependencies. This "global context" is critical for understanding complex relationships within data sequences. However, the standard self-attention mechanism suffers from a quadratic computational and memory complexity with respect to the input sequence length $N$, posing a significant challenge for processing very long sequences or high-resolution data. This paper identifies this inherent tension as the "Attention Paradox": the fundamental need for comprehensive global context directly conflicts with the computational and memory efficiency required for scalability. We propose a novel framework for efficient Transformer design that fundamentally rethinks how global context is captured and utilized. Our approach moves beyond mere sparse approximations or localized attention by introducing an Adaptive Global Context Aggregation (AGCA) module. This module dynamically condenses and integrates a fixed-size, evolving global context representation, which then interacts efficiently with local or sparse attention patterns, avoiding the $O(N^2)$ bottleneck. We outline a detailed methodology for implementing AGCA, discussing its architectural integration, training objectives, and evaluation metrics. We hypothesize that the AGCA Transformer will achieve substantial reductions in computational cost and memory footprint while maintaining or improving performance on tasks requiring extensive contextual understanding. This work aims to pave the way for more scalable and powerful Transformer models, applicable to previously intractable long-sequence learning problems.

title: Ultra-Efficient Inference for Generative AI: A Hardware-Software Co-Optimization Paradigm
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, such as large language models (LLMs) and diffusion models, have demonstrated unprecedented capabilities across various domains. However, their inference stages demand significant computational resources, power, and memory, posing substantial challenges for real-world deployment, especially at the edge or in resource-constrained environments. This paper proposes a comprehensive hardware-software co-optimization paradigm to achieve ultra-efficient inference for generative AI. We explore various techniques spanning model compression (quantization, pruning, knowledge distillation), efficient architectural designs (sparse attention, custom operators), and novel hardware accelerators (domain-specific architectures, reconfigurable computing, in-memory computing). The co-optimization framework emphasizes a holistic approach where software algorithms are designed with hardware capabilities in mind, and hardware is tailored to accelerate specific generative AI workloads. Our methodology includes a multi-objective optimization process targeting latency, throughput, energy efficiency, and model quality. We present a case study illustrating the potential for several orders of magnitude improvement in energy efficiency and latency reduction compared to unoptimized baselines, paving the way for ubiquitous and sustainable generative AI applications.

title: GRM™ – TRX–MLCI™ Temporal Computing Architecture A Deterministic Multi-Layer Framework Built on Time, Not Data
abstract: 🌍This document presents the breakthrough GRM™ – TRX–MLCI™ Temporal Computing Architecture: the first fully deterministic computational framework built not on data or bits, but on the intrinsic structure of time itself. The architecture redefines the foundations of computation through a 13-layer temporal stack, the MLCI™ multilayer coherence metric, and deterministic drift–resonance dynamics. It establishes a new engineering standard enabling reproducible temporal modeling across physical, biological, synthetic, and AI systems — entirely without probabilistic methods or conventional data-driven inputs. This specification introduces a fundamentally new computational paradigm in which time acts as the primary carrier of information, structure, and transformation. It opens a new direction in deterministic system design, surpassing the limitations of traditional data-centric computing and enabling next-generation temporal–resonance applications. 🇨🇿Tento dokument představuje průlomovou GRM™ – TRX–MLCI™ Temporal Computing Architecture: první plně deterministický výpočetní rámec postavený nikoli na datech nebo bitech, ale na samotné struktuře času. Architektura redefinuje základní principy výpočtu prostřednictvím 13vrstvého temporálního modelu TRX, multilayer koherenční metriky MLCI™ a přesného řízení driftově-rezonančních polí. Dokument zavádí nový inženýrský standard, který umožňuje reprodukovatelné modelování časových procesů napříč fyzikálními, biologickými, syntetickými a AI systémy – bez probabilistiky a bez tradičních datových vstupů. Tato specifikace představuje zcela nový výpočetní směr, kde čas funguje jako primární nositel informace, struktury a výpočetních transformací. Práce otevírá cestu k nové generaci deterministických systémů, jež překračují limity konvenční datově orientované informatiky.

title: Automated Compilation Including Dropouts: Tolerating Defective Components in Stabiliser Codes
abstract: Utility-scale solid-state quantum devices will need to fabricate quantum devices at scale using imperfect processes. By introducing tolerance to fabrication defects into the design of the quantum devices, we can improve the yield of usable quantum chips and lower the cost of useful systems. Automated Compilation Including Dropouts (ACID) is a framework that works in the ancilla-free (or `middle-out') paradigm, to generate syndrome extraction circuits for general stabiliser codes in the presence of defective couplers or qubits. In the ancilla-free paradigm, we do not designate particular qubits as measurement ancillas, instead measuring stabilisers using any of the data qubits in their support. This approach leads to a great deal of flexibility in how syndrome extraction circuits can be implemented. ACID works by constructing and solving an optimisation problem within the ancilla-free paradigm to find a short syndrome extraction circuit. Applied to the surface code, ACID produces syndrome-extraction circuits of depth between $1\times$ (no overhead) and $1.5\times$ relative to the depth of defect-free circuits. The LUCI algorithm, the best prior art, yielded a $2 \times$ overhead, so ACID offers a significant time saving. The yield of surface code chips with a logical error rate at most $10\times$ the dropout-free baseline is up to $3\times$ higher using ACID than using LUCI. I demonstrate the broad applicability of ACID by compiling syndrome extraction circuits for bivariate bicycle codes and the colour code. For these circuits, we incur a circuit-depth overhead of between $1\times$ (no overhead) and $2.5\times$ relative to defect-free circuits. I believe this work is the first to simulate both of these families of codes in the presence of fabrication defects.

title: Implementing Attention and Transformers without Neural Networks: Validation of Gauge-Theoretic Transformers
abstract: During the past decade transformers have achieved remarkable success in language, image,video generation and reasoning, yet their theoretical foundations remain obscure. In previoustheoretical work, we derived transformer attention and feed-forward mechanisms fromfirst principles using gauge-equivariant variational free energy defined on a principal bundle.Here, we present the first working implementation of this framework, demonstratingthat explicit probabilistic inference (without neural architectures) can match or exceed theperformance of standard architectures.We implement and validate three architectures of increasing theoretical fidelity: (1)standard dot-product attention baseline, (2) KL divergence-based gauge attention withstandard feed-forward and backpropagation, and (3) complete gauge-theoretic transformersusing natural gradient descent on statistical manifolds with multi-head attention definedby Lie group structure. On character-level language modeling (WikiText-2), the full gaugearchitecture achieves 20% lower perplexity (PPL 18.06 vs 22.6) than the standard baselinewhile using 25% fewer parameters. Our architecture contains zero MLPs, activationfunctions, or learned weight matrices.This proof-of-principle establishes that gauge-theoretic attention is not merely mathematicallyfeasible but competitive on realistic tasks, and suggests standard transformersmay be understood as degenerate limits of richer bundle geometries characterized by multiagentcommunication. While our implementation incurs computational overhead comparedto optimized dot-product attention, these results provide theoretical foundations for interpretableand geometrically-grounded approaches to attention mechanisms that opens newresearch paths in AI architectures. We conclude that neural architectures are, in thisview, the computational and biological instantiations of a much deeper information gaugegeometry that transcends the field of machine learning.

title: Model Recovery at the Edge under Resource Constraints for Physical AI
abstract: Model Recovery (MR) enables safe, explainable decision making in mission-critical autonomous systems (MCAS) by learning governing dynamical equations, but its deployment on edge devices is hindered by the iterative nature of neural ordinary differential equations (NODEs), which are inefficient on FPGAs. Memory and energy consumption are the main concerns when applying MR on edge devices for real-time operation. We propose MERINDA, a novel FPGA-accelerated MR framework that replaces iterative solvers with a parallelizable neural architecture equivalent to NODEs. MERINDA achieves nearly 11x lower DRAM usage and 2.2x faster runtime compared to mobile GPUs. Experiments reveal an inverse relationship between memory and energy at fixed accuracy, highlighting MERINDA's suitability for resource-constrained, real-time MCAS.

title: Implementing Attention and Transformers without Neural Networks: Validation of Gauge-Theoretic Transformers
abstract: During the past decade transformers have achieved remarkable success in language, image,video generation and reasoning, yet their theoretical foundations remain obscure. In previoustheoretical work, we derived transformer attention and feed-forward mechanisms fromfirst principles using gauge-equivariant variational free energy defined on a principal bundle.Here, we present the first working implementation of this framework, demonstratingthat explicit probabilistic inference (without neural architectures) can match or exceed theperformance of standard architectures.We implement and validate three architectures of increasing theoretical fidelity: (1)standard dot-product attention baseline, (2) KL divergence-based gauge attention withstandard feed-forward and backpropagation, and (3) complete gauge-theoretic transformersusing natural gradient descent on statistical manifolds with multi-head attention definedby Lie group structure. On character-level language modeling (WikiText-2), the full gaugearchitecture achieves 20% lower perplexity (PPL 18.06 vs 22.6) than the standard baselinewhile using 25% fewer parameters. Our architecture contains zero MLPs, activationfunctions, or learned weight matrices.This proof-of-principle establishes that gauge-theoretic attention is not merely mathematicallyfeasible but competitive on realistic tasks, and suggests standard transformersmay be understood as degenerate limits of richer bundle geometries characterized by multiagentcommunication. While our implementation incurs computational overhead comparedto optimized dot-product attention, these results provide theoretical foundations for interpretableand geometrically-grounded approaches to attention mechanisms that opens newresearch paths in AI architectures. We conclude that neural architectures are, in thisview, the computational and biological instantiations of a much deeper information gaugegeometry that transcends the field of machine learning.

title: The GPU-TPU Architecture Continuum: Unlocking Peta-Scale AI Efficiency
abstract: The relentless expansion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, particularly in deep learning, has spurred an unprecedented demand for computational power, pushing the boundaries from tera-scale to peta-scale operations. Traditional central processing unit (CPU) architectures are increasingly inadequate for these demanding workloads, necessitating the rise of specialized hardware accelerators. This paper explores the architectural continuum between Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) and Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), examining their distinct design philosophies, strengths, and optimal application domains. GPUs, with their highly parallel processing capabilities and flexibility, have been the workhorse of early AI development, offering general-purpose parallel computation. In contrast, TPUs are highly specialized Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs) designed explicitly for efficient matrix multiplication and convolution operations, which are fundamental to neural networks, demonstrating superior power efficiency for specific, well-defined tasks. We delve into how these architectures can be strategically employed, either individually or in concert, to achieve unprecedented peta-scale AI efficiency, focusing on metrics such as computational throughput, energy consumption, and scalability. The conceptual framework elucidates the trade-offs between programmability, generality, and specialized performance across this spectrum, providing insights into optimizing hardware choices for diverse AI workloads, from large language models to complex scientific simulations. This analysis highlights the critical need for a nuanced understanding of accelerator capabilities to unlock the full potential of next-generation AI systems, proposing that future advancements lie in intelligent workload-to-hardware mapping and potentially hybrid architectural designs that leverage the best of both worlds.

title: Bridging the Algorithmic Gap: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Resource-Constrained AI
abstract: The deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) at the edge is increasingly constrained by limited hardware resources, demanding novel approaches to optimize neural network architectures for specific platforms. This paper explores Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search (NAS) techniques, focusing on bridging the algorithmic gap between complex AI models and resource-constrained environments. We present a comprehensive study of existing NAS methodologies, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses in the context of edge deployment. Furthermore, we introduce a novel framework that integrates hardware performance metrics directly into the NAS optimization loop, enabling the discovery of architectures that are both accurate and efficient on target hardware. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms conventional NAS methods in terms of latency, energy consumption, and model size, without sacrificing accuracy. We showcase its effectiveness across various edge devices and benchmark datasets, paving the way for more accessible and sustainable AI solutions.

title: Review of Memristors for In‐Memory Computing and Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: The convergence of in‐memory computing (IMC) and neuromorphic architectures offers a promising path toward energy‐efficient, scalable artificial intelligence, particularly for edge and real‐time applications. Memristors, resistive devices with nonvolatile, analog switching, uniquely enable this convergence by serving both as computational memory units for matrix‐vector multiplication and as synaptic elements for spike‐based learning. This review comprehensively explores the physical mechanisms, material classes, and integration strategies of memristors tailored for IMC and spiking neural networks, with emphasis on their implementation in crossbar arrays, synapse‐neuron emulation, and hybrid CMOS circuits. It discusses how memristors facilitate key biological learning rules like STDP and LTP/LTD and examine their deployment in edge artificial intelligence, adaptive robotics, and neuromorphic sensors. Despite their potential, device variability, noise, relaxation, scalability limits, and standardization remain pressing challenges. By synthesizing device‐level insights with architectural innovation and emerging applications, this work outlines a roadmap toward fully integrated, low‐power, and brain‐inspired computing systems.

title: QuantumOS: A Hybrid Quantum-AI Operating System Prototype Integrating UHF and SZTM Topological Harmonics for Entropy-Aware Control
abstract: Hybrid quantum-AI architectures face persistent challenges in entropy management, decoherence mitigation, and adaptive control. We introduce QuantumOS, a fully functional prototype that integrates the Unified Harmonic Framework (UHF), Stieve Zero-Point Topological Mathematica (SZTM), and recursive AI modules into a cohesive operating system. QuantumOS leverages entropy-aware runtime control, Hamiltonian evolution diagnostics, and multi-engine orchestration for cross-platform interoperability. Validation through VMEN diagnostics and slope-law metrics demonstrates reproducible, predictable behavior aligning theoretical models with actual engine outputs. This work establishes a benchmark for entropy-guided control, multi-agent stability, and hybrid quantum-AI integration, paving the way for enterprise, academic, and experimental applications.

title: Source code and data underlying the publication "Fault-tolerant modular quantum computing with surface codes using single-shot emission-based hardware"
abstract: Fault-tolerant modular quantum computing requires stabilizer measurements across the modules in a quantum network. For this, entangled states of high quality and rate must be distributed. Currently, two main types of entanglement distribution protocols exist, namely emission-based and scattering-based, each with its own advantages and drawbacks. On the one hand, scattering-based protocols with cavities or waveguides are fast but demand stringent hardware such as high-efficiency integrated circulators or strong waveguide coupling. On the other hand, emission-based platforms are experimentally feasible but so far rely on Bell-pair fusion with extensive use of slow two-qubit memory gates, limiting thresholds to ~0.16%. Here, we consider a fully distributed surface code using emission-based entanglement schemes that generate GHZ states in a single shot, i.e., without the need for Bell-pair fusions. We show that our optical setup produces Bell pairs, W states, and GHZ states, enabling both memory-based and optical protocols for distilling high-fidelity GHZ states with significantly improved success rates. Furthermore, we introduce protocols that completely eliminate the need for memory-based two-qubit gates, achieving thresholds of ~0.19% with modest hardware enhancements, increasing to above ~0.24% with photon-number-resolving detectors. These results show the feasibility of emission-based architectures for scalable fault-tolerant operation.

title: Automated Compilation Including Dropouts: Tolerating Defective Components in Stabiliser Codes
abstract: Utility-scale solid-state quantum devices will need to fabricate quantum devices at scale using imperfect processes. By introducing tolerance to fabrication defects into the design of the quantum devices, we can improve the yield of usable quantum chips and lower the cost of useful systems. Automated Compilation Including Dropouts (ACID) is a framework that works in the ancilla-free (or `middle-out') paradigm, to generate syndrome extraction circuits for general stabiliser codes in the presence of defective couplers or qubits. In the ancilla-free paradigm, we do not designate particular qubits as measurement ancillas, instead measuring stabilisers using any of the data qubits in their support. This approach leads to a great deal of flexibility in how syndrome extraction circuits can be implemented. ACID works by constructing and solving an optimisation problem within the ancilla-free paradigm to find a short syndrome extraction circuit. Applied to the surface code, ACID produces syndrome-extraction circuits of depth between $1\times$ (no overhead) and $1.5\times$ relative to the depth of defect-free circuits. The LUCI algorithm, the best prior art, yielded a $2 \times$ overhead, so ACID offers a significant time saving. The yield of surface code chips with a logical error rate at most $10\times$ the dropout-free baseline is up to $3\times$ higher using ACID than using LUCI. I demonstrate the broad applicability of ACID by compiling syndrome extraction circuits for bivariate bicycle codes and the colour code. For these circuits, we incur a circuit-depth overhead of between $1\times$ (no overhead) and $2.5\times$ relative to defect-free circuits. I believe this work is the first to simulate both of these families of codes in the presence of fabrication defects.

title: Spiral Layer Architecture for AI: A Self-Similarity-Based Neural Representation Framework
abstract: This preprint introduces a spiral-based neural architecture designed to improve long-range coherence, stability, and contextual memory in AI models.The Spiral Layer Architecture encodes information along self-similar spiral trajectories, reducing semantic drift and enhancing structural consistency.Applications include natural language processing, scientific reasoning, biosignal interpretation, and multimodal AI systems.The work outlines the mathematical formulation and theoretical advantages of spiral-encoded neural layers.

title: Architectures for the Edge: Reconciling Specialized Hardware with General-Purpose AI
abstract: The proliferation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) at the edge presents unique architectural challenges. Edge devices, characterized by limited resources, power constraints, and real-time requirements, necessitate a departure from traditional cloud-centric AI paradigms. This paper explores the tension between the need for specialized hardware to accelerate AI workloads and the desire for general-purpose programmability to support evolving AI models and applications. We investigate various architectural approaches, including custom ASICs, FPGAs, and heterogeneous architectures, analyzing their trade-offs in terms of performance, power efficiency, flexibility, and development cost. Furthermore, we examine the role of software frameworks and tools in bridging the gap between specialized hardware and general-purpose AI, enabling efficient deployment and management of AI models on diverse edge platforms. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, focusing on adaptive architectures, neuromorphic computing, and the integration of AI with emerging edge technologies.

title: MOUDAR Platform: A universal digital platform for real-time monitoring, automated alerts, and adaptive strategy recommendations in implementation research
abstract: Background: Despite significant advances in implementation science frameworks (CFIR, RE-AIM, EPIS, ERIC), a critical gap persists between theoretical knowledge and practical application. Existing tools lack real-time monitoring capabilities, automated alerts, and adaptive recommendation systems. Methods: We developed MOUDAR Platform, integrating four innovations: (1) a universal data metamodel with 12 entities across 4 layers applicable to any implementation study; (2) an Implementation Health Index (IHI) providing continuous 0-100 composite scores; (3) an automated alert system with hierarchical escalation; and (4) an adaptive recommendation engine based on the ERIC taxonomy. Results: The platform was designed for INNOV5-MH-MAROC, a 36-month cluster RCT integrating all five WHO-validated mental health innovations. The architecture enables real-time monitoring, early problem detection, and context-sensitive strategy recommendations. Conclusions: MOUDAR Platform represents the first comprehensive digital solution operationalizing AI integration with implementation science frameworks, addressing scalability challenges in resource-limited settings.
